# Changelog

All notable changes to AIPass will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/).
Entries are grouped by merge under a dated section header (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Package
releases follow [SemVer](https://semver.org/) and are tracked by the git tag and
PyPI version — not the changelog header.

---

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- **hooks**: OpenCode 2 is the third CLI the engine gates. `apps/handlers/bridges/opencode_plugin.ts` (installed as `~/.config/opencode/plugins/aipass.ts`) runs the manifest's `cli.opencode` rows through `bridges/opencode.py`: prompt → SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit, tool execute.before → PreToolUse (a deny is thrown and shown to the model), execute.after → PostToolUse, compaction → PreCompact, the execution events → Stop. The bridge maps tool names and file-tool keys to Claude's, refuses OpenCode's `execute` code tool, and fails closed. The settings gate covers `~/.config/opencode` and the OpenCode auth file; `drone @hooks verify` names a missing or stale plugin copy (`docs/wiring.md`).
- **aipass**: the OpenCode switch legs: `/opencode [fresh] [provider/model]` on Claude Code, `$opencode` on Codex, `/claude` and `/codex` on OpenCode, plus `/memo`, `/prep` and `/compass` as OpenCode commands over the shared skills (`.opencode/commands/`). The pane respawns into `opencode --standalone --auto --prompt` with the handoff; the model rides as inline config.
- **ai_mail**: `dispatch … --provider opencode [--model provider/model]` wakes a citizen on OpenCode 2 (`opencode run --standalone --format json --auto`). OpenCode mints every fresh session id (the free tier refuses any other shape) and the pointer follows the stream's `sessionID` at the end of every attempt; a resume passes the pointer's id after a read-only check of its `session_v2` row. The monitor parses the JSON stream (last text part, summed tokens and cost, the first error event stops retries, a 429 bounces with its retryAfter), strips `OPENCODE*` from the child env, and sets `PWD` to the branch since OpenCode files a session under `PWD`. `pid_lock` counts `opencode` as an agent, never its serve daemon or standalone child (`docs/wake_pipeline.md`).
- **daemon**: `wake.provider: opencode` is a valid schedule provider.
- **devpulse**: the watchdog scanner follows an OpenCode pointer by reading the pointed session's `session_v2` row in `opencode.db`, read-only, once per tick: `time_updated` moving is growth, in flight until `time_idle` follows it (`docs/watchdog.md`).
- **aipass**: `/codex fresh` and `$claude fresh` switch the pane to the other CLI with no handoff: no memory pass, no `handoff.md`, an empty chat in the same directory for the startup protocol to open as usual. A chat with nothing in it yet counts as fresh without the word. Both switch files come from `scaffold_content.py` 1.5.0, so every project gets the lane on its next `aipass init update` (`docs/two_clis.md`).
- **spawn**: `drone @spawn update` reports a branch `.gitignore` against the citizen template (`matches`, `differs`, `absent` or `unreadable`, the `.md` lane's states) in the branch report and as `gitignore-drifted` in the fleet summary, and never writes an existing one, preview or `--apply` (`handlers/update_ops.py` 2.6.0, `modules/update.py` 1.3.0, `tests/test_update.py` 1.3.0, `docs/update_engine.md`; 5 pins red first, 5 mutants red).
- **aipass**: `aipass doctor` reads OpenCode: Wiring rows `opencode binary`, `opencode login` (`opencode auth list`, "none (free models only)" when signed out) and `opencode model` (the `model` in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`), plus `opencode plugin` (the installed `~/.config/opencode/plugins/aipass.ts` byte-equal to the hooks source: SET, MISSING or DIFFERENT). `doctor --fix` installs the plugin through the settings-backup door (backup, receipt). Absent OpenCode is one PASS row and nothing runs; doctor never runs `opencode run`.
- **aipass**: the scaffold ships the seven OpenCode switch and ritual files (`.claude/commands/opencode.md`, `.codex/skills/opencode/SKILL.md`, `.opencode/commands/{claude,codex,memo,prep,compass}.md`) as managed files; `aipass init update` writes them into existing projects. `aipass handoff launch --cli opencode` starts OpenCode standalone with `--auto` and `~/.opencode/bin` on PATH. A test pins the nine scaffold switch texts byte-equal to the repo-root files, so an edit to either side fails CI instead of shipping stale to every init.
- **hooks**: `drone @hooks parity --provider claude,codex,opencode` runs the lanes on OpenCode (`opencode run --standalone --format json --auto -m opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`, the session id read from the stream; a free-limit answer reruns the lane once on nemotron, then reads no data). `opencode` is opt-in: the default stays `claude,codex` since it spends free quota. The runner sets `PWD` to the branch, since OpenCode seats itself at `$PWD` before its real cwd.
- **hooks**: the context gauge reads an OpenCode session from `opencode.db` (read-only; `$OPENCODE_DB` or the XDG data home): the newest assistant message's input, output, reasoning and cache tokens, the same count as OpenCode's status line. The window is read as 200k for every model and the call it names is `/prep`.
- **ai_mail**: `dispatch … --provider opencode --opencode-config '<json>'` hands a JSON object to OpenCode as `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`, merged under `--model` (which wins on `model`); set in the child's env after the `OPENCODE*` strip, so a parent seat's own value never reaches the child; refused when not a JSON object or given with another provider. The wake header's sub-agent rule is said without any CLI's parameter name: run sub-agents in the foreground and wait for them.
- **hooks**: on OpenCode the four grounding loaders (kernel, navmap, branch prompt, identity) answer as keyed instruction entries (`aipass-kernel`, `aipass-navmap`, `aipass-branch-prompt`, `aipass-identity`) that the plugin puts with `ctx.session.instructions.entry.put`; they sit in the instruction block of every model call and survive a compaction, since OpenCode compacts inside the agent step and calls the model again with no user prompt. An entry that cannot be kept travels with the prompt, so the text arrives once either way. The context gauge reads the model's real limit from the models.dev catalog in OpenCode's store and the compact point as limit minus `compaction.buffer` (config content, project `opencode.json`, then the user's), else limit minus `max(15%, 16k)`: 170k on a 200k model. Measured live: eight auto-compactions in one canary run, 32 PreCompact rows, the grounding present after the last one.
- **ai_mail**: the session pointer carries a run record (`host_cli`, `model_provider`, `model_requested`, `model_observed`, `selection_source`, `observed_at`). The requested model and its source come from the dispatch's own flags (`flag`, `inline_config`, else `cli_default`); the observed model comes only from the runtime's own newest assistant row (OpenCode's store, Claude's transcript, Codex's rollout) and reads `pending` until seen, never promoted from the request. The dispatch result, the wake-back, the manager mail and both bounces end with one run line: `run: opencode · openai/gpt-6.1-sol (observed; flag) session ses_…`. No config contents, no credentials. A Claude continue-dispatch over another host's pointer takes the fresh lane (a minted id, a `wake-fresh` pointer) instead of `-c` over a session Claude cannot resume; and the run stamp refuses to pair one host with another host's session id, leaving the record pending with a WARNING rather than a mixed label.
- **devpulse**: every `DISPATCH` wire line ends with the finished branch's grounding reading from its receipt (`grounding=verified gen1`, `ungrounded missing=…`, `unverified (none)`, `stale`, `no receipt`) and its run from the session pointer (`run=opencode·gpt-6.1-sol`, a `?` on a requested model not yet observed). A bad or absent file reads as no receipt, never an error.
- **aipass**: `aipass doctor --smoke [--model provider=model,..]`, an opt-in live model turn per installed provider through `drone @hooks smoke --json`: pass and skip are ✓ rows with the reason, fail a ✗ row with hooks' why and the cure; `--smoke --json` passes hooks' objects through and exits 1 on any fail; refused with `--fix`; never a row nor a call without the flag, since doctor's first run burns no credits. `pyproject.toml` depends on `tomli>=2` on Python 3.10, so the Codex rows read `config.toml` there instead of degrading quietly.
- **hooks**: `drone @hooks smoke [--provider claude,codex,opencode] [--branch] [--model] [--json]`, one isolated live turn per installed bridge: the prompt carries a nonce, the temporal row answers it with `smoke-ack:<nonce>` (the ack string is not in the prompt), and the verdict is read from the provider's own record of the hook for that session (Claude's transcript attachment row, Codex's developer response item, OpenCode's user message in the store), never from the model's reply. `pass`, `fail` or `skip` with a fixed-sentence reason (not installed, plugin not installed, not logged in, rate or usage limit, free limit, no readback); the branch's pointer and receipt are restored byte for byte and `AIPASS_HOOK_PROBE=1` keeps the turn from starting @memory's archive. The callable `smoke(provider, branch, model) -> SmokeResult` is what `aipass doctor --smoke` wraps. Each run costs one model turn per provider.
- **hooks**: a grounding receipt beside the session pointer, `.ai_mail.local/grounding.json`: one current row (`session_id`, `branch`, `generation`, `required_set_revision`, `expected_digest`, `observed_digest`, `observation_boundary`, `status`, `missing`, `stale`, `checked_at`) plus a history of 20. On OpenCode the store shows what the last model call carried (`instruction_state.current_values`, measured across a forced compaction), so the receipt reads `verified` or `ungrounded` and names the missing keys and their sources in the prompt answer; on Claude Code and Codex it reads `unverified` with boundary `none`. PreCompact sets `pending` for the next generation. `drone @hooks receipt` prints it.
- **hooks**: culture is the fifth keyed entry on OpenCode (`aipass-culture`, from the SessionStart row), so the culture text survives a compaction like the other four; the bridge keys its grounding map by event and hook. The PreCompact rollover trusts a clean `drone @memory rollover check` for 30 minutes per project and branch (a stamp in the temp dir) and skips the 7 to 15 s subprocess within that window; a ready verdict, a failed check or a timeout is never trusted. The gauge caches each model's catalog limit in the temp dir, valid while the catalog row's update time holds and for at most a day: the per-prompt read drops from about 180 ms to under 20 ms.

### Fixed

- **ai_mail**: the ponytail audit of the run record (@ai_mail, on devpulse's dispatch, the owner's "fix them all"; `dispatch_monitor.py`, `session_pointer.py`, `modules/dispatch.py`, `email/header.py`, `docs/dispatch_register_and_feed.md`; suite 1496 to 1499). The run-record stamp after a dispatch is wrapped so an odd row in OpenCode's store (NULL `data`, a list) can no longer take the bounce, the wake-back, the report and the register close with it; a failed fresh Codex run no longer stamps the previous thread's model as observed (requested-only line, session pending); transcripts are read line by line instead of whole (a 110 MB transcript peaked at 595 MB); the Claude transcript folder name follows Claude's real rule (every non-alphanumeric character, proven with a live run under a path with a space, `+`, `@` and parentheses); the two dispatch verbs share one flag parser and one admin check; the OpenCode stream is parsed once per attempt; the header's dead `__main__` block is gone; the doc lists only the `selection_source` values the code writes.
- **aipass**: the ponytail audit of doctor's provider wiring (@aipass, on devpulse's dispatch, the owner's "fix them all"; `provider_wire.py` 1.11.0, `_doctor_wire.py` 1.7.0, `doctor.py`, `bootstrap.py` 2.6.1, `opencode_cli.py`, `shared/scaffold_content.py`, `docs/doctor.md`; suite 1448 to 1454, 16 mutants red). The Codex hooks rows and plan and the OpenCode plugin rows and plan are gated on the CLI being installed, the rule setup.sh already used, so a machine without them no longer gets `~/.codex/hooks.json` and `~/.config/opencode/plugins/aipass.ts` written by the install preflight nor warnings doctor cannot clear; `doctor --fix --json --yes` answers `error` instead of a crash when a settings write is refused; `--fix` no longer writes provider switch files without recording them (the cure names `aipass init update`, which records their hash, so the next template change reaches them); the six switch texts come from one `_handoff_shape`, byte-identical; a default doctor runs the provider probes once (the interactive re-run only when a Services row is non-pass) and parses settings once; the Codex and OpenCode probe helpers are one pair in `opencode_cli`. `pyproject.toml` (devpulse) loses the wheel's `aipass/_hooks` force-include of the disabled hook scripts nothing reads and the empty `seedgo` extra. `aipass init update` ran in `projects/baud`, `earmark`, `finch` and `aipass-site`: each gained the seven OpenCode and Codex switch files BAUD's switch dropdown types.
- **api**: the two OpenRouter GETs use `urllib.request` from the standard library, and `requests` leaves the package's core dependencies (@api, on devpulse's dispatch, the aipass audit's finding 8; `openrouter/models.py` 1.1.0, `usage/tracking.py` 1.3.0, their tests; suite 2008 to 2010, 10 mutants red, live against OpenRouter). Callers see the same errors with the same sentences: an HTTP status, a timeout in both urllib forms, any other network error with its reason. Every install pulled `requests` for these two calls, including installs without the `llm` extra that uses OpenRouter.
- **memory**: `drone @memory pool process` takes the same lock as the background auto-process child, so two runs never race the same pool files. While another run holds it, the verb names the holder's pid, processes nothing and exits 2 (`auto_process.py` 1.2.0 `run_locked`, `pool.py` 1.1.0; two pins in `tests/test_auto_process.py`).

## [2026-10-27] — v2.8.29: the new-project system after Vera-Studio's day (AGENTS.md managed, the gitignore template and merge, updateignore, doctor's shadow and coverage rows), the watchdog per seat, a manager writes in its citizens, Codex wake lanes and parity

### Added

- **aipass**: `aipass init`, `new` and `adopt` seed `.aipass/.gitignore` (a whitelist, so the scaffold manifest and `.aipass/.backup/` are never committed) and a root `.updateignore` holding only its header, the owner's file for what update must never touch.
- **aipass**: `aipass init update` merges a project's `.gitignore` line by line: template lines the file lacks are appended under one dated comment, no owner line is removed or reordered, and `--dry-run` prints the lines. It seeds a missing `.aipass/.gitignore` and `.updateignore` without rewriting existing ones (Vera-Studio's dry run: four lines to add).
- **aipass**: a new project's `.claude/settings.local.json` carries `autoCompactWindow: 350000`, the manager-seat default that needed a hand edit through the settings gate; existing files are never given it.
- **aipass**: `aipass doctor` Structure row `gitignore coverage`, read-only: runtime files on disk that git tracks (`.chroma`, `docs.local`, `dropbox`, `*_json`, `.spawn`, the registry json) get one FAIL per folder with `drone @git untrack` as the fix; this is the check that would have caught Vera-Studio's 144 tracked files.
- **aipass**: `aipass doctor` Structure row `instruction shadow` FAILs a live `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md` or `CLAUDE.local.md` beside an `AGENTS.md` (Claude Code reads AGENTS.md only when no CLAUDE file sits in cwd or above, so the project's AGENTS.md was never read: Vera-Studio and four other scaffolded projects, all passing doctor), says whether the two texts match, and `--fix` renames it to `(disabled)`: never a copy, delete or overwrite, never under `$HOME`, never through a `.claude` symlinked outside the root (`structure_scanner.py` 1.2.0, `doctor.py` 1.10.0, `docs/doctor.md`; ten tests, 1411 green).
- **hooks**: a project's manager writes inside its own citizens' branches (`modules/write_ownership.py` 2.5.0, `docs/edit_gate.md`; the owner's ruling 2026-10-26, the same shape as #808 for git). @vera was refused `Cross-branch write blocked: vera cannot write to writer` on both lanes because the manager exception covered only files outside every branch row. A non-AIPass project's manager row now writes its whole project; a citizen into a sibling citizen's row is still refused, crossings between projects are still refused, and inside AIPass the verified admin seat stays the only exception. One new test, two pins reversed, 3/3 mutants red, 2781 green.
- **hooks**: `navmap_cap` (`prompt/navmap.handle_edit`, PostToolUse) says at edit time when `.aipass/tier1_navmap.md` is over its 8,000-char cap, with the count, instead of the injection cutting it silently near 10,000.
- **hooks**: the project template (`.aipass/project_hooks.json`) carries `culture`, `session_pointer`, `settings_gate`, `settings_backup` and `navmap_cap`, so an external seat gets the culture file, a resume pointer for BAUD, the provider-settings gate and the navmap warning. `compass_recall`, `auto_process`, `comment_budget` and `presence_gate` stay host-only, reasons in `src/aipass/hooks/docs/project_config.md`. Existing projects take the entries through `aipass init update`.
- **drone**: `drone @git push`: a project's manager pushes its own repo's checked-out branch to origin, never forced, no arguments. In AIPass it refuses and names `dev-pr`; `push --repo` stays the admin door.
- **drone**: `drone @git issue create|comment --repo AIOSAI/AIPass` from any seat in any project, the body signed with the seat and project (`--body` only; `--body-file`, `--editor` and `--web` refuse there). Issues are the contribution channel; close, edit and delete stay owner-tier.
- **drone**: git writes are fenced by the session, not the cwd: owner and ci-cure verbs refuse when the running Claude Code session started outside the project (its transcript sits under the launch directory, which a `cd` cannot move), unless the seat is admin. Gate and door logs carry the session id and where it started beside the seat.

- **hooks**: `drone @hooks parity [--branch @canary|<path>] [--lane A,..,F] [--provider claude,codex] [--json]` runs the same scripted prompts headless on Claude Code and on Codex from one branch's cwd and compares what the hooks did, row by row: the twelve UserPromptSubmit handlers, SessionStart, the four gates (cross-branch write, raw git, raw rm, new test file), PostToolUse, Stop and SubagentStop, the over-cap `.trinity` edit. The oracle is `logs/engine.jsonl`: every per-hook line now carries the payload's session id, so a session's whole hook record is read back by the id each CLI prints. Accepted differences (culture native on Claude, the sub-agent mechanism) are marked, never counted; exit 1 on a real difference or a session that left no record, so the merge train can gate on it. First live run on canary: 32 rows, all same or accepted. `docs/provider_parity.md`.
- **daemon**: a job's `wake` block names the provider next to the model: `"wake": {"fresh": true, "model": "gpt-6-sol", "provider": "codex"}`. Absent is claude, wake.py's own default, never a second copy; a value that is not `claude` or `codex` is refused at discovery by owner, job id and value. The scheduler pins both, the owner's ruling (`discovery.py` 2.6.0, `run.py` 1.9.0, `rotation.py` 1.4.0, `job_reference.py` 1.1.0, `docs/schedule_contract.md`; six pins in existing test files, six mutants red; proven live by a one-off canary job that woke on Codex, register row 371e953d).
- **aipass**: the handoff's end choice is Claude Code or Codex, and the provider does not matter: choosing codex launches `codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` (the posture the rooms, the `/codex` skill and dispatch use, hooks being the gates) and the way back is `codex resume --last`; Claude's launch and breadcrumb are unchanged. `aipass doctor` gains four read-only Codex rows after `codex hooks`: the binary and its version, `codex login status`, the configured model checked against `codex debug models` for this login, and the four config pins (memories off, plan mode off three ways), each missing pin's fix being the exact TOML line to add by hand; `--fix` never touches `config.toml`, and a pin proves its bytes unchanged (`handoff_platform` 1.1.0, `_doctor_wire.py` 1.4.0, `provider_wire.py` 1.7.0, `doctor.py` 1.8.0, `docs/two_clis.md`; 1382 green, eight mutants red).
- **aipass, hooks**: Codex hooks move to the user level, so a Codex seat in any project runs under the same 24 hooks as inside AIPass. @hooks measured Codex 0.164: `$CODEX_HOME/hooks.json` (else `~/.codex/hooks.json`) fires from every cwd; the repo-level `.codex/hooks.json` loads beside it with no dedupe, so both files together fire every hook twice; trust is keyed `<file>:<event>:<group>:<index>` on content with no cwd, so one trust covers every project; untrusted rows skip silently. The writer now targets the user-level file and merges rather than replaces: AIPass rows (the ones running the Codex bridge) are replaced wherever they sit and placed first in each event, every foreign row and top-level key is kept behind them, backup and receipt as before. The tracked repo `.codex/hooks.json` leaves the tree. Doctor gains `codex trust` (a `trusted_hash` under each AIPass key in config.toml, else WARN naming the one key to press) and `codex double-fire` (FAIL while a repo-level file still holds bridge rows; `--fix` leaves the project's file). The bridge is unchanged (`provider_wire.py` 1.8.0, `_doctor_wire.py` 1.5.0, `tests/test_provider_wire.py` 1.9.0 with `CODEX_HOME` pinned to tmp for every test, `docs/two_clis.md`, `docs/doctor.md`; 1387 green, eight mutants red).
- **devpulse**: the watchdog sees a Codex session. A branch whose session pointer names provider `codex` is watched through its one rollout under `~/.codex/sessions`, re-read from the pointer on each refresh so a `/codex` switch is followed; a Codex turn is in flight until the rollout's last line is an `event_msg` of type `task_complete` or `turn_aborted` (Codex writes no session-end record), an unparseable tail counts as in flight. The wire and the sign-in take this seat's session id from `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, else from a Codex pointer's thread id (`agent.py` 1.6.0, `dispatches.py` 2.1.0 `seat_session_id`, `wire.py` 2.5.0, `watchdog.py` 2.2.0, `docs/watchdog.md`; seven pins in the existing test files, one mutant red). ai_mail's `door_session_pointer` 1.1.0 exports `codex_thread_file`, `CLAUDE`, `CODEX` for it.
- **seedgo**: `host_portability` arm G flags a stdlib import newer than pyproject's `requires-python` floor (`tomllib` on a 3.10 floor; `zoneinfo`, `graphlib` on older ones) unless the same `try`/`if` falls back to the backport (`import tomli as tomllib`); a `sys.version_info` gate alone is not an acquittal, it moves the degraded answer to the floor's lane without running it. The floor is read from the nearest `pyproject.toml`, none means the arm is off. It is the species behind PR #811's 3.10-only red: fourteen aipass Codex tests whose degraded except branch no newer seat ever ran. Three pins red-first on the provider_wire reduction, five mutants red, fleet 0 live rows after seedgo's own cure (`host_portability_check.py` 1.5.0, `host_portability_content.py` 1.4.0, `host_portability.md`, `docs/aipass_standards.md`; FPLAN-0707).
- **seedgo**: `host_coupled_oracle`, a tests-only standard (branch level): a test that passes its own `os.getpid()`/`getppid()` to an args/cmdline/title reader, or pins a literal runner `call_count == N` on a function that both forks on platform and runs a subprocess, is host-coupled and fails. Born of PR #807's three clone-only reds (pytest-xdist retitles its workers; macOS reads args through `ps`). Two pins on reductions of the real tests, seven mutants red, fleet 0 hits after hooks' cures.

### Changed

- **aipass**: a project's `AGENTS.md` is managed by manifest hash like the tier files (current / update / kept-local with the `.aipass-new` sidecar when the owner edited it), with an `.updateignore` row as the opt-out; it was a seed written once and never revisited, so tonight's template fix reached no existing project. A manifest from the seed era carries no trusted hash, so the first update never overwrites an edit an older update adopted (`scaffold_manifest.py` 1.1.0, `bootstrap.py` 2.5.0).
- **aipass**: a new project gets a project navmap stub (its name, its citizens from the registry, the drone basics) in place of the host's roster map, which described AIPass's citizens in every external project. An unedited stub follows the roster on update; a host map or the project's own map is kept and the stub offered as `.aipass-new`.
- **spawn**: `drone @spawn update` reads the project-root `.updateignore` as well as the branch's, matching root patterns against the project-relative path on the gitignore model (`src/vera_studio/*/docs.local/` protects every citizen, a slashless name matches at any depth), so one file at a project's root protects all its citizens; the branch-local file stays as an optional extra and either one protects. A wildcard directory pattern now also withholds the bare directory row; an unreadable root file refuses before any write (`update_ops.py` 2.5.0, `update_ignore.py` 1.2.0, `docs/update_engine.md`; five new tests in the existing file, 3/3 mutants red, 1127 green).
- **prompts**: `.aipass/tier1_navmap.md` trimmed under its 8,000-char cap (it was 9,422, cut silently at injection); the "Finding your way" section went, the kernel already says it; the settings line names the Codex files beside Claude's.
- **README**: the install line says Codex as a choice (a second CLI, each agent runs on either, per task), no longer "optional", matching aipass.ai.
- **ai_mail**: managers wake on Codex in the same lanes as on Claude: headless in the scheduled and admin lanes, and through a tmux session running `codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` on a @daemon self-wake. The Claude-only refusal of `--provider codex` for a `citizen_class: manager` is gone; the owner's ruling, after Vera's first Codex release post needed a hand-opened pane (`wake.py` 3.8.0, `dispatch.py` 3.7.0, `docs/wake_pipeline.md`, `tests/test_wake.py` 1.5.0: one refusal pin becomes four cases, two mutants red).

### Fixed

- **seedgo**: the provider hooks snapshot fixture (`tests/fixtures/provider_hooks_snapshot.json`) carries the Claude `SessionStart:culture` row the provider manifest gained, so the six `test_hooks_snapshot` reds are green.
- **hooks**: `README.md` back under seedgo's 10,000-char README cap (was 10,099, the ratchet fleet walk red): seven Documentation-table descriptions shortened, wording only.
- **devpulse**: the watchdog wire's identity primitives are public names (`stdout_target`, `cmdline`, `looks_like_ours`, `session_dir_of` in `wire.py` 2.7.1): the tests that prove them against a real process reached them as private names, seedgo's `through_the_command` row on the pre-push audit; no behaviour change, `test_watchdog_wire.py` 2.4.1 follows.
- **aipass**: the Codex config reads (`doctor`'s model and pin rows, `set_codex_pins` behind `setup.sh` and `doctor --fix`) fall back to the `tomli` package where `tomllib` is absent, the structure scanner's own shape, so Python 3.10 reads and pins `config.toml` like 3.11+; before, 3.10 answered "needs Python 3.11+" on every row and skipped the pins, and the fourteen Codex tests were red on CI's 3.10 lane (PR #811 run 40477098528). Without either parser the rows still say so, naming tomli now (`provider_wire.py` 1.9.1).
- **seedgo**: the test inventory reads `pyproject.toml` on Python 3.10 through `tomli` instead of falling back to pytest's defaults on a `sys.version_info` gate; without either parser the note names both (`test_inventory/collection.py` 1.0.3, arm G's one fleet hit).
- **ci**: the standards gate's expected count moves 83 → 84 for `host_coupled_oracle`, which landed without moving `EXPECTED_STANDARDS` in `.github/scripts/seedgo_audit.py`; the tripwire fired on the first branch of the local pre-push run and would have been the standards job's red.
- **aipass**: the project `.gitignore` template covers the runtime state spawn and the services write (`.chroma/`, `docs.local/`, `dropbox/`, `artifacts/`, `tools/` with a negation example, `**/*_json/`, `.spawn/`, `.backup/`, the registry and roots json, `.env`, local plans, WAL sidecars, `.claude/worktrees/`); Vera-Studio had 144 of one installation's files tracked on the old template (`scaffold_content.py` 1.4.0).
- **aipass**: `aipass init update` retires a live `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md` or `CLAUDE.local.md` beside `AGENTS.md` to `(disabled)` with doctor's shadow fix and its refusals, and retires the pre-2.8.20 `.claude/hooks/*.py` scripts the manifest recorded while they are unedited.
- **aipass**: `aipass init <target> --dry-run` took the flag as the project name and scaffolded a `--DRY-RUN_REGISTRY.json`; flags are refused before anything is written.
- **devpulse**: arming the watchdog wire takes over only this seat's older wires; a wire registered by another seat (a project manager's, `metadata.seat`) is left alive and named on stderr, where before every live wire in the registry was SIGTERMed and the other manager's completions went unreported. Entries without a seat (pre-2.6.0) are taken over as before (`wire.py` 2.6.0).
- **devpulse**: the watchdog's seat is the sealed owner of the caller's project, read through `AIPASS_CALLER_CWD`, where before drone's cwd switch made every seat `@devpulse`: @vera's wire delivered devpulse's completions, took devpulse's wire over as a same-seat arm, and `watchdog status` from her seat counted devpulse's dispatches as hers (#810). Each seat now drains the feed through its own cursor files (`devpulse_json/<seat>.feed_cursor.json`, same for the dead cursor), so one manager's drain never marks another's completions as seen; `status` lists the caller's seat's dispatches only and names the seat on each wire row (`dispatches.py`, `feed.py`, `presenter.py`, `wire.py` 2.7.0).
- **memory**: `drone @memory config get|set @branch` resolves citizens of declared roots (@vera), so BAUD's settings panel saves for a project citizen; `process-plans` vectorizes every visible project's `.backup/processed_plans` (host, resident projects, declared roots), tags each chunk with its project, and `search` shows the project under the hit.
- **flow**: a closed plan archives into its own project's `.backup/processed_plans`, never the host's (an external's plan history had landed under `$AIPASS_HOME/.backup`); restore looks there too.
- **flow**: `drone @flow list` shows the caller's project's plans; `list all` from the host seat still lists every project. Plan numbers stay global.
- **aipass**: the project `AGENTS.md` template (`.aipass/project_AGENTS.md`) and its generator follow the host startup protocol: memories read one file per call, no README read at startup, dashboard refresh and read, and the todo pad rules. It had drifted; a project scaffolded from it inherited the old startup. `AGENTS.md` is a seed file, so `init update` never rewrites an existing copy; only `init`, `new` and `adopt` write the new text.
- **hooks**: Claude Code seats in external projects get the AIPass culture file at SessionStart (the Claude manifest has the `SessionStart:culture` row now); inside `AIPASS_HOME` Claude reads `.claude/AGENTS.md` natively and the hook stays silent, so nothing is injected twice.
- **drone**: `drone @git commit --all` no longer dies with E902 in a project with no root `tests/`, and no longer rewrites files before refusing: the lint gate runs first over the dirs that exist, then `ruff check --fix` and `ruff format` touch only the changed files and the result names every file they rewrote.
- **aipass**: projects get the provider switch. `init`, `new` and `adopt` write `/codex` (`.claude/commands/codex.md`) and `$claude` (`.codex/skills/claude/SKILL.md`) as managed scaffold files, `init update` adds them to older projects and keeps edited copies, and doctor's `provider switch` row names a missing one, which `--fix` writes. Before this the pair lived only in the AIPass tree, so no external project could switch CLI.
- **commands, skills**: the switch files (`/codex` in `.claude/commands/codex.md`, `$claude` in `.codex/skills/claude/SKILL.md`) point their prep step at `.agents/skills/prep/SKILL.md`, where prep lives since the shared skills folder; they named `.claude/commands/prep.md` and `.codex/skills/prep/SKILL.md`, neither of which exists.
- **aipass, setup.sh**: a fresh install with `codex` on PATH installs the Codex hooks again. `setup.sh` had looked for the repo's `.codex/hooks.json`, retired, and skipped the Codex step, leaving a new Codex seat ungated; the block it would have run also rewrote `~/.codex/config.toml` wholesale with deprecated keys and a default model. Now `setup.sh` runs `provider_wire.refresh_codex()`, the same plan `aipass doctor --fix` applies: `cli.codex` merged into the user-level `$CODEX_HOME/hooks.json` with the owner's own rows kept, then the four Codex pins (`memories`, `collaboration_modes`, `include_collaboration_mode_instructions`, `tools.experimental_request_user_input.enabled`, all false) set one line each in `config.toml`, every other line kept, after a backup and with a receipt. A config.toml the line edit cannot set safely (a dotted key, an inline table) is refused and left untouched. `refresh_provider_hooks()` is Claude-only now. The install summary and the README name the user-level file and the one-time trust step.
- **hooks**: `drone @hooks verify` reads Codex's hook rows from the user-level `$CODEX_HOME/hooks.json` (`~/.codex/hooks.json`), the only place they live since the repo `.codex/hooks.json` retired; it had kept reading the repo path and reported the Codex-only culture handler as unwired. A missing user-level file is now an ERROR naming the cure (`aipass doctor --fix`, then trust the hooks once in `codex`), not a skipped check, since a Codex seat without it runs ungated. One home rule in `context_window.py` (`codex_home()`) serves both `codex_config_path()` and the new `codex_hooks_path()`. The settings gate keeps protecting the retired repo path so the file never returns unnoticed beside the user-level one.
- **aipass**: `aipass doctor` run from an external project's root no longer reports `AIPASS_HOME split` against that project. The terminal's tree is the registry root when that root is an AIPass tree (it holds `src/aipass`); in an external project it is the tree the project's `.claude/settings.local.json` (then `settings.json`) names in `env.AIPASS_HOME`. Two AIPass trees still fail the row (`doctor.py` 1.7.1, `tests/test_doctor_home.py` 1.2.0, three pins, two mutants red). Found by Vera-Studio's update to 2.8.28, the first run of the release ritual.
- **memory**: rollover's trim re-reads the memory file before writing and removes only the archived entries, so an edit made while vectors were being stored (a new todo, a meta bump) is no longer overwritten by the image read at extraction. Found at 12:16 on devpulse's own pad: one Edit added a todo and pushed sessions to 11, the rollover it fired had read the file three seconds earlier, and its trimmed write put that older image back (`extractor.py` 0.9.0, `orchestrator.py` 1.4.1, `tests/test_orchestrator_exec.py` 1.1.0 pins the real sequence, two mutants red; `docs/rollover_pipeline.md`).
- **hooks**: on Codex, an `apply_patch` that names no file is denied with that reason and logged at WARNING; it is a malformed call, not a broken engine, so it no longer raises `HOOKS BROKEN`. PostToolUse on such a patch runs nothing (`bridges/codex.py` 2.5.0, `tests/test_codex_bridge.py` 2.5.0, four mutants red).

## [2026-10-25] — v2.8.28: Codex as a second provider (dispatch, hooks, context gauge, one skills dir for both CLIs), the owner's settings gate, the ratchet's budget exit, the api suite at 75 s

### Added

- **hooks**: `settings_gate`, the provider-settings gate (fail-closed, PreToolUse, before `settings_backup`): no AI changes `~/.codex/*.toml`, `hooks.json`, `auth.json`, `rules/**` (and the same under `$CODEX_HOME`), `~/.claude/settings*.json`, the repo's `.claude/provider_manifest.json` or `.codex/hooks.json`, or runs `aipass doctor --fix`/`setup.sh`/`provider_wire.py`, without the owner. Interactive Claude Code asks (its own settings stay with Claude Code's native prompt); a Codex caller and every headless seat are denied, the reason pointing at @devpulse. The Codex bridge turns any PreToolUse `ask` into a `deny`, since Codex runs the call on an ask. `docs/settings_gate.md`. (hooks suite 2,730 passed.)
- **ai_mail**: `dispatch --provider codex [--model <slug>]` wakes a branch on the Codex CLI (`codex exec --json`, or `codex exec resume <thread_id>` when the branch's pointer names a Codex thread) through the same monitor, lock, register row and wake-back as a Claude wake. The session pointer and the register row carry `provider`; a pointer for the other provider starts fresh. The monitor reads startup from the live stream, the thread id from `thread.started` and the result from the last `agent_message`; an `error` event or a run with no `turn.completed` bounces and is not re-run. `--model` is passed to Codex verbatim; none means Codex's own config. Codex hooks ride the repo `.codex/hooks.json` written from the manifest's `cli.codex` rows (the hand scripts it replaced rest in `.codex/hooks/.archive/`).
- **hooks**: `SessionStart:session_pointer` records every interactive session as its branch's resume target, with the CLI that runs it: the Codex bridge tags each payload `provider: codex`, a payload without the tag is Claude's, a `compact` start leaves the pointer alone, a cwd without a passport writes nothing. Interactive sessions only: a `claude -p`/`--print` ancestor or a Codex rollout whose `session_meta` source is `exec` leaves the pointer as it is, so a stray one-shot never becomes a branch's resume target. Rows in `.aipass/hooks.json` and in both manifest `cli` blocks. A missing transcript at turn 0 logs at debug, not as a failed stat; a hook chain that ends in Codex's app-server daemon logs "Codex session" once at debug instead of "no session-file ancestor" at info.
- **commands**: `/codex` (Claude Code) and `$claude` (Codex skill) move a chat to the other CLI in one turn: memories saved, the live thread written to `.ai_mail.local/handoff.md`, and the tmux pane respawned with the other CLI greeted by the handoff. The pane is found by walking the shell's ancestry, else by command and path (Codex runs its shells from a daemon, not the pane). `setup.sh` also exports `AIPASS_HOME` in `~/.profile`, which every login shell, Codex's daemon included, reads.
- **skills**: one source for the rituals both CLIs run. `.agents/skills/{prep,memo,compass}/SKILL.md` is the master (the Agent Skills standard folder Codex scans natively); `.claude/skills` is a tracked symlink to it, so Claude Code lists the same three as `/prep`, `/memo`, `/compass` and Codex as `$prep`, `$memo`, `$compass`. The duplicated `.claude/commands/{prep,compass}.md` are gone (Claude Code reads a skill folder exactly like a command file); `compass` states its arguments as the words after the command, since Codex has no `$ARGUMENTS`. The switch skills stay provider-local: `/codex` in `.claude/commands/`, `$claude` in `.codex/skills/`. `.agents/skills/README.md` says the rule.
- **hooks**: the context gauge and the compact snapshot read a Codex rollout as well as a Claude transcript (`context_window.py` 1.4.0; the shape comes from the first line, `session_meta` means Codex). On Codex the fill is the newest `token_count` event's `last_token_usage.total_tokens` (what Codex's own status line counts), the model the newest `turn_context`, the window the rollout's `model_context_window` (else 95% of `model_context_window` in `~/.codex/config.toml`, else 200k), and the auto-compact point 90% of the full window, lowered by `model_auto_compact_token_limit` when set (codex-rs `openai_models.rs`). The gauge says `$prep` when the payload carries the bridge's `provider: codex`, `/prep` otherwise. Before this, the gauge never fired on Codex and the snapshot stamped a None fill. Eight Codex cases inline in the existing tests (hooks suite 2,696 passed).
- **aipass**: `init`, `new` and `adopt` write a project's prep skill at `.agents/skills/prep/SKILL.md` and make the `.claude/skills` symlink, instead of `.claude/commands/prep.md`; where the filesystem refuses a symlink the skills are copied into `.claude/skills` and the CLI says the copy will not follow the master (`git config core.symlinks true`). `init update` and `doctor --fix` make a missing link and retire an unedited legacy `prep.md` to `prep(disabled).md`; an edited one is kept and named. `doctor` gains the Scaffold rows `shared skills` (every SKILL.md named and described), `skills link` (resolves to `.agents/skills`; warns on missing, copy or elsewhere) and `legacy prep`. New doc `src/aipass/aipass/docs/two_clis.md`: what each CLI reads, the spelling of each ritual on each, a compaction on each, the limits; `.claude/README.md` rewritten as the short map of that folder and `.codex/README.md` added. (aipass suite 1,370 passed.)

- **daemon**: a command job may declare `ok_exit_codes` in its schedule row; a run ending in one of them is recorded as a completed fire, not a FAILED one. Seedgo's `ratchet-weekly` declares `[6]`, the budget-spent exit: a week that measured a fragment is a recorded week.

### Fixed

- **hooks**: the Codex context gauge reads `config.toml`'s compact limit and window on Python 3.10 too (one top-level int by regex, no `tomllib`; `context_window.py` 1.5.0), and the process-args test waits for its child to exec and accepts the macOS framework interpreter.
- **hooks**: three tests now pass in a clean CI clone: the process-args test reads a child it spawns (pytest-xdist retitles its workers), the reclaim help test builds its own registry (a clone carries none, `AIPASS_REGISTRY.json` is gitignored), and the failed-ps test counts only ppid lookups (macOS reads args through `ps` too).
- **hooks**: the Codex bridge's ask-to-deny branch states the parsed answer exists, clearing a type-check error; Codex's config path lookup is tested directly (`codex.py` 2.4.2; hooks suite 2,759 passed).
- **hooks**: settings_gate judges a move or delete of a settings folder (`mv ~/.codex`, `rm -r ~/.codex/rules`, a folder holding one) and counts only an executed installer (`./setup.sh`, `bash setup.sh`), not one that is read; the Codex bridge still denies PreToolUse when prax cannot load; `sessions reclaim` stops sessions by branch path, not a namesake; the PreCompact stamp locks `.trinity/`; `boot`'s dead-window resume uses the picked session id; a failed tmux kill falls through to the signal; testwrite_gate reads relative paths from the payload's cwd; `verify` checks the Codex PreToolUse matcher reaches Bash and apply_patch; `test` reports a crashed injector as crashed; `speak` leaves no WAV behind; `feedback on` says when hooks.json still has it off; the alert cut marker names `.aipass/alerts.json`. The thirteen findings of @hooks' own ponytail audit, run on Codex, fixed on Claude. (hooks suite 2,755 passed.)
- **api**: the test suite runs in 75 s instead of 212 s (361 s under load) with the same 2,008 tests: a session fixture makes `os.fsync` a no-op (the autouse fleet-cache clear logged an fsynced JSON write four times per test), and the read-only host-API test modules share one session-scoped FastAPI app while the modules that mutate app state (pairing rate window, face, added routes) keep their own. Seedgo's mutation probe can now afford the suite.
- **ai_mail**: Codex's `app-server`/`mcp-server` daemon and a headless `codex exec` no longer count as an interactive session, so they no longer block a dispatch (`pid_lock.py` 1.2.0 `branch_occupant`; the daemon trio is spawned by the first Codex TUI opened in a folder, parented by `systemd --user`, and outlives every ended room, so a dispatch to that branch was refused as occupied with no room open). The occupancy row names the CLI it found (`wake.py` 3.7.0).
- **ai_mail**: a dispatch to a branch whose dispatch lock is held (a session woken for other work, or a monitor draining) now says "NOT woken" in the output and the log and exits non-zero with the re-wake command, instead of reporting that the running session will read the mail; that session has its own prompt and may finish without reading it.
- **seedgo**: a ratchet campaign that runs out of budget exits 6 (`EXIT_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`), not 2, and still writes its series line; a branch whose last series line is a budget fragment is the next pick, before never-probed branches, and the run probes only the functions the fragment left (`slice k/N`, N forecast from this slice's rate) until the tree is measured. `ratchet-weekly` declares `ok_exit_codes: [6]`.
- **flow**: the post-close runner's stale-lock takeover is serialized under an OS lock on `<lock>.takeover` and re-reads staleness inside it; two runners that read the same dead pid could both take over, the slower one deleting the faster one's live lock. 46 dead registry rows (the `/tmp` and external-path quarantine plus the test-made FPLAN-9990) dropped and saved to flow's `.archive/`, their 22 backup copies archived; `register`/`unregister` with a missing argument pinned at exit 2 with the usage line. (@flow's 2026-10-25 rounds, the owner's cleanup ruling.)

### Changed

- **prompts**: the tier 0 kernel states the standing rule that `.archive/` is ignored everywhere in the tree: never read, moved, swept, fed or processed by any agent or sweep.

- **trigger**: `log_events status` and `branch_log_events status` printed "Active: False" while the watcher service was running (they read an in-process flag); they now print the systemd unit's state ("Service: running|stopped|unknown|unavailable") and the flag as "This process:"; the ci-poll schedule note said DISABLED for a job that is enabled; the unit template marks the reload sentinel's exit 75 as `SuccessExitStatus` with `RestartForceExitStatus=75`, so the journal stops logging each reload as a failure (an installed unit keeps the old text until re-rendered). ## [2026-10-23] — v2.8.26: a gated CI cure retries until its gate opens, a failed interval job shows the next run it will fire

### Fixed

- **a gated CI cure retries on every poll until its gate opens or the run is superseded** (@trigger, on devpulse's dispatch; `handlers/events/ci_red.py` 1.1.0, `modules/ci.py` 1.1.0, `handlers/ci/ledger.py` 1.1.0, `tests/test_ci.py` 1.1.0, `tests/test_ci_red.py` 1.1.0, `docs/ci_red_lane.md`; suite 50 green). The lane's first real red (PR #800, drone's `stale_header_date`) was triaged right in ten minutes, then the wake was refused by drone's 24-hour build mute and the cure sat `gated` for good: a gated cure was terminal. Now `_drain` re-fires every `queued` or `gated` cure with its stored payload on each poll, only a fresh red feeds the breaker and escalation counters (`_gate_reason(..., fresh=True)`), and `supersede()` closes queued and gated cures alike when a newer run lands. A mute delays a cure instead of dropping it.
- **a failed interval job's next_run moves to attempt + interval, so the queue no longer shows a slot days past** (@daemon, rounds; `handlers/schedule/runstate.py` 1.7.0, `modules/run.py` 1.7.1, `tests/test_run_blocked_contract.py` 1.1.0, `tests/test_runstate_failure_retry.py` 1.1.0; suite 782 green, audit 100). `seedgo/ratchet-weekly` exited 2 on 10-18 and kept its seeded `next_run`, so `drone @daemon queue` read "next 2026-10-18" five days later while the scheduler, which measures an interval from the attempt, was right. `record_job_failure` takes `schedule=` and moves an interval job's next_run; windowed jobs retry in-window, unchanged. Two red-first pins: dropping the handler line and dropping the run.py wiring each kill a test.

## [2026-10-23] — v2.8.25: the CI red lane in @trigger with the drone ci-cure tier, secret values in the login keyring behind drone @api, Telegram out of the tree, Drive as the truth for the backup sync, the .trinity cap band, plan templates drop the spoken summary

### Fixed

- **hooks' cadence turn token answers -1 when the transcript cannot be measured, so a failed stat no longer reads as an empty transcript** (@hooks, on devpulse's dispatch; `modules/cadence.py` 2.11.0, `tests/test_cadence.py` 1.9.0 two pins, `.seedgo/bypass.json` lines re-pointed, `pytest.ini`; suite 2547, audit 100). The CI audit step on dev went red: d8310ffa added two lines above the nine `logged_fallback` lines the leg-5 bypass pins by number, so all nine stopped matching and the audit printed the first, `cadence.py:133`. That one is cured at the source: no path or a failed stat answers -1, which no size can be, and `_should_increment`'s guard reads `token > 0`, so two unmeasurable turns in a row still count where 0 would have frozen the counter. The other eight lines are re-pointed under the unchanged reason. The branch-local `pytest.ini` now ignores the parked telegram tests, as the root pyproject already did.
- **devpulse audit: twelve findings fixed in one pass** (@devpulse; `apps/devpulse.py` 1.0.4, `handlers/release_notify/compose.py` 1.0.1, `handlers/feedback/storage.py` 1.1.0, `handlers/feedback/compose.py` 1.4.0, `handlers/feedback/inbox.py` 1.0.1, `modules/feedback.py` 1.2.0, `handlers/compass/store.py` 1.0.1, `handlers/owner/guard.py` 1.4.0, `handlers/watchdog/registry.py` 1.2.0, `handlers/watchdog/dispatches.py` 2.0.1, `handlers/watchdog/presenter.py` 1.0.1, `handlers/watchdog/schedule.py` 1.0.1, `handlers/watchdog/feed.py` 1.1.1, `modules/watchdog.py` 2.1.1, new `handlers/file_lock.py`; @ai_mail by devpulse: `__init__.py` gains the `post_to_inbox_file` door, `tests/test_public_surface.py` 1.1.0; devpulse suite 545 to 549). `release-notify` matched the CHANGELOG section by substring, so v2.8.2 mailed the v2.8.24 notes; the version is matched whole now. `feedback send "subject" "two word body"` read the subject as the sender and lost the reply path; the sender is the drone rail only. The feedback inbox was written unlocked and in place; the watch registry's lock moved to a shared `FileLock`, every load-modify-save holds it, and saves go through a tmp file and `os.replace`. Replies to feedback wrote the sender's ai_mail inbox by hand with no lock and no feed event; they go through ai_mail's door now. A command module that failed to import was logged at INFO and its command read "Unknown command"; it is named on stderr. Compass created and dropped an FTS5 probe table on every connect, so every recall-hook read wrote the DB; one read probe now. The owner guard walked the process cwd when the caller rail was unset, which names the routed branch; it uses the admin lane's env-only resolver. Scheduled commands had no timeout (600s now, reported in the exec-failure shape) and the help said "via shell" where there is none. `watchdog status` listed watches twice and read the dispatch register twice; once each, `overdue()` deleted. The feed cursor said "replaying" where a fresh cursor seeds. The dead cross-branch warning in the entry point and its `_handle_command` indirection are gone. Eleven scanner scripts that duplicate seedgo's checkers moved to `tools/.archive/` (4,455 lines). Follow-up (`handlers/owner/guard.py` 1.5.0, `tests/test_owner_guard.py` 1.2.0, `tests/test_compass_store.py`, `.seedgo/bypass.json`): `owner_address` answers "" when the lookup itself raised and None when no owner is sealed, so a caller can tell a crashed lookup from an unsealed project; both stay falsy, so every refusal message still prints instead of a traceback. `route_command`'s "handled" True after a module raised is the CLI handler contract (error() marks the exit 2), recorded in `.seedgo/bypass.json` beside compass's identical entry. The compass read-only pin compares file bytes, not mtime, so a coarse clock cannot hide a write.
- **spawn's retire-project tests read a refusal through collapsed whitespace, so a Rich line wrap under xdist no longer turns a correct refusal red** (@spawn; `tests/test_lifecycle.py` 1.2.1, test only). The `[ancestor]` oracle grepped two words that Rich wrapped once the xdist worker directory lengthened the tmp path; passed serial, failed `-n 2` every run. The oracle and its two two-word siblings now read both channels with whitespace collapsed; a mutant that changes the refusal text still turns them red. 61 passed under `-n 2`.
- **trigger's log watcher fires the handler on every occurrence from its fallback path too** (@trigger; `handlers/log_watcher.py` 2.8.1, `tests/test_log_watcher.py` 1.5.1 red first; suite 1158 to 1159, audit 100). The main registry path fires `error_detected` on every occurrence and lets the handler own the count, backoff and breaker gates; the lazy-import fallback path, taken when the registry import failed at load or `registry_report` raised, returned early unless the error was new or its count was 2, so occurrence 3 and later never reached the handler, escalation undercounted and an elapsed backoff could never re-dispatch. Both paths follow one rule now.
- **`drone @api integrations call` prints a contract's result as data: no rich markup, no highlighting, no wrapping** (@api; `modules/integrations_manager.py` 1.0.2, `tests/test_integrations_manager.py`). A JSON document or a URL came back wrapped at the terminal width and with brackets read as markup, so a caller parsing stdout (Vera's search tool, through `search_bluesky`) got broken JSON unless it forced `COLUMNS`.
- **The host-api unit is a unit of the graphical session: it starts at login and stops at logout, and `host-api autostart` no longer reads or sets lingering** (@api; `handlers/host/autostart.py` 1.2.0, `modules/host_serve.py` 1.0.2, `modules/host_api.py` 1.5.1, `tests/test_host_autostart.py` 1.2.0, `tests/test_host_lifetime.py` 1.1.2, `docs/host_autostart.md`, `docs/host_api.md`, `docs/SECURITY.md`; four pins red first, 5 mutants killed, suite 2005). Measured 2026-10-22: the machine rebooted at 16:58 for a kernel update, lingering started the unit at 16:59 before any login, the server now reads its tokens from the login keyring, which is locked until the owner logs in, so it exited 2 sixty times and systemd gave up at 17:06; the login at 17:58 unlocked the keyring and the unit stayed dead. `After=` and `PartOf=graphical-session.target`, `WantedBy=graphical-session.target` in place of `default.target`; the `loginctl enable-linger` step, `linger_enabled` and the lingering report are gone, since lingering is the daemon timers' concern, not this unit's. Installing over the old unit needs `systemctl --user disable` first: `enable` adds the session symlink but leaves the old `default.target.wants` one, which would start the unit at boot again.
- **hooks R6 refuses `python -m keyring`, not every `python -m` command whose argv holds the word keyring** (@hooks, by devpulse; `git_gate.py` 5.2.1, `tests/test_git_gate.py` 5.4.1). The clause read "keyring in args and -m in args", so `python -m pip install keyring` and `pip show keyring` were refused as the keyring command, and the api branch could not install the package its keyring-backed store needs. The module after `-m` must be `keyring`; the `keyring` program, `secret-tool`, gh's files and the interpreter-text shapes are unchanged. One pin red first, suite 2675, promoted live.
- **hooks' edit fence no longer deadlocks on a pin that reaches a name another module has not defined yet** (@hooks; `diagnostics_state.py` 2.2.0, `tests/test_edit_gate.py`, `docs/diagnostics.md`). pyright reports that shape as "is not a known attribute of module" (or `for class "ModuleType"`), which was missing from the cross-file signatures, so the error set was not all cross-file and the gate refused the edit to the very module that cures it. Both signatures are cross-file now; a local typo, an attribute on a class or on `None` still shuts the fence. Known limit: the match is on text, so a typo on a real module attribute no longer blocks either. Four mutants killed.
- **`drive_sync` fails the command when Drive authentication fails or the snapshot store is missing** (@backup, by devpulse; `apps/modules/drive_sync.py` 2.6.1). Both early refusals returned a result with `error` set, logged a warning and exited 0 with nothing on stdout, so the 05:51 retry of `nightly-drive-aipass` during a DNS outage was mailed as "passed, 0.7s, no output". They now print their sentence as the last stdout line and call `mark_command_failed()`, exit 2, like the listing and headroom refusals. Pinned in `tests/test_drive_snapshot_lane.py` 1.2.1; `docs/drive_sync.md` states both.
- **drone's `aipass_github` test fixture commits as a fixed identity** (@drone, by devpulse; `tests/conftest.py` 1.3.1). PR #800's first CI run erred at setup in all 13 `TestRestore` cases on every Python: the fixture emptied git's global config but set no author, and a GitHub runner has no identity git can auto-detect, so `git commit` exited 128. A developer machine passed because git derived one from the OS user. Same four `GIT_AUTHOR_*`/`GIT_COMMITTER_*` variables the gh-door fixture already sets.
- **A module routed in-process now carries the caller stamp, so a gate inside `@spawn`, `@git`, `@seedgo` or `@cli` can prove who is calling** (@drone, by devpulse; `handlers/router_handler.py` 1.4.0, `handlers/module_registry_handler.py` 2.1.0, `handlers/git/repo_door.py` 1.9.1, `tests/test_module_registry.py` 1.1.0, `docs/caller_identity.md`, `docs/external_repo_door.md`). ### Added

- **trigger routes a red CI run on dev to its owner, gates the cure through @seedgo, and pushes it: the CI red lane** (@trigger, on devpulse's dispatch; new `modules/ci.py` 1.0.0, `handlers/ci/` ledger, triage, replies, git_door, outbound 1.0.0, `handlers/events/ci_red.py` 1.0.0, `handlers/events/registry.py` 0.5.0, `tests/conftest.py` 1.6.0, new `tests/test_ci.py` and `tests/test_ci_red.py`, `docs/ci_red_lane.md`, `.daemon/schedule.json`; suite 1159 to 1204, audit 100). `drone @trigger ci poll`, fired by the daemon every 10 minutes, reads `drone @git run list`, keeps a ledger of runs and cures in `trigger_json/ci_ledger.json`, considers only the newest run per workflow on dev and marks older reds superseded; an infrastructure failure gets a feed event and no wake. A red's failed log names its owner (a seedgo-audit `<branch>: NN%` line or a failing test path under `src/aipass/<branch>/`); `ci_red` fires on the bus and the handler walks medic's gates (enabled, mute, registry membership, gate four so @devpulse is emailed and never woken, breaker, backoff) and the two-awake cap, then dispatches the owner with the run id, the failing lines and the reply shape (FILES, CHANGELOG, NOTE). The fact must sit on exactly one registry entry; two holders refuse both. The subject must start `fix(<owner>): ` and name the run id; absolute paths, `..`, globs and any path outside the fence are refused by name; off dev is a capability refusal. Pathspecs are literal. Every call, refused or pushed, is one row in `.ai_central/git_ci_cures.jsonl`. Nothing else moves: no PR, merge, sync, tag, rerun or `--repo`.
- **api: secret values rest in the login keyring; `drone @api secrets migrate [--dry-run]` imports the store's files and shreds them; `get-secret --out` is gone** (@api; `handlers/auth/secrets.py` 2.0.0, `handlers/auth/keys.py` 2.2.0, `handlers/google/auth.py` 1.2.0, `handlers/host/tokens.py` 1.3.0, `handlers/host/pairings.py` 1.2.0, `modules/secrets.py` 1.1.0, `modules/api_key.py` 1.1.0, `docs/SECURITY.md`; `keyring>=25.0` joins `pyproject.toml` dependencies; 22 pins red first in existing test files, 5 mutants killed, suite 1982 to 2004 serial and `-n 3`, audit 100). One entry per secret through the python `keyring` package: service `aipass`, username `<provider>/<slug>`; SecretService on Linux, the Keychain on macOS, the Credential Locker on Windows; a provider's index entry keeps `list_secrets` off the disk. A backend that cannot hold a secret (keyring's fail and null backends, a `keyrings.alt` plaintext one, a locked keyring) raises `SecretsUnavailable` naming the backend, never a value or a path; a missing entry stays `None`. API keys read `<provider>/api_key`, Google reads `google/creds` and `google/client_secret` as JSON documents, host-api token, pairing and config rows are JSON entries; only the host-api write lock, the pairing receipts and Telethon's session files stay under `~/.secrets/aipass/`. Files are the import source: the owner writes a value by hand and `secrets migrate` writes the entry, reads it back, then zeroes, fsyncs and unlinks the file with one log row per entry, leaving and naming what is not a store shape; a `.env` holding other settings is kept. `--out` went because `drone` is the hooks' one exempt program, so a value written to a file was a value a seat could read. The devto and bluesky integration drivers read `devto/api_key`, `bluesky/handle` and `bluesky/app_password` through the module door and never the `.env`; the doc's table maps each `.env` line to its entry (the drivers and their tests are private files beside the repo; suite 2005 locally, four mutants killed).

Measured that morning, a `python -c` from the devpulse seat listed `~/.secrets/aipass` where `cat` is denied by the owner's settings, since that deny list is four command names. Reads: any argv word naming the store as a path (`.secrets` with a slash or tilde beside it), for any program, and interpreter program text naming the store, `SECRETS_BASE`, the api secrets modules or `get_secret`/`set_secret`/`list_secrets`/`get_api_key` calls, in the R6 lane; the program `drone` is exempt; a bare `.secrets` word is a pattern and passes. - **seedgo's `host_portability` gains arm F: a file that empties git's config must name a commit email** (@seedgo; `host_portability_check.py` 1.4.0, `host_portability_content.py` 1.3.0, `host_portability.md` v1.4, `tests/test_aipass_standards.py` 1.3.0, 4 pins red first, 8 mutants red, fleet sweep 2,140 files 0 rows, audit 100). A file holding `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` or `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` must also hold both emails or a `user.email` string; one row per file at the first emptying line. - **`drone @spawn delete <path>` resolves a branch from the registry that seals the path, case kept; new `drone @spawn retire-project <root> --yes` retires a whole project from the verified admin seat** (@spawn; `handlers/delete_ops.py` 1.3.0, new `handlers/deletion_receipts.py` and `modules/retire_project.py`, `tests/test_lifecycle.py` 1.2.0, `docs/retire.md`; 11 tests red first, 11 mutants killed, suite 1071 serial and -n 3, audit 100). ### Changed

- **The `.trinity` write gate allows up to 10 percent over each per-entry character cap; the caps and the meta lines are unchanged** (@memory, on devpulse's dispatch; `handlers/json/entry_limits.py` 1.12.0 with `tolerance_percent()` and `allowed_chars()`, `handlers/json/config_loader.py` 1.8.0, `handlers/templates/trinity_push.py` 1.7.0, `handlers/json/budget.py` 1.0.1, `memory.config.json`, `docs/trinity_standard.md`; `tests/test_entry_limits.py` 1.2.0, `test_tab_renderer.py` 1.4.0, `test_lint.py` 1.1.0, `test_trinity_push.py` 1.3.0, `test_rollover_pipeline_todo.py` 1.0.1; band pins red first, 7 of 7 mutants killed, suite 1992, audit 100). The owner's ruling 2026-10-23: agents missed a 100 or 200 cap by one to four characters on most edits because a model estimates length and cannot count it. `entry_limits.tolerance_percent` (10) is stamped by the one resolver behind the gate, lint, the push, the renderer and the todo restore; an entry is refused only past `cap * (100 + pct) // 100`, the refusal text and `over_by` still read against the plain cap, and the meta lines say nothing about the band, so the writer keeps aiming at the cap. hooks' edit gate measures through memory's door and needed no change. `budget.py` 1.0.2 keeps the plain cap in the keep-count arithmetic by the owner's ruling (local.json's worst case at default counts is 23,973 of 25,000; the band is the gate's slack, not budgeted size). @seedgo's trinity check follows the band (on @memory's dispatch; `trinity_groups.py` 1.4.0 `_tolerance_percent` reads `entry_limits.tolerance_percent` as an int 0-100, seed 10, and the Char caps group refuses only past `max_chars * (100 + pct) // 100` while naming the plain cap; `trinity_content.py` 1.3.0, `trinity.md` v1.3; `tests/test_trinity_check_entry_caps.py` 1.1.0 `TestTheToleranceBand`, 300 green across the four trinity files, checklist 42/42).

The owner's ruling 2026-10-23: the section was rarely used and cost tokens on every plan. Each template ends its guidance with one line instead: a spoken summary only when the user asks, in plain sentences with no markup; `weekly_update.md`'s step 9 no longer names Listen. No flow code read the section, so close and vectorise are unchanged; existing plans are untouched. - **hooks' shipped cadence grounds the kernel and the navmap once, at turn 0** (@hooks; `cadence.py` 2.10.0, `tests/test_cadence.py`, `tests/test_cadence_regroup.py`, `docs/prompt_injection.md`). `DEFAULTS` give `tier0` and `navmap` `"beat": false`, so a fresh clone fires them at session start, `/clear` and post-compact only, as this checkout's config already did; identity, branch, alert and mail keep their beat; a config file's `"beat": true` restores the kernel's. Eight tests that assumed the old default now say their beat explicitly. Five mutants killed.
- **`nightly-drive-aipass` may run eight hours** (@backup, by devpulse; `.daemon/schedule.json` `timeout_seconds` 3600 to 28800). The owner's number, 2026-10-22: a Drive sync takes hours and a cap that cuts it has to go. A full rebuild is about 21,000 files at 30 to 58 a minute, so an hour cut every large night short and the tracker carried the rest to the next. The daemon runs a command job inside the tick lock, so a night that runs long holds other branches' timer fires meanwhile, accepted with the number; the job's note carries the rates and the reason.
- **AIPass's Drive upload is its own nightly job** (@backup; `.daemon/schedule.json`: `nightly-drive-aipass` at 05:45 with a 3600 s timeout; AIPass's `drive_sync` setting off, so `nightly-all` skips that step). Measured by hand on 2026-10-21: the Drive lane runs long and does not hang, about 58 files a minute whatever their size, so a full catch-up of 18,714 files is five hours and a normal night costs the files the snapshot changed (108 to 6,742 over four nights). Inside `nightly-all` that upload hit the 1800 s timeout two nights running and the lane never completed for AIPass. One hour covers about 3,500 changed files; a timeout saves the tracker and the next night sends only the rest. `nightly-all` stays at 05:00 / 1800 s, measured at 8.5 to 14 min without the upload, and its note now says catch-up is opt-in.
- **The merge playbook bumps the version and dates the CHANGELOG before the push** (`flow/templates/playbook_plans/merge.md`). CI runs once on the final state; a bump committed after green was a second full run for nothing (the owner, 2026-10-21). Pre-flight now starts the local audit gate in the background first, since it takes over twenty minutes and grows with the fleet; section 7 verifies the versions and never bumps.

### Fixed

- **Drive is the truth for what is remote: the sync lists Drive at run start and heals its tracker** (@backup; `handlers/drive/remote.py` 1.0.0, `modules/drive_sync.py` 2.6.0, `handlers/drive/upload.py` 1.5.0, `handlers/drive/client.py` 2.1.0, `modules/status.py` 1.4.0, `modules/display.py` 3.1.0, `handlers/state/backup_timestamps.py` 1.1.1, `docs/drive_sync.md`, `docs/cli.md`; 528 green serial and with `-n 3`, 5 mutants red, audit 100). The only hand that deletes on Drive is the owner's, and the lane never knew: the tracker said a file was there, so a file deleted on Drive was skipped forever, an edited one failed its update, and a cleared tracker uploaded the whole store a second time beside the first. One paged listing at run start (the `drive.file` scope sees only what this app created, about 17 calls for 23,000 files) now drops every tracked id Drive no longer has, so those files upload again; a create first looks the name up in that folder and updates the file already there (`adopt`); a listing with no answer fails the run with `Drive listing unavailable: <reason>. Nothing uploaded.` and exit 2. Every run that uploaded a file records itself, stopped or aborted included, so `status --json` and BAUD no longer say never after 14,745 files went up; `lanes.drive_sync.complete` says whether the last run finished. The `Backups now:` panel reads the project's own lanes instead of the branch clock, which had printed AIPass's times on a brand-new project. The late tracker reset on a new root folder is gone, superseded.
- **Drive upload ends after 20 consecutive failures with one line naming the last error and exit 2** (@backup; `handlers/drive/upload.py` 1.4.0 with `BREAKER_FAILURES`, `modules/drive_sync.py` 2.5.0, `docs/drive_sync.md`, `tests/test_stop.py`, `tests/test_drive_pipeline.py`; 522 green serial and with `-n 3`, 3 mutants red). The 2026-10-21 catch-up hit a DNS outage at 14,745 of 16,764 files; with no network every file fails in milliseconds, so the run walked the queue at 2,666 log lines a minute until it was stopped by hand. Failures are counted in the worker threads, since the three workers start the next file before the main thread sees the last one fail; the 20th in a row with no success between trips the breaker, no worker starts another file, the trail row carries `aborted`, the tracker keeps what went and the rest go on the next run. A failed run, not a stop: no changelog entry, `mark_command_failed()`, exit 2.
- **Every error-registry writer holds the registry lock** (@trigger; `handlers/error_registry.py` 2.5.1, `tests/test_error_registry.py` 1.3.0 with `TestRegistryWritersHoldTheLock`; suite 1154 to 1158, audit 100). `update_status`, `update_source_fix_status`, `clear_resolved` and `purge_stale` read, changed and saved the registry without `json_file_lock`; only `report()` held it, so a status change racing a report could drop one side's write. Each writer now runs under the lock; the test holds it, starts the writer in a thread, asserts it waits, writes a concurrent entry and checks both survive.
- **The daemon's MISSED line names a failed attempt instead of "no run"** (@daemon; `handlers/schedule/runstate.py` 1.6.1 with `failed_today_at`, `modules/run.py` 1.6.3, `tests/test_run_module.py` 1.2.4, `docs/scheduler_tick.md`, `docs/schedule_contract.md`; 789 green, audit 100). @backup's nightly fired twice on 10-18 and 10-19. Not a double fire: a windowed job is measured from its last success and the failure backoff lets it retry ten minutes after a failed run while the window is open, by design; both first runs failed on a host network outage in the 05:00 hour. The MISSED line then read "closed with no run" after two real runs. It now says "closed with no successful run (last attempt failed at HH:MM)" when the job failed today, and the docs say that a command job's non-zero exit or timeout counts as failed and retries inside its window.
- **backup's stop test raced its own fake upload** (@backup; `tests/test_stop.py`; 21 green; 0 of 60 red under `sys.setswitchinterval(1e-6)` where 7 of 15 were red before, a stop-ignoring mutant red, product untouched). The fake upload counted `len(sent) == 60` unlocked across the three upload threads: when two appends landed before either thread read the length, no thread saw 60, SIGTERM never fired, all 120 uploads went and the run exited 0 instead of 130 (PR #799 run 2, Python 3.12 lane). The count and the SIGTERM now sit under one lock, the fake client carries a real `threading.local` instead of a `MagicMock` that grew children unlocked across threads, the exit code is asserted after the 60..62 seam so a missed patch fails by name, and the worker is asserted dead after the join.
- **seedgo's dead-cwd guard convicted a parallel worker's `.ruff_cache`** (@seedgo; `tests/test_import_dead_cwd.py` 1.2.1; 80 green in the file under `-n 4`, suite 6153). The module's litter detector diffed the repo root, which every xdist worker shares, and a fresh CI checkout has no `.ruff_cache` until the first parallel ruff call mints one mid-module (macOS lane, PR #799 run 2). The children now run in a room the module owns under `tmp_path_factory`, the guard diffs that room, and a mutant child that writes a relative file still errors the module by name.

### Removed

- **Telegram is out of the tree: the skill lib sits untracked in `projects/telegram`, every Telegram handler that stayed is renamed `(disabled)`, no process, no citizen** (the owner's ruling 2026-10-22; @skills, @daemon, @hooks, devpulse). The skill (`skills/lib/telegram`, 52 modules and 29 tests), its doc and the two standards json files moved whole; `projects/*` is gitignored and off pytest's testpaths, so the move alone takes it out of git, CI, seedgo and CodeQL. In the tree: skills' `door_notifier`, daemon's `schedule/telegram_notifier` and hooks' `notification/telegram_response` are `(disabled)`; daemon's `run.py` 1.7.0 loses the notifier imports and every ping (the mail notices stay, a job's `notify` key is still accepted); the root `.aipass/hooks.json` loses `UserPromptSubmit.user_message_relay` (it named a module no longer in the tree and erred on every prompt) and `Stop.telegram_response`, and the provider manifest loses the relay bridge line; the `telegram` optional dependency group is gone; `pyrightconfig.json` excludes `*(disabled)*` so a parked file's dead import is no diagnostic. Tests that imported the lib are cut or parked, the skills off-switch examples use `screen_lock`, `switch_state.json` drops the telegram row, 42 dead bypass rules go. The prax monitor relay stays as it is: self-contained, opt-in, off. Suites: skills 476, daemon 780, hooks unchanged (its Telegram tests were already out of collection by name).

## [2026-10-21] — v2.8.24: AGENTS.md is the one instruction file on the host and in every project, doctor's sandbox-off row and Claude Code version row, pytest skips scratch dirs, the init update plan line, canary's no-break space, cli's bare demo

### Changed

- **AGENTS.md is the one instruction file; CLAUDE.md retired on the host** (DPLAN-0418 wave 1; `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/AGENTS.md`). Claude Code reads `AGENTS.md` natively since v2.1.277 whenever no `CLAUDE.md` sits in the working directory or above it, and every other coding agent reads the same file. The split is now a run of spaces or tabs, the same separator `align` uses; a no-break space is data inside a name. ### Fixed

- **The context gauge measured every session against a 200k window and cried compact at 23 percent** (@hooks, `modules/context_window.py` 1.1.0, `handlers/prompt/context_gauge.py` 1.2.0, `docs/project_config.md`; 24 pins red-first, suite 2605 to 2629). A seat on Opus 5.5 at 230k read `~230k/180k (128%) — compact fires soon` while Claude Code's own status line read 70 percent remaining, and no compact came, because Claude Code sizes the window per model: a `[1m]` suffix or a native-1M id is 1,000,000, anything else 200,000, capped by an explicit `autoCompactWindow` or `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW` (both real Claude Code settings, env first, clamped 100k to 1M), and auto-compact fires at window minus 33k. The gauge now reads the model from the transcript's newest assistant line, resolves that window, triggers at the real compact point instead of nine tenths of a guessed one, and prints the percent the status line prints. - **The phone's agent settings sheet refused every citizen of an external project** (@api, `handlers/host/server.py` 1.1.7, `handlers/host/settings.py` 1.0.1, `docs/host_api.md`; three route pins and one mode pin red-first; suite 1975 to 1978). `GET` and `POST /v1/agent-settings` resolved the branch against the AIPass registry alone, so vera under VERA-STUDIO read `400 settings_refused: Unknown branch` while the wheel beside it resolved her through the census. Both routes now take `project` (query on the read, a field on the write; absent or empty is the seat) and resolve through the census the way the wheel does. Found by the proof on vera's real file: a write staged through `mkstemp` carried the temp file's 0600 over the file's own mode; the staged file now takes the existing file's mode before the rename, and the BAUD settings door, which shares the writer, is cured with it. The phone face has to send the card's project with the branch; that change is BAUD's. The owner's phone, relayed by Vera Studio.

The pytest row ran `sys.executable -m pytest` from a parent of the package: on the pipx route that is pipx's venv, with no pytest and no `src/` beside it, so a clean install reported a fault it did not have while the clone's own venv collected 25353 tests.
