## [2026-10-19] — v2.8.22: a diagram kit and the How it works picture drawn from the code, RPLAN for research of any kind, the repo's GitHub chores through the door, a read token could switch on the relay

### Added

- **A diagram kit, and the README's "How it works" drawn from the code instead of from memory** (`tools/diagrams/`, `assets/diagrams/`, `README.md`). One JSON spec per picture (tiles, hubs, edges, labels, footers on a 1600×900 grid), `python tools/diagrams/build.py <name>` renders it to `assets/diagrams/<name>.png` and `src/<name>.svg` in one house style (navy, glowing tiles, white line icons, curved connectors); headless Chrome or Chromium first, Inkscape only when none is on PATH, a clear error with neither. The builder refuses an unknown icon, node, kind or key, overlapping tiles, text that collides, a line through a tile or a label, and anything off the canvas; `--check` renders every spec and verifies each PNG's size. The first picture replaces the README's ASCII block, which was written as a summary and said the owning agent wakes with "its README": it never does. The picture shows the round trip as the code runs it — terminal seat or phone room → manager → `drone @ai_mail dispatch` → the owning agent waking in its own folder with its prompt, `.trinity` memory, dashboard and the task mail → `drone @ai_mail reply` back to the manager's inbox — with the footers reworded to what holds ("every command goes through one bus", "every tool write passes the gates"). The ASCII block goes, the picture stands alone; the citizen tree gains `docs/`, `docs.local/`, `dropbox/` and `DASHBOARD.local.json`, and its README line says what the file is for today: the page for people. `.gitignore` re-includes `tools/diagrams/` under the blanket `tools/` ignore.

- **RPLAN holds research of any kind, and the navmap names all seven plan types** (@flow `templates/research_plans/default.md`; `.aipass/tier1_navmap.md`). The research template said RPLANs study external work and live in the external repo's root; it now serves a trace of our own code, a study of an external repo or package, a comparison or a measurement, with internal research living in the researching branch. Its Source table carries Subject, Version or commit, Question, Method, Brief, Report and Spot-checks, and Patterns Worth Adopting is Findings, a table that can name a bug or a gap. The navmap's Plans section listed three types and left the rest to `drone @flow templates`; it now names DPLAN, FPLAN, PPLAN, RPLAN, APLAN, CPLAN and TDPLAN in one line each. Found when a manager ran a research sweep as a scratch brief, six RPLANs in seven months.

- **`GET /v1/git-changes` at `repo` grain names the files root its paths open under** (@api, `handlers/host/reads.py` 1.2.0, `handlers/host/git_reads.py` 1.2.0, `docs/host_api.md`, seven pins red-first, nine mutants killed; suite 1963 to 1970). A `??` row at repo grain has no diff, and the phone could not open it through the files lane because nothing said which published root a repo-relative path was relative to, so the row answered in words. The answer now carries `root`: `{kind: aipass, name: null}` when the discovered repository is this server's own repo, `{kind: project, name}` when it is a census project's directory by resolved-path equality (never a prefix), `null` for a nested foreign tree or no repository; branch grain carries no `root`. A census that cannot answer for a non-seat repository is a 503 `read_unavailable`, never `null`, since `null` would claim "neither" when the truth is "unknown". The phone side follows in BAUD.

- **`drone @git release edit`, `label list|create` and `alerts list|dismiss`: the repo's GitHub chores through gh, owner tier** (@drone, `handlers/git/gh_chores.py`, `label_handler.py`, `alerts_handler.py` 1.0.0, `release_handler.py` 1.1.0, `repo_door.py` 1.8.0, `git_module.py` 1.11.0, `devpulse_ops/auth.py` 1.6.0, `help_pages.py` 1.5.0, `docs/git_interface.md`; suite 1703 to 1725). Three chores had no door, so a release whose notes publish.yml had taken from the wrong block, a Dependabot label the repo lacked and a code-scanning alert with its reason already written stayed the owner's by-hand work. OWNER/NAME is read from the repo's own `origin`, never from an argument, so a write lands on the repo whose ownership the gate checked; writes are gated `release-write`, `label-write`, `alerts-write` (devpulse in AIPass, a project's manager in its own repo), reads are global, `--repo <path>` is the admin door. `release edit <tag>` rewrites the notes with the tag's CHANGELOG block by publish.yml's rule (the tag between non-version characters, `---` dropped, cut on an entry boundary over 120,000 characters with a pointer at the full block) and sends nothing when they already match. `label create` compares names without case and reports a present label unchanged. `alerts dismiss` requires `--comment`, caps it at GitHub's 280, sends the reason in GitHub's words and dismisses only an open alert. Every write, no-ops included, is one row in `.ai_central/git_gh_writes.jsonl`. No force or bypass flag anywhere.

## [2026-10-18] — v2.8.21: the README rewritten around a 17-second demo, the phone's Files screen pages, the repo door merges a diverged project by name, the ratchet measures from a real checkout, CodeQL at zero

### Added

- **`GET /v1/dir` pages by `offset` and answers a `total`** (@api, `handlers/host/reads.py` 1.1.0, `server.py` 1.1.6, `docs/host_api.md`, 17 pins red-first, 11 mutants killed; suite 1949 to 1963). The host capped a directory at 400 entries with no count and no way to ask for the rest, so the phone drew a dropped-tail box on a 1,059-entry folder. Built to @baud's spec with its names: `offset` is a whole number from 0 (a negative, non-numeric or boolean one is the handler's 400 `read_refused`, never FastAPI's 422, so the route takes it as a string), `total` counts after the noise filter and before the cap, the page is `sorted[offset : offset + 400]` in the same order, `truncated` holds while `offset` plus the page is under `total`, an offset past the end answers an empty page with the total, and the audit line carries both. The phone's Files screen pages with a "show more" row on this shape. The running server serves it after a restart.

- **The repo door compares against `origin/<branch>` by name when no upstream is configured** (@drone, `handlers/git/repo_door.py` 1.6.0, `docs/external_repo_door.md`, three pins, three mutants; suite 1696 to 1698). A branch created locally never gets `branch.<name>.remote`, so `fetch`, `sync` and `merge-upstream --repo` refused projects/baud's dev while origin/dev sat eight commits ahead of it. After the fetch, when `@{u}` resolves to nothing, the door verifies `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` and uses it for the stand, the fast-forward and the merge, marking the stand line `(by name; none configured)`; `.git/config` is never written. A branch with neither keeps the old refusal.

- **`merge-upstream --repo` takes `--theirs <path>...`, a conflict resolution the caller names** (@drone, `handlers/git/repo_door.py` 1.7.0, `modules/git_module.py` 1.10.0, `docs/external_repo_door.md`, eight pins, twelve mutants; suite 1698 to 1703). A diverged project branch whose only conflicts are generated files (a lockfile and a manifest bumped by Dependabot) had no cure through the door. The paths are read before any fetch, repo-relative only (a bare flag, a leading slash, an absolute path or one outside the repo is refused); when every conflicted path is listed, each takes the upstream's side (`checkout --theirs`, `add`) and the one merge commit completes, the answer naming the paths taken and the new HEAD; any unlisted conflict aborts as before with every conflicted path named and the unlisted ones marked; a listed path that did not conflict is reported not needed. Never a push, never a force. The ledger row carries `theirs_taken`.

- **The external-repo door's ledger lives in AIPass's `.ai_central`, anchored on the AIPass home** (@drone, same files, one pin). The ledger path followed the deletion log's walk up from the caller's cwd, so a caller standing inside a project wrote an untracked `.ai_central/git_repo_door.jsonl` into that project. It now anchors on `resolve_aipass_home`, `AIPASS_DELETION_LOG` still overriding; a door use leaves nothing new in the repo it served.

- **`drone @spawn delete @branch --retire` is the door for a registered citizen** (@spawn, `handlers/registry.py` 1.1.0, `handlers/delete_ops.py` 1.2.0, `modules/delete.py` 1.2.0, `docs/retire.md`, five pins; suite 1052 to 1060). `create` writes `citizenship.registered: true`, so every citizen was protected from the moment it existed and `delete` had no way through short of hand-editing the live passport. A plain `delete` still refuses and now names the flag. `--retire` clears the passport layer only: the floor (spawn, devpulse, drone) and the registry owner still refuse, and the confirmation prompt still runs unless `--yes` is given. The archive is written first, then the ARCHIVED passport is rewritten with `registered: false` (its `registry_id` kept), then the branch is deregistered and its directory removed. The live passport is never edited: if the archive or that rewrite fails, the partial archive is removed and the branch stays whole, registered and protected. `--retire --dry-run` writes nothing.

### Changed

- **The README is rewritten around the install, the demo and three ideas** (`README.md`, 342 lines; drafted from a spec, two research passes over 13 framework READMEs and four agent-CLI demos, read by Vera Studio against raw main and the live CLIs, then by Gemini, Grok and Perplexity; the rulings sit in devpulse's record). Tagline "An operating system for AI agents that remember" and one who-for sentence; three badges on top (Tests, PyPI, License; status, coverage and the OpenSSF badges under Project status); the demo GIF under the link row; a two-line pipx install, proven in a clean sandbox, with what each line puts on screen, the side effects in one sentence and the full list of what install changes in a collapsed block; Start here in three steps that end at `drone @spawn create` (the old `aipass init agent`, which does not exist, is gone); How it works before Why AIPass, with a trimmed `passport.json` so the file shows what an agent is; Why AIPass cut from 172 to 118 words; the fleet, requirements, uninstall and compliance collapsed. Claims scoped to what verify could check: CI audits cover the 18 and `drone @seedgo audit` runs the same checks on the user's agents; nothing leaves the machine except what Claude Code itself sends to Anthropic; any Claude plan that includes Claude Code, not only Pro or Max; the PowerShell line is gone since native Windows is unsupported.

- **The README demo is a 17-second recording of three bus commands, and the logo has a light variant** (`assets/demo.gif` 181 KB, 1021x605, 70 frames, replacing a 4.2 MB, 90-second Claude-session capture whose frames showed the owner's hostname and a session URL; `assets/demo.sh`, the script that types the three commands at a fake prompt, recorded with asciinema 2.4 and rendered with agg 1.8 in the github-dark theme; `assets/logo-light.png`, logo.png inverted, for a `<picture>` light source). The commands: `drone systems`, `drone @memory search` finding a lesson an agent kept a month ago, `drone @seedgo audit aipass @cli` at 100. The README embeds them under the link row.

- **CONTRIBUTING.md says stable and names the seat to work from** (line 3 said "in beta" while the README, the status badge and the PyPI classifier said stable; the Development list gains the line that work on AIPass itself runs `claude` in `src/aipass/devpulse`, the orchestrator that holds the repo's git write).

- **One prose-skipper sorts docstrings from code for every line-based checker** (@seedgo, `handlers/aipass_standards/prose_lines.py` 1.0.0, 21 checkers migrated, 77 pins; suite 6066 to 6143). Twenty-one checkers each carried their own docstring toggle and the toggles disagreed, so the audit's 100 depended on which one a file happened to meet. The helper names docstring lines through `ast` (the string-constant first statement of a module, class or function; a docstring sharing its `def` line leaves that line code), comment-only lines and multi-line literal bodies through `tokenize`, and calls every other string literal code. Unparseable source raises, never an all-code answer: checkers fall back to `#` lines as the only prose they can name, and `modules` and `cli_flags` fail their row instead, since a `def` named only in a docstring must not pass. `cli_ux`'s Examples row needs a printed string starting with `examples` once Rich markup is stripped; a docstring or an unprinted constant never counts. Fleet audit after: 15 of 18 at 100; cli and memory surfaced a real Examples gap each (a help page with the word only in its docstring, a singular `Example:` heading), both cured the same night.

### Fixed

- **`sync-registry --fix` with no registry refuses on stderr instead of raising, and a class-filtered `update --all` turns an unreadable passport into a failed row** (@spawn, `handlers/sync_registry_ops.py` 1.0.2, `modules/sync_registry.py` 1.1.2, `handlers/update_ops.py` 2.3.2, two pins). The no-registry answer of `fix_owner_identity` came back check-shaped, so `_handle_fix` died on `KeyError: 'actions'`; it now answers `error` and the module prints it and exits 1. The class read of `update_all` sat outside the per-branch try, so one branch with a broken `passport.json` ended the whole run; it now records that branch as a failed row and goes on.

- **The weekly ratchet measures from a copy that holds the repo root, names a red baseline's failures, and records a week it could not measure as a point, not a failed job** (@seedgo, `tests_pytest_standards/envcopy.py` 1.3.0, `mutation_runner.py` and `mutation_shapes.py` 1.1.0, `audit_tests/selfcheck.py` 1.1.0, `modules/ratchet.py` 1.1.0, nine pins, five mutants; suite 6143 to 6152). The ratchet picked aipass and saw 35 red where a plain run is green: the env copy held only `src/aipass` and `conftest.py`, so the launcher, `setup.sh`, `CLAUDE.md`, the `.aipass` tier files and `tests/` a checkout has were missing and bootstrap, deriving its home from the package location, found no templates. The copy now carries the tracked repo-root files too (top-level files plus `.aipass` and `tests`, asked of `drone @git tracked` so ignored state stays out) and says the basis. A red baseline records every failing nodeid and message in the artifact and the archive, and self-check 4 reads the totals line so a long tail is no longer undercounted. `ratchet run` exits 0 on `measured` or `not_applicable` and prints the reason as a warning; a lane refusal still exits non-zero.

- **`update_project`'s managed-dirs pin reads the home as throwaway or real** (@aipass, `tests/test_bootstrap_update.py`; the one real red among the ratchet's 35). bootstrap skips `settings.local.json` for a throwaway home (a checkout under `/tmp`: CI, seedgo's audit copy) and the test expected six updated files either way. Parametrized over both homes with `is_throwaway_path` patched, the count pinned per case.

- **The host handlers cut CodeQL's taint paths where it looks** (@api, `handlers/host/reads.py`, `attach.py`, `backup.py`, `docs/host_surfaces.md`, four test files, ten pins; the twelve code-scanning alerts that turned PR #795's check red, open on main for weeks). reads.py, six path-injection sinks: `_fence` normalises with `realpath` and refuses unless the result starts with the root plus a separator before any `exists` or open, the guard shape CodeQL models; `read_file` and `list_dir` only see what `_fence` returns. attach.py, command-line injection: the argv builders refuse a room outside `[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*` or a watch target outside `[a-z0-9_,-]+` before any argv exists; argv was already a list, never a shell string. backup.py, four stack-trace alerts on the shared `answer()`: the unknown-job 404 returns a fixed sentence and logs the exception, the caller id no longer echoed; the `not_running` and `verb_refused` sentences stay, since the host API promises BAUD the backup line verbatim and the refusal sentence, both composed from constants and the caller's own values with no traceback, dismissed on GitHub with that reason. config.py, bind on all interfaces: a false positive, the probe binds the configured literal address on port 0 and `validate_bind` refuses every wildcard first. Suite 1938 to 1948.

- **`set_secret` logs that it wrote, never where** (@api, `apps/modules/secrets.py`, `docs/SECURITY.md`, one pin; the last CodeQL alert of the leg, clear-text storage with its sink in prax's JSON writer and four taint paths all sourced in api). The written secret file's path was logged into the operations log, against api's own rule that a path in the secrets base reads as a secret's location; the entry now carries `wrote: True`. The other three paths end in the auth-refusal audit, which records only `token_id`, the public 12-hex record id, never the bearer token, its hash or a prefix; the token store never passes through the JSON service and is written `0o600`. Dismissal reason for the owner: the value stored is token_id, the public 12 character hex identifier of a token record (uuid4 hex, first 12), logged in the auth-refusal audit so an operator can tell which revoked token was presented; it is never the bearer token, its sha256 hash or any prefix of them; the raw token is shown once at mint and never stored; the token store itself is written owner-only (0o600) by tokens.write_private_json, pinned by test_the_store_file_stays_owner_only. The config.py bind alert is a false positive: the taint starts at the wildcard string literals in `tests/test_host_api_config.py`, the probe binds the configured literal address on port 0, and `validate_bind` refuses every wildcard first. Suite 1948 to 1949.

- **The GitHub release takes the CHANGELOG block that names its tag, not the topmost one** (`.github/workflows/publish.yml`; reported by @verify: the v2.8.20 release body was the empty `## [Unreleased]` header that sat above the dated section at tag time). The extract step now selects the `## [...]` header carrying the tag between non-version characters, so `v2.8.2` never claims `v2.8.20`, and fails the job when no header carries it, never an empty release. The v2.8.20 body is corrected by hand on GitHub.

- **The broker secret is born 0600 and swapped in whole, never written in place** (@drone, `handlers/broker/daemon.py` 2.1.4, `docs/broker.md`, two pins in `TestIdentity`; CodeQL clear-text-storage on line 132). `Path.write_bytes` then `chmod 0600` left the fresh HMAC secret in a umask-mode file until the chmod, and a restart wrote into the same inode so a process still holding the previous file read the new secret. `_generate_secret` writes a staged file created with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` at 0600 and swaps it in with `os.replace`; the log line names the path only. Suite 1694 to 1696. If the rule still flags the staged write, the dismissal reason: the broker HMAC secret must be readable by its local launcher to sign the identify step; it is regenerated on every start, written to a git-ignored file staged with an exclusive create at mode 0600 and swapped in with os.replace, never logged, and used only between local processes of the same user.

- **The README links BAUD's repository, not a path that is not in the tree** (`README.md`; the owner 2026-10-17 23:49: "baud link doesnt work. it goes to aipass readme"). The face section linked `projects/baud/README.md`, a gitignored clone that GitHub cannot serve, so the link fell back to the AIPass README. BAUD is a separate repository, and the README now says so three times: a "BAUD, the phone face" link in the header row, the repository named where BAUD is introduced, and the face section pointing at `github.com/AIOSAI/baud` with the one-line installer under it.

## [2026-10-17] — v2.8.20: the fleet's comments say why, the audit at 100 on all 18, a project's manager runs its own repo's git, docs say what exists

### Added

- **`POST /v1/verbs/new-project`: the phone creates a project** (@api, `handlers/host/verbs.py` 1.1.0, `new_project_route.py` 1.0.0 new, `server.py` 1.1.5, `denials.py` 1.0.2, `docs/host_api.md`, `tests/test_host_verb_new_project.py` 22 tests; @aipass seam by devpulse: `handlers/new_project/__init__.py` 1.1.0 `create_project(host=)`, `modules/new_project.py` 1.1.0 publishes `create_project` and `TEMPLATES` on first use; FPLAN-0649, the owner 2026-10-16: "Lets add the create new project button"). Operate scope, body `{name, template?}`. The verb calls @aipass's `create_project` with the installation root named (a server cannot chdir per request), the same thing `aipass new <name> --template <t>` makes: project, registry, scaffold, resident manager agent, birth commit. A name outside `^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]{0,63}$` or an unknown template is 400 before the door is called; an existing project is 409 with the door's own sentence; a git, spawn, root or disk failure is 503 `project_door_failed` with a fixed sentence and a log ref, the words kept off the wire (the house rule from PR #774). 200 carries the new manager agent's branch name so the face can open its room. Red first (21 of 22 were 404), six mutants red, @api suite 1938, audit 100. BAUD's "+ new project" row in the phone switcher follows (@baud).

- **A project's manager opens and merges its own PRs** (@drone, `handlers/git/external_pr_handler.py` 1.0.0 new, `dev_pr_handler.py` 1.1.0, `plugins/devpulse_ops/merge_plugin.py` 1.1.0, `auth.py` 1.5.0 `external_owner_verbs()`, `help_pages.py` 1.4.0, `docs/git_access.md`, five test files, 15 new tests; the owner 2026-10-17: "Set up dev branch so pr goes to dev, just like aipass", "baud is a project owner, he has git, he is the branch manager"). `drone @git dev-pr` and `merge <PR#>` now run in an external project's repo for that repo's own manager, from its seat, under the CWD-bound owner tier. dev-pr refuses before any push unless the tree is on dev, no tracked file is modified and dev is ahead of origin/main; then it pushes dev and opens the PR dev → main on the repo's own GitHub slug read from origin. merge merges on that slug, deletes the head only when it is known and neither dev nor main, then checks out dev and fast-forwards it; a local failure after GitHub merged still names the merge. No PR lock, no sync with AIPass, no `pr_merged` event (that event syncs AIPass's own status page). The untranslated-verb refusal and `drone @git --help` list what an external manager may run, from one source; still refused there: pr, close-pr, smart-sync, fix, delete-branch. Tests run against a real repo and a bare origin with only gh and origin's URL stubbed; 12 mutants red; suite 1679 → 1694; audit 100. BAUD is the first project on the lane: @baud created dev from its own seat (its owner tier was already real: status, branches, checkout, commit), devpulse pushed the branch through the admin door, and the first PR dev → main opens from @baud's seat.

Four tests, 8 mutants red; suite 473.

- **The phone's host API serves the busiest processes, and a room that ends says so on its socket** (@api, `handlers/host/machine_route.py` 1.0.0 new, `handlers/host/machine.py` 1.1.0, `handlers/host/pump.py` 1.1.0, `server.py` 1.1.3; DPLAN-0414 themes 3 and 5, contracts C-B and C-C). `GET /v1/machine/processes?limit=20` (read) relays @skills' `machine_processes(limit)` verbatim: a fresh half-second cpu sample per read, never cached, asked when the PROC sheet opens and never on the monitor row's poll; a refusal maps as the vitals refusal does (503 `machine_refused` with the reason), a door that raises or answers off-shape is 503 `machine_door_failed` with one fixed sentence, a limit that is not a whole number is 400 `machine_limit_refused`. The room socket now closes with **4000 "room ended"** when the tmux session ends under it, instead of the framework's default normal close, so the phone can tell a finished room from a server that hung up and stop recreating an empty room with attach-or-create; a client that closed in the same instant is logged at info. 15 tests, 8 mutants red; suite 1905.

- **A delivered mail's feed notification carries the message's address** (@ai_mail, `handlers/email/delivery.py` 3.5.0; DPLAN-0414 theme 2, contract C-A, the owner on the phone's bell: "rly annoying, I click a sent email, it completely cut off"). The notification body stays the subject and a 100-character preview, because the feed file is read whole on every poll and is the wrong store for whole letters; the event now also carries `mail_id` (the id written into the recipient's inbox), `recipient` (branch, no `@`) and `project` (the registry's name for the recipient's root: `BAUD_REGISTRY.json` → `baud`, several registries answered by the one named after the root, none → `unknown` with a warning), so the phone's bell row opens the full message from the inbox file. Both delivery lanes stamp it; wake and dispatch events are unchanged. Two tests, red first; 10 mutants red; suite 1523.

- **Backup is back in daily use: the Drive lane uploads the snapshot, a nightly run of every registered project, and a prune lane for the stores** (@backup, `drive_sync` 2.1.0, `all` 4.1.0, `settings` 0.2.0, `status` 1.2.0, `drive_stats` 1.1.0, `prune` 1.0.0 new, `handlers/drive/floor.py` 1.0.0 new, `handlers/drive/tracker.py` 1.2.0, `handlers/drive/upload.py` 1.1.0, `handlers/cleanup/prune.py` 1.0.0 new, `handlers/project/config.py` 1.2.0, `backup.py` 1.2.0; DPLAN-0411, the owner's ask of 2026-10-16: "back up the snapshot not versioned ... versioned can get quite large ... say at 5am backup runs all daily, so we are always backed up"). `drive_sync` uploads the **snapshot** store under `AIPass Backups/<project>/snapshot/`; the versioned store, append-only at roughly twice the project, never leaves the machine again, and what an earlier sync put on Drive is left there for the owner to remove by hand. A tracker from the versioned era is set aside as `drive_tracker.versioned.json`, never overwritten, and a fresh one starts stamped `_lane: snapshot`. A never-leaves floor holds back `.secrets/`, `*.key`, `*.pem`, `.env`, `.env.*` and the host API's token store whatever `.backupignore` says: the local snapshot keeps them, only the lane that leaves the machine refuses them. The `drive_sync` setting in `.backup/config.json`, written and displayed since the rewrite but read by no code, is live: `all` runs the Drive step only when it is on and otherwise prints `Drive sync off for this project`; `drone @backup settings drive_sync on|off <project|@name>` sets it; the bare `drive_sync` verb runs regardless because the caller named it. `all --registered [--quiet]` runs the cycle for every registered project in registry order, one summary line each, exit non-zero if any failed, and that is the line `@daemon` runs as a command job from backup's own `.daemon/schedule.json` every day at 05:00 with a mail to @devpulse on start and finish; the AIPass repo root is registered as `aipass` beside `baud`. `status <project> --json [--sizes]` prints the backup door's status object for BAUD's card. `drive_stats` prints the Drive account's storage used and limit. `prune <project> [--apply]` lists, per store and top-level directory, the snapshot files and versioned file-folders whose project path the ignore spec now matches, with counts and bytes, and deletes nothing without `--apply`; with it, one trail row per removed path. The dry run tonight: 48.1 GB in baud's store and 48.0 GB in the root's, nearly all the Rust `target/` tree copied in August before `target/` was in `.backupignore`. 38 new tests, 41 mutants red; suite 467.

- **The phone's host API has a backup door** (@api, `handlers/host/backup.py` 1.0.0, `backup_route.py` 1.0.0, `server.py` 1.1.1; DPLAN-0411, the owner's ask of 2026-10-16 for a Backup card in BAUD's apps wheel). `POST /v1/backup/run` (operate) takes `{project, lane}` with `lane` one of `snapshot`, `versioned`, `all`, `drive_sync`, resolves the project through the read lane's resolver, runs `drone @backup <lane> <root>` on a worker thread and answers **202** with the running job at once, since `all` and `drive_sync` outlive a phone request; the same lane already running for that project is a 400 naming when it started. `GET /v1/backup/job?id=` (read) answers the job as `running`, `done` or `failed` with the last 600 characters of its output verbatim; jobs live in the server's memory, a finished one is kept an hour, and a forgotten id is **404 `job_unknown`**. `GET /v1/backup/status?project=[&sizes=1]` (read) passes `drone @backup status <root> --json` through with the server's running jobs added, and answers 503 rather than scrape the panel when `--json` is not on the machine. The door owns no mechanism: it imports no subprocess code and reaches @backup only through drone's router. Every wire shape is devpulse's backup door contract. 51 tests, five mutants red.

- **The backup door can stop a lane and shows what is running** (@api, `handlers/host/backup.py` 1.1.0, `backup_route.py` 1.1.0, `server.py` 1.1.2; DPLAN-0412, the owner's report of 2026-10-16 06:50: "ive no way to stop it. once it starts"). `POST /v1/backup/cancel {project, lane}` (operate) asks @backup to stop a lane through `drone @backup stop <root> <lane>` on the request thread and answers 200 with stop's line verbatim, or 404 `not_running` with @backup's line when nothing of that lane runs; the job table is never touched, the run's job closes by itself. A job whose lane exits 130 reads **`stopped`**, its summary the lane's last lines; every other non-zero exit stays `failed`. `GET /v1/backup/status` now passes @backup's own `running` list through entry for entry, each with `job` added (this server's id, or null for a run started from a terminal or by the daemon), so the phone sees every run and its progress, not only the ones the server started; an older @backup with no `running` key falls back to the server's in-flight jobs with one log line. The door still imports no subprocess machinery, and a test now pins that from the loaded module's namespace. Suite 1890, 20 mutants red.

- **Every backup lane can be stopped and shows its progress while it runs; the Drive lane checks its headroom before the first upload** (@backup, `stop` 1.0.0 new, `handlers/state/progress.py` 1.0.0 new, `handlers/state/stop_flag.py` 1.0.0 new, `handlers/state/lane_process.py` 1.0.0 new, `handlers/drive/quota.py` 1.0.0 new, `backup.py` 1.3.0, `snapshot` 2.2.0, `versioned` 3.1.0, `drive_sync` 2.4.0, `all` 4.2.0, `status` 1.3.0, `drive_stats` 1.1.1, `handlers/copy/snapshot.py` 3.2.0, `handlers/copy/versioned.py` 2.1.0, `handlers/drive/upload.py` 1.3.0; DPLAN-0412, the owner's report of 2026-10-16 06:50 after a Sync to Drive press ran fifteen minutes into a Drive with no room for it: "ive no way to stop it. once it starts. some info would be nice, like a status bar with progress too"). Every lane writes `.backup/running/<lane>.json` while it runs, once a second at most: the files and bytes done, the file just finished, the planned total when the lane knows one, and the verb that started it, so `all`'s sub-lanes read as Full backup; the file goes when the run ends, however it ends. `status <root> --json` reports a `running` list of the lanes in flight, `[]` when none, and drops a file whose process is gone; the status page names running lanes too. `drone @backup stop <root|@name> [lane]` stops a project's running lanes: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 30 s, signalling only a process whose command line is that root's backup lane, so a recycled pid is never hit. A stopped lane finishes the file in flight, saves the Drive tracker, writes no changelog entry, ends on `stopped by request: <done> of <total> files, <bytes>` and exits **130**; under `all` the remaining sub-lanes do not start, and `all --registered` starts no further project. `drive_sync` reads the account's quota before the first upload and prints `Drive: X to upload, Y free`, or refuses with `Drive has X free; this run needs Y. Nothing uploaded.` as its last line, exit 2, nothing uploaded; a quota it cannot read refuses the same way with `Drive quota unavailable: <reason>. Nothing uploaded.`; an `all` whose Drive step cannot fit ends on that sentence and exits 2 while its snapshot and versioned copies stand. By hand: a 20,001-file snapshot stopped 6.4 s in with 18,794 files copied, the running dir empty afterwards, exit 130. 31 new tests, 23 mutants red; suite 516.

### Changed

- **A project's manager writes its own project's files; a dry-run update and a shell syntax check are reads** (@hooks, `modules/write_ownership.py` 2.4.0, `shell_programs.py` 1.4.0, `shell_reader.py` 1.3.0, `handlers/lifecycle/rollover.py` 2.3.0, `docs/edit_gate.md`; the owner's ruling of 2026-10-16, superseding DPLAN-0356 item 5). @baud, @vera and @aipass_site were refused on their own project's files outside their branch row (the project root, `app/`) and told to email the manager, which was themselves; for weeks they drafted under `docs.local/` for devpulse to land. The edit and Bash lanes now let the project's manager row write its project's unrowed files; a non-manager seat is still refused and told whom to email, a file inside another branch's row is still that branch's, and AIPass's own root stays the verified admin seat's. `aipass init update <root> --dry-run` is a read; `bash -n <file>` (a syntax check) is a read for both gates while `bash <file>` stays a write. The promote probe no longer writes a false ERROR into the shipped rollover log, and AIPass's own config carries `SessionStart:release_notice` so the provider entry is no longer an orphan (silent at the source repo by its own rule). Nine red-first tests, 11 mutants red, live proof on the real registries; suite 2589.

### Fixed

- **The 260-character store-path guard is Windows-only; POSIX files over it are stored** (@backup, `handlers/path/builder.py` 2.2.0, `copy/snapshot.py` 3.2.1, `copy/versioned.py` 2.1.1, `tests/test_snapshot_fidelity.py` 2.2.0, `tests/test_versioned_engine.py` 2.1.0; CI 38999228656 on PR #792). 260 is Windows' MAX_PATH; both lanes applied it everywhere, so on macOS and Linux a long path was silently kept out of every snapshot and versioned store, the nightly run included (CI met it first: the prune fixture's 60-character name under macOS's 150-character tmp prefix). `_MAX_PATH` is 260 on Windows and None elsewhere, `exceeds_max_path()` is the one guard both lanes call, and an over-long POSIX path is the OS's own OSError, which the lanes already record as an errors row. Red-first pins under both seams, four mutants red, the macOS prefix simulated locally (4 failed before, 8 passed after).

- **A raised stop flag no longer leaks into the next backup test on the same xdist worker** (@backup, `tests/conftest.py` 1.3.5; CI 38999228669 on PR #792). The stop flag is process-global and `catch_sigterm` lowers it only on entry, so a stop test that fired a real SIGTERM left it up and every versioned-engine class that followed on that worker stored nothing (serial green, `--dist loadscope` red). An autouse fixture resets the stop state before and after every backup test; the product and the entry-point contract are untouched. Two-file xdist run green at 2, 3 and 4 workers; the fixture emptied is red again. Suite 520 serial and under xdist.

- **Backup's degraded-resolve tests pin the exact path** (@backup, `tests/test_dead_cwd_imports.py` 2.0.2; FPLAN-0647, recorded on the owner's ledger at PR #774). `TestSafePathHelper`'s two oracles accepted any absolute path with the right name and re-derived the climb from the product's own expression; both now assert the exact path the fixture built under `tmp_path`, so a fallback that answers the cwd, or a climb off by one, fails the suite. Three mutants red; suite 516.

- **The healthy-world path oracle resolves a real symlink** (@backup, `tests/test_dead_cwd_imports.py` 2.0.3; FPLAN-0647). `test_returns_resolved_path_normally` compared a path with no symlinks against its own resolve, so a `module_file` that skipped `resolve()` stayed green. The test now builds a directory symlink under `tmp_path` and expects the real file spelled from the fixture's realpath, never from the product; it skips with a reason where symlinks cannot be made. Return-raw mutant red; suite 516.

- **A dispatch bounce that could not be delivered is no longer silent** (@ai_mail, `handlers/dispatch/dispatch_monitor.py` 2.10.0, `tests/test_dispatch_monitor.py` 1.5.0, `docs/wake_pipeline.md`; FPLAN-0647, the owner's loose-ends night 2026-10-16). Both callers dropped `_send_bounce`'s result, so a bounce drone did not deliver left the dispatcher believing the sender was told. Both now pass it through one helper: on failure, one `BOUNCE NOT DELIVERED` warning naming the branch, the sender and the reason, and the dispatch's completion status (the report, the register's closing record, the feed title) ends with `, bounce NOT delivered to @sender`. `_send_bounce` no longer logs its own warning, so a failure is one line, and the transport's exception text is kept in `last_bounce.json`. Three tests, two red first; 8 mutants red; suite 1526.

- **A command job's timeout no longer SIGKILLs a process group that may have been reissued** (@daemon, `handlers/schedule/command_job.py` 1.0.1, `tests/test_run_module.py` 1.2.3, `docs/command_jobs.md`; FPLAN-0647, the owner's loose-ends night 2026-10-16). `_stop_tree` waited on the leader after SIGTERM, which reaped it, then sent SIGKILL to its group unconditionally; a reaped pid, and so its pgid, can be reissued to an unrelated process. The grace is now polled with `os.waitid(..., WNOWAIT)`, so a leader that exits on TERM stays an unreaped zombie holding the pgid while the group is killed, and only then is it reaped; a leader found already reaped skips the group signal with a warning naming why. The private group signal became the public `signal_group` seam. Three red-first tests (a grandchild that ignores SIGTERM dies with its group whether the leader exits or ignores; a group signal sent after the leader is reaped never reaches a sentinel holding the pgid), the old order red on the reuse pin; suite 787.

- **A rollover limit's `is_override` follows one rule, and a budget-clamped default is never listed as an override** (@memory, `handlers/json/config_loader.py` 1.7.0, `tests/test_config_loader.py` 1.3.0; held from DPLAN-0414 theme 7, landed on the owner's loose-ends night 2026-10-16). `is_override` is true only when the count in force came from `per_branch` and differs from the default, written by one function for every row; the budget clamp lowers the number in force without moving where it came from, so `drone @memory config get` no longer lists a clamped default under OVERRIDES. Five tests pin (count, source, is_override) whole, one red first; 3 mutants red; suite 1974.

- **A file tap in the phone's Git app opens its patch from an agent card, a staged-only change opens, and a repository with no remote is an answer** (@api, `handlers/host/git_reads.py`, `server.py`, `api.py`, `modules/host_pair_cli.py`, `host_serve.py`, `host_config_cli.py`, `docs/host_api.md`, `docs/git_remote.md`; DPLAN-0414 theme 11, the owner on his phone 2026-10-16: "Git is also a bit glitchy. Half the time I can't click into a file"). At branch grain the change rows are branch-local paths while `/v1/diff` matched the patch's repo-relative headers exactly, so every tap from an agent card's GIT tile was refused: the path now gains the branch's repo-relative prefix before matching, a path already carrying it is matched as given, repo grain is unchanged. A file `git status` lists from the index alone (`M `, `A `) had no patch because the worktree diff runs without `--staged`: when the worktree patch does not touch the file the index is asked, the staged patch is served with `staged: true`, and an `MM` row shows its unstaged half (both halves need a HEAD flag drone's diff door does not have). A repository with no remote answered a refusal where the phone's Git sheet draws its links; it now answers 200 with `remote`, `url` and `web` null (contract C-D), and an unreadable repository stays the refusal. Also: `drone @api --help` and `host-api --help` name the real verbs (`tokens` never existed; `host_pair_cli` claimed `--help` first and printed only its own line). 11 tests, red first; 13 mutants red; suite 1916, audit 100.

- **A memory limit write re-renders the branch meta line it moved, and `health @branch` is a working door** (@memory, `handlers/tracking/tab_renderer.py` 1.7.0, `modules/rollover_config.py` 1.3.0, `modules/health.py` 1.1.0, `memory.py` 1.3.1; found by DPLAN-0414 theme 7's live test on @canary: set sessions to 3, roll, set back to 15, and the file's `sessions_meta` still read "keep 3" until the next rollover or push). `config set` and `config set-default` now compare the enforced count of every registry branch before and after the write through the one resolver and re-render the `*_meta` lines of the branches whose count moved, naming them ("Meta lines re-rendered: @canary"); a branch holding its own count is left byte-identical, an unreadable registry is one warning and no render, and the `--json` payloads are unchanged. `drone @memory health @branch` printed the module docstring; it now renders the branch's health (per file "ok (N lines)" / "rollover due - reason" / "not found", then the entry-size violation count, each violation a warning), exits 2 on an unknown branch or a second argument, and a help flag anywhere explains. Ten tests red first, 6 mutants red; suite 1969.

- **`status --json` shows the Drive lane's last run** (@backup, `drive_sync` 2.2.0, `status` 1.2.1, `handlers/path/builder.py` 2.1.0; DPLAN-0411 follow-up). `lanes.drive_sync` answered null even after an upload, because `drive_sync` never wrote to the project changelog the status reader reads. A run whose uploads all succeed now appends one changelog entry with mode `drive_sync`, written by the same changelog writer and in the same shape as snapshot and versioned, with `files_copied` set to the files that run uploaded; `status --json` reads `last` and `files` from it, and `runs` counts it. A run with a failed upload, or with nothing to upload, writes none, which is the snapshot lane's rule. `all`'s Drive step is the same function, so it writes the same entry. `builder.build_drive_path`, which has no callers, described the old versioned-era layout and now names `<root>/<project>/snapshot/<path>`. Three tests added to existing files and three edited; 5 mutants red; suite 470.

- **`drive_sync` saves the Drive tracker every 50 uploaded files, as its code always said** (@backup, `handlers/drive/upload.py` 1.3.0, `drive_sync` 2.4.0; DPLAN-0412, found while building stop). The periodic save in the upload loop never ran: the loop was called without the project root the save needs, and the test that stood for it gated on `hasattr` of a MagicMock, which is always true, so the dead path read as covered. This morning's killed Sync to Drive left about 300 MB on Drive with a tracker reading zero files, every upload orphaned. The root is passed through now, the save fires every 50 files, and a killed, stopped or failing run leaves what it uploaded tracked.

- **Wake-backs and bounces reach a manager in another project again** (@ai_mail, `handlers/dispatch/dispatch_monitor.py` 2.9.0; found by @ai_mail's own rounds on 2026-10-16, devpulse's ruling A). Since e26abd25 (2026-10-04) every monitor notice was sent from ai_mail's home inside AIPass, so a manager in another project, @vera in Vera-Studio, had its wake-backs refused by delivery's cross-project fence: three finished `@verify` runs on 2026-10-15/16 were never announced. When the recipient is a citizen of the woken branch's own project and that project is not AIPass, the notice is now sent from the woken branch's home, which sits beside the recipient; every other notice still goes from ai_mail's home, and a project registry that cannot be read logs a warning and falls back to it. The fence in `delivery.py` is unchanged: the alternative, an exemption for monitor notices, would have widened a security wall that anything setting `AIPASS_BRANCH_NAME` could walk through. Four pins in existing test files, red on the old code; nine mutants red; suite 1521.

- **The memory search stand-ins read stdin before exiting** (@memory, `tests/test_search_extras.py` 1.0.2; macOS CI 38128154826). A stand-in store that exited unread left the search writing into a closed pipe, and a worker with the kernel-default SIGPIPE died there with no traceback. Each stand-in now reads its stdin first, as the real store does.

- **hooks' README is back under the 10,000-character startup ratchet cap** (@hooks `README.md`, 9,969 characters). The comment-budget rows pushed it to 10,213 and seedgo's fleet-walk test went red; six docs-table descriptions were trimmed.

## [2026-10-15] — v2.8.18: Windows leaves CI, Windows users run AIPass inside WSL2

### Changed

- **Windows leaves CI; Windows users run AIPass inside WSL2** (the owner's ruling 2026-10-15 after a precedent survey; DPLAN-0410). The `Windows Test` lane is retired by rename, `windows-test.yml` → `windows-test.yml(windows_disabled)`: GitHub Actions runs every `.yml` under `.github/workflows/` whatever its stem, so the suffix sits after the extension and the file stays in git, unread. The `e2e-wheel` matrix drops its `windows-latest` leg. Nothing else moves, as every project that took this road did (Ansible, Celery, Redis, metis, clanker): the product files carrying Windows branches, the Windows-behaviour tests that run on Linux through a mocked platform and seedgo's `windows_compat` standard all stay, so the code keeps tolerating Windows paths while no runner proves them. The README's platform line now reads Linux and macOS natively, Windows through WSL2, and says plainly that native Windows and Git Bash are no longer tested. One Windows-only test (hooks `test_cc_sessions`) no longer runs anywhere. The `Windows Test` required status check in branch protection is the owner's to remove; until it goes, every PR waits on it.

## [2026-10-15] — v2.8.17: the personal settings file never changes unseen (a backup and a receipt on every door, doctor --fix asks first), drone @git untrack, aipass install --source, the autofix lane skips scratch

### Added

- **`aipass doctor --fix` shows the settings change and asks before it writes** (@aipass, `provider_wire` 1.5.0, `provider_reconcile` 1.2.0, `_doctor_wire` 1.2.0, `doctor` 1.3.0, `_doctor_fix` 1.1.0; FPLAN-0646, the owner's ruling of 2026-10-15). `doctor --fix` and plain `doctor` now print the planned changes to `~/.claude/settings.json`, one line each, plus a unified diff of the file, and ask once: `Apply these N changes to ~/.claude/settings.json? [y/N]`. Anything but `y` writes nothing and says so. With no tty and no `--yes`, `--fix` writes nothing and its row reads `not applied: no tty — aipass doctor --fix --yes`; the new `--yes` keeps the old silent write. The install tail never asks (it runs inside the installer's one Enter). Each receipt's summary opens with the consent: `consent: y (tty)`, `consent: --yes` or `consent: install`. `doctor --fix --json` carries the plan under `provider_settings` (`planned`, `notes`, `diff`, `applied`) and writes only with `--yes`. Breaking for headless callers: an agent that ran `aipass doctor --fix` to wire settings must now pass `--yes`. Six tests, three mutants red.
- **A backup and a receipt before any tool writes `~/.claude/settings*.json`** (@hooks, `security/settings_backup` 1.0.0, `config/gates` 1.2.0; FPLAN-0645, the owner's ruling 2026-10-15). His ask rules already made the Edit tool prompt him on his personal settings file, but nothing kept the file as it was when he accepted, and a Bash write met no rule at all. A new fail-closed PreToolUse gate, last in the gate set, fires on Edit, MultiEdit, Write, NotebookEdit and Bash: when the call writes `~/.claude/settings*.json` (`~`, relative paths and symlinks resolved; a Bash target as `git_gate`'s protected lane reads it) it copies the file into `~/.claude/.backup/settings/` as `<file>.<YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SS>.<door>` (`-2` on a same-second collision, never an overwrite, no pruning), appends one line to `receipts.jsonl` there (door, actor, pid, `before_sha256`, summary), then allows; a failed copy or append refuses the call, naming the path and the error. Stdlib only on the tool lane, no import shared with @aipass's Python doors, which write the same folder in the same shape. A non-matching Edit costs ~35 µs. Six tests, three mutants red. Wired in `.aipass/hooks.json` as the last PreToolUse entry.
- **`drone @git untrack <path ...>`** (@drone, `untrack_handler` 1.0.0, `git_module` 1.8.0, `auth` 1.3.0, `help_pages` 1.2.0; DPLAN-0409 C1, from the 2026-10-15 review of agent work). `3ccc004f` committed four seedgo ratchet artifacts carrying the owner's home path; `56109bf5` ignored their directory, but a `.gitignore` line never untracks, and with raw git blocked for every seat there was no door to `git rm --cached`. The new owner-tier verb classifies each path as `tracked` does: a tracked file leaves the index and stays on disk; an untracked, ignored, missing or outside path is refused by name with its class, a directory unless `--recursive`; exit 1 on any refusal, after the accepted paths ran. It never commits, and its last line names the next step, `drone @git commit "<message>"` with no paths, since commit with paths would stage the file back. `--repo` is not served. Seven tests on a real repo, four mutants red.
- **`aipass install --source PATH|URL`** (@aipass, `install.py` 1.5.0; DPLAN-0408, the install sandbox). Clones AIPass from that path or URL instead of the public repo. A local path is cloned as its `file://` URI with `--depth 1`, so only its committed HEAD crosses, never the working tree; a missing path, a file or a directory without `.git` is refused with the path named (exit 2), never a silent fall back to GitHub. The default is unchanged. BAUD's `docker/sandbox.sh` uses it to install the local checkout in a fresh container in minutes instead of a merge train per change.

### Fixed

- **README: the personal settings file's cleanup entry tells the truth again** (PPLAN-0067 truth check). It still said each doctor re-wire left a `settings.json.bak.*` beside the file, a scheme this release retires; it now names the `~/.claude/.backup/settings/` copies and the receipts ledger, that `doctor --fix` asks first, and lists that folder among the things install leaves outside the project. The `aipass install` flag list gains `--source PATH|URL`.
- **The AUTO-FIX diagnostics lane no longer judges scratch** (@hooks, `lifecycle/auto_fix` 1.5.0; devpulse's concern 2026-10-15, three sightings on two seats). An edit under a directory named `docs.local`, `dropbox`, `.backup` or `.archive`, or under the harness scratchpad (a `scratchpad` directory below a `claude-<uid>` one), ran the full lint, pyright and seedgo lane and answered with "Fix these errors now. Do not skip or defer": a throwaway probe was ordered dressed with a META block and a layer, and a recorded type error on it would have fenced the seat's next edit through `edit_gate`. Such an edit now runs no check, records nothing in the seat's diagnostics state, and answers `[diagnostics] skipped: <ground> is scratch`. Matched on whole directory names, either slash; a `scratchpad` without the harness root and a name that only shares a prefix (`docs.localized`) stay judged. Git-ignored paths are deliberately not skipped: `.trinity/` is ignored, and its JSON is what the corruption check guards. Nine tests, three mutants red.
- **A failed settings write raises and leaves no receipt** (@aipass, `provider_wire` 1.5.1; FPLAN-0646 follow-up). The fleet json writer returns False on a failed write instead of raising, and the backed-up door ignored that, so a failed write still appended a receipt whose `after_sha256` was the unchanged file. `_write_with_receipt` now checks the return: on False it raises `SettingsBackupError` naming the path and writes no receipt; the backup taken just before stays. One test, the ignore-the-return mutant red.
- **The installer writes the provider settings file once, through the backed-up door** (@aipass, `provider_wire` 1.4.1; FPLAN-0645 follow-up; setup.sh cut by devpulse). setup.sh ran a second, stdlib heredoc right after `refresh_provider_hooks` that rewrote the personal settings file with no backup and no receipt, setting `AIPASS_HOME`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY`, `PYTHONUTF8` under MSYS and 30 deny rules (the manifest's 25 plus five home-expanded duplicates of the `~/.secrets` rules). `refresh_provider_hooks` now merges the manifest's env and permissions too, through the same `_merge_env` / `_merge_permissions` helpers `auto_wire_provider` uses, so install takes one backup and leaves one receipt under `setup-sh`, and the heredoc is cut. Both merges stay additive: a value already in the file is kept, a rule already there is not added twice. The one exception is `AIPASS_HOME`: install re-points it to the tree being installed with a `Re-pointed AIPASS_HOME <old> -> <new>` line, as the heredoc did, so a re-install from a new clone heals the split; `doctor --fix` never re-points. `PYTHONUTF8=1` lands only under Git Bash / MSYS (the heredoc's own predicate, now in the wire). Nine tests, nine mutants red.
- **Every Python door that writes the personal Claude settings file backs it up and leaves a receipt first** (@aipass, `handlers/settings_backup.py` 1.0.0, `provider_wire` 1.3.0, `provider_reconcile` 1.1.0, `doctor` 1.2.0; FPLAN-0645, the owner's ruling of 2026-10-15). Four doors rewrote `~/.claude/settings.json` from Python with no prompt: `doctor --fix`, the install tail's doctor run, setup.sh's `refresh_provider_hooks` and the stale-deny cleanup. Two of them backed up to `settings.json.bak.<date>`, which a second write the same day overwrote, and two backed up nothing. Each now copies the file into `~/.claude/.backup/settings/` as `settings.json.<YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SS>.<door>` immediately before its write (0700 folder, 0600 copy, `-2`, `-3` on a same-second collision, an existing backup never overwritten, never pruned) and appends one line to `receipts.jsonl` after it: time, door (`doctor-fix`, `install`, `setup-sh`, `reconcile-stale-deny`), actor, pid, backup, sha256 before and after, the door's action lines. A backup or receipt that cannot be written raises `SettingsBackupError` and the settings file is left as it was. `doctor --fix` prints both paths; the `.bak.<date>` scheme is retired; the hooks row's stale "Run aipass init run" hint now says `aipass doctor --fix`. The folder shape is the contract @hooks' tool-door handler writes too. Nine tests, eleven mutants red.
- **prax: "a logger never raises" holds at the last two sites** (@prax, `handlers/logging/setup.py` 1.4.0; DPLAN-0409 C4, from the 2026-10-15 review of agent work). `055e7bea` guarded the module tiers, but `setup_system_logger` still called `get_system_logs_dir()` bare, and the external-project branch of `setup_individual_logger` still made `<project>/system_logs` and `logs/` bare, so an unmakeable log home raised out of a logging setup call. Both now open through `_tier_handler`, the external branch resolving its directories inside the guard: one `Log handler failed for …` line and a NullHandler for that tier, which stays silent until the process restarts, by design. `setup_system_logger`'s own local tier took the same guard, and its `logger_setup_complete` record names a muted tier's file as null. Two tests, one per site, red with either guard removed.
- **The four seedgo ratchet artifacts are untracked** (`1e66860a`; DPLAN-0409 C1, from the 2026-10-15 review of agent work). `3ccc004f` committed four per-branch ratchet JSONs under `src/aipass/seedgo/.seedgo/ratchet/` (about 1.1 MB, carrying the owner's home path); `56109bf5` scrubbed the content and ignored the directory, but an ignore line never untracks a file already in the index, so they rode every clone since. The first use of `drone @git untrack` takes them out of the index; the files stay on disk for seedgo's ratchet and `ratchet_series.jsonl` stays tracked as the public series. No history rewrite: the paths carried a username only.
- **The external-repo door's git can no longer hang drone** (@drone, `repo_door` 1.4.0; DPLAN-0409 C2, from the 2026-10-15 review of agent work). Since `97446b67` the door's own runner fetches origin and merges, with no timeout and a child that could prompt: a dead remote, a stalled network or a credential prompt held the call until drone's 60 s command timeout killed the parent, and git kept running. Every runner call now carries a budget (120 s for `fetch` and `merge`, 60 s for the local reads) and `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` in a copy of the environment, and a timeout is the verb's failure naming git's verb, the seconds and the repo. Three tests, four mutants red.
- **`run --repo <path>` refuses gh's attached `-RVALUE`** (@drone, `repo_door` 1.4.0; DPLAN-0409 C2). The check caught `-R VALUE` and `-R=VALUE` only, so `-RAIOSAI/other` passed and named a second repo beside the door's. gh's only `-R` short flag is `--repo`, so any argument starting `-R` is now refused with the same text. One parametrized test, red on the old check.
- **`drone` finds its AIPass home without `AIPASS_HOME`** (@drone, `registry_handler` 1.3.0, `drone.py` 1.3.0; the owner's test 14, DPLAN-0407). A stranger's install ended on `Branch '@api' not found in registry`: the terminal that ran the one line started before setup.sh wrote `AIPASS_HOME` into the shell rc, and the branch lookup's fallback read only that variable. `resolve_aipass_home()` now answers in order: `AIPASS_HOME` as given; the interpreter's own install (`<home>/.venv/bin/python3` → `<home>`, when it holds `AIPASS_REGISTRY.json`), which is every installed `drone`; the newest enrolled home in `~/.aipass/trusted_projects.json`. Every reader in the router goes through it, so `drone @api …` works in any terminal after an install. The "Tip:" prints only when all three failed and then names what was tried.
- **`drone` runs a branch app on its home's own interpreter** (@drone, `registry_handler` 1.4.0, `router_handler` 1.3.0, `discovery_handler` 1.1.0, `scanning/scanner` 1.1.0; the owner's first sandbox run, DPLAN-0408). A stranger's machine holds aipass twice: the uv tool venv whose `drone` comes first on PATH, and the home's own `.venv` with the home's code installed editable. The home's `api.py`, launched on the tool venv's python, imported its handlers from the tool's site-packages and the handlers fence refused it (`ACCESS DENIED: Cross-branch handler import blocked`), so `drone @api host-api pair phone` crashed instead of printing the QR. `branch_interpreter(branch_path)` now answers at every launch site: `sys.executable` when the branch is outside the resolved home or this drone is the home's; otherwise the home's `.venv/bin/python` (`Scripts/python.exe` on Windows), logged INFO once per home; a home without a venv keeps `sys.executable` with one WARNING naming it. Nine tests across the handler and the three launch-site suites.
- **api: the server runs on its home's interpreter, and `pair` refuses when nothing listens** (@api, `host/lifetime.py` 1.2.0, `host/pairings.py` 1.1.0; the owner's second sandbox run, DPLAN-0408). With drone's launch cured, the QR printed with the right tailnet URL and the phone got "site can't be reached": no server. `aipass install` runs in the uv tool venv, which has no `host` extra, and calls the `serve_detached` door in-process; `serve_argv` spelled the server as `sys.executable` plus this copy's `api.py`, so the tool venv's copy started, outlived the settle and died on `No module named 'fastapi'`. `write_unit` shares that spelling, so a desktop's boot unit would have carried the same bug. `server_home()` now answers which interpreter and which api branch the server runs from: this process's own when no home resolved or this copy lives inside the home (drone's `resolve_aipass_home` door); otherwise the home's `.venv` python and the home's `src/aipass/api`, logged INFO once; a home missing either is a `LifetimeError` naming the path, never a fall back. `serve_argv`, the Popen's cwd and the unit's `WorkingDirectory` all take it, and so do the serve record, the detached server's log and the rendered unit (`lifetime` 1.3.0: `_runtime_dir()` is the home's api `logs/`), so `drone @api host-api status` and `stop` from the home see a server the install started from the tool venv. Then the second fault: `pair phone` had minted for the dead server because it checked only the configured bind. `mint_pairing` now sends one GET to the bind before anything is stored; nothing answering is a `PairingError` whose text is the two pasteable lines (`serve --detach`, then the same `pair` command); an error status names `host-api status`. Eleven tests, five mutants red.
- **spawn: a newborn's todos tab names its own backlog** (@spawn, rounds 2026-10-14; `core.py` 1.4.2, `mint_ops.py` 1.1.1). A freshly minted citizen's `todos_meta` read `.backup/todo/<branch>/backlog.json` and `next #?`, because the mint asked @memory's renderer for the meta tabs without saying which branch. `mint_citizen` now hands the newborn's folder name to `load_meta_tabs`, and `core._load_meta_tabs` passes it to `render_all_meta_tabs`. One test, red on the old code.
- **`aipass install` reads every value flag in both spellings** (@aipass, `install.py` 1.5.1; DPLAN-0409 C3, from the 2026-10-15 review of agent work). `_flag_value` read only `--flag value`, so `--source=/x` clones the public repo without a word, against `19f7408e`'s own "never a silent fall back"; install.sh passes the space form, so the sandbox never saw it. One module-level `_flag_value(args, flag)` now serves `--path`, `--baud-tag` and `--source` in either spelling; an empty `--source=` or `--baud-tag=` is refused with exit 2 before anything is created, as the valueless form already was. Six tests, one mutant red.
- **aipass: the phone step's dead token-receipt path is gone** (@aipass, `phone_ready.py` 1.2.0; DPLAN-0409 C3). `receipt_line`, `RECEIPT_REFUSED`, `LABEL_PLACEHOLDER` and `PhoneReady.receipt` fed a line nothing has printed since the pairing QR replaced the token hop (`7b0f7694`); grep found no reader. Removed with their test, whose behaviour was removed on purpose there.
- **setup.sh: a missing srt resolver is a broken checkout, back in ACTION NEEDED** (devpulse, root file; DPLAN-0409 C6, from the 2026-10-15 review of agent work). The zero-question install (v2.8.16) moved the whole sandbox block out of ACTION NEEDED, including `srt … skipped (resolver script missing: …/_srt_resolve.mjs)`. That resolver is a tracked file of the checkout, not an optional tool: its absence means the clone is incomplete. That one row now adds an ACTION NEEDED item naming the file and the cure (`drone @git status`, `drone @git fix`, or re-run the install line). The optional tools (bwrap, node, npm, srt itself, rg) stay quiet, as DPLAN-0407 ruled.
- **trigger: `errors detail` renders a logged message that holds bracket markup** (@trigger, rounds 2026-10-15; `apps/modules/errors.py` 1.4.1). A registry row whose message carried Rich markup (live row 2cb55c40 holds `[/rc]`) raised `MarkupError` inside the detail panel, and drone answered `Unknown command`. The message, normalized message, suppress reason and log path are now escaped before the panel renders them, so the text prints verbatim. One test in `test_errors.py`, red on the old code.

## [2026-10-13] — v2.8.15: QR pairing (the pair door, the install ends with the QR), seedgo's rendered_path_oracle, the README uninstall line

### Added

- **api: QR pairing, the phone joins by holding it up to the screen** (2026-10-13; api building, devpulse landing; DPLAN-0406 / FPLAN-0643). Test 12 of the front door passed on the owner's own phone and surfaced the one real gap: the bearer token had to be carried from the machine to the phone by email or typed by eye, the two routes SECURITY.md forbids. `drone @api host-api pair <label> [--scope read|operate] [--ttl 30..900]` mints a one-use pairing code (32 random bytes, only its sha256 stored in `~/.secrets/aipass/host_api/pairings.json`, five minutes by default) and prints a QR of `http://<bind>:<port>/#pair=<code>` as terminal block characters (segno, a new core dependency), the URL beneath it, and the expiry line; a loopback bind is refused before minting, since a phone cannot reach it. `POST /v1/pair` is the one route without a bearer: a live code is marked used under the token store's lock and only then traded for a bearer through `issue_token` (no receipt file: the phone holds the only copy); unknown, expired and used get one identical 401 `pairing_refused` (which it was goes to the log with the caller's address), the eleventh attempt per address per minute is 429 `too_many_attempts`, a missing or non-string code is 400 `invalid_request`, an unreadable store is 503 `pairing_unavailable` with a ref. Module door: `mint_pairing(label, scope, ttl_seconds)`, `render_qr(text)`, `PairingError`, for the install's phone step. `handlers/host/pairings.py` 1.0.0, `pair_route.py` 1.0.0 (server.py sits at its line cap), `modules/host_pair_cli.py` 1.0.0, `tokens.py` 1.2.0 (`store_lock`, `write_private_json` shared by both stores), `server.py` 1.1.0, `host_api.py` 1.4.0; 29 tests in `test_host_pairing.py` (the one new file permitted this leg), five mutants red, 1767 → 1796; audit 100. The face's side (baud main 3d4217f) reads the fragment, strips it from the address bar before the first paint, redeems once and opens.
- **aipass: the install ends with the pairing QR** (2026-10-13; aipass building, devpulse landing; DPLAN-0406 / FPLAN-0643). When the phone step's re-probe finds the server answering on this machine's tailnet bind, `aipass install` mints a one-use, five-minute code through @api's pairing door (`mint_pairing("phone", "operate")`) and prints, as the install's last block, `Pair your phone`, the camera line, the QR, its url and the expiry line with the `Later:` command; the guide line moves above it, because the QR is the one thing to act on and the bottom of the screen is where the eye lands when the install stops. On a loopback bind, a silent server, an @api without the door or a `PairingError` (a stated state, never a traceback) nothing is minted and one line, `Then pair your phone: drone @api host-api pair phone --scope operate`, sits above the guide; the token command and receipt-path lines are gone. Round one of the train went red on both OS runs for one test: an assert whose needle was an f-string interpolating `tmp_path` into captured console output. conftest pins `err_console` at 200 columns; the Windows and macOS pytest tmp paths push the line past it, Rich wraps at the last space before the path, and `str(OSError)` renders the filename with `%r`, so on Windows the backslashes are doubled and the line never matches even unwrapped. No row covered it: `literal_path` judges paths handed to a call, `weak_oracle` judges asserts that cannot fail, `conftest_fixtures` only checks the width is pinned. The new standard (tests only, every test file, **advisory**) convicts an `in` / `not in` / `==` / `!=` whose needle interpolates a PATH (`tmp_path`, `tmp_path_factory.mktemp`, an expression rooted at either, a `Path`/`PurePath` call, `str(path)`, `path.parent`) and whose haystack is captured output (`capsys`/`capfd` `readouterr()`, `CliRunner().invoke` or `subprocess.run` output); `.name`, `.stem`, `.suffix` acquit, as does a path compared against `str(exc)` or a returned value. The cure text names WRAP and REPR: assert the words without the path, and the path's `.name`. Red-first on the exact pre-cure specimen; 50 tests; two mutants red from seedgo's seat. Fleet: 9 rows, all real (backup 8 across `test_caller_path.py`, `test_share.py`, `test_versioned_engine.py`; devpulse `test_feedback_compose.py:346`), which is why it lands advisory; it ratchets to gating once those are cured. `.github/scripts/seedgo_audit.py` `EXPECTED_STANDARDS` 82 → 83. ### Added

- **drone: the external-repo door reads gh runs** (2026-10-13; drone building, devpulse landing; FPLAN-0642). Baud's first front-door release was building and no seat could watch it: `run` was home-only. `run list|view <id> [--log|--log-failed]|watch <id> --repo <path>` now go through the door (same admin gate, resolution and ledger, verb `run`): the door reads the repo's origin URL (https, https with a token, scp ssh, ssh://, with or without `.git`) and hands gh its `--repo OWNER/NAME`; a non-GitHub host, a local path or a malformed URL refuses rather than aiming gh at someone else's repo, and the URL is never printed or logged. Reads only: rerun, cancel, delete and download refuse under `--repo`; `-R` beside `--repo` refuses. A `--repo` value that names a directory is the door's, anything else reaches gh untouched, so `run list --repo AIOSAI/baud` still works as gh's own flag (`repo_door.py` 1.3.0, `git_module.py` 1.7.0). Tests +21, four mutants each red; 1604 → 1625; `docs/external_repo_door.md` ten verbs. First use: baud's Release run 38378928388 read from this seat, success in 10m43s.

The gate returns to seedgo alone: every fence leg has landed.

- **drone: `drone @git merge-main` brings main into a diverged dev without a rewrite (owner tier).** Main took six commits dev never saw (the #777 README edit and dependabot bumps). `sync` is fast-forward only and refused, `fix` compared dev with origin/dev only, and `smart-sync` would rebase pushed history, which needs a force push. The fleet never forces. The new verb runs on dev only and fetches. It refuses, touching nothing, on staged changes, a merge in progress, or a file main changes that is uncommitted locally (listed). Then it runs `git merge --no-ff --no-edit origin/main`, and on conflict it aborts and names the files. It never pushes, forces or stashes. `fix`'s help points to it. 12 pins against a temp repo, with 12 mutants killed. First live run: 66d9df16, 6 commits and 5 files, clean.

- **hooks: per-branch cadence overrides, and `"beat": false` for a loader that fires at turn 0 only** (DPLAN-0355; the owner, 2026-09-30 00:54, "test on canary first"; hooks building, devpulse landing). The four grounding loaders (kernel, navmap, identity, branch prompt) fire at turn 0 and every 5th prompt. Injected text never leaves the transcript until compaction, so each periodic fire is a duplicate. The config was global, so trialling "start and post-compact only" on one agent needed a seam. `cadence_config.json` gains `branches.<name>.loaders.<loader>`, taken from the prompt payload's cwd and merged over the global entry for that loader only. `beat: false` fires at turn 0 (new chat, /clear, post-compact) and never on the period. A malformed override logs ERROR and serves global. Decision lines carry `beat=` and `branch=`. Ships inert, with no branch entries. 7 pins (5 red first), 5 in-memory mutants all red, hooks suite 2,268 passed.

- **trigger: a WARNING that repeats for 24 hours belongs to its own branch, not to a manager's inbox** (trigger FPLAN-0637, devpulse go 2026-09-19; trigger owning, devpulse landing 2026-09-27). Repetition into an inbox nobody reads for a day is a pile, not a signal. A WARNING still repeating `warning_age_hours` (24) after it was FIRST seen now leaves the manager's lane: it opens an error-registry row at level `WARNING` (never dispatched, because only medic dispatches and it dispatches off error events) and one upserted mail goes to the branch that LOGGED it, on the same thread key, `auto_execute=False`, naming the registry id and both ways out (`errors resolve` when fixed, `errors suppress` when benign). The owner is the logging branch and never a name parsed out of the message text. The manager gets one roll-up on its own permanent thread (`escalation:rollup`) naming every open row, rewritten when the row list grows and otherwise paced by `rollup_hours`; the repeat digests for those signatures stop. Two refusals to go dark: with no registered owner to mail, and with a `first_seen` this lane cannot parse, the manager digest stays. `apps/handlers/escalation.py` 1.4.0 → 1.5.0, `apps/modules/escalation.py` 1.0.0 → 1.1.0 (status names the lane and counts aged rows, `list` marks them), `config_loader.py` gains both knobs (`0` disables). 11 red-first cases inside existing classes, 16 of 17 mutants red; the survivor is published as equivalent (`_age_hours` returning `0.0` instead of `None` on an unreadable stamp takes the same manager path).

- **seedgo: `logged_fallback`, narrowed and landed, the product pack's second checker** (DPLAN-0354; the owner, 2026-09-25 12:17, asked what it is for and ruled "ok narrow it then land it"; seedgo building, devpulse landing). `silent_catch` acquits any handler that logs; this rule reads what the handler returns. As first measured (any literal default) it was stopped at 656 hits and about 31% precision, a third of the sample being sentinels the callers check. Narrowed, mechanically: convict an `except` that does not raise and ends in `return` of a literal default (a constant, an empty container, or a string built from the exception) only when a `return` outside every handler of the same function returns an equal literal (same type, `False` is not `0`) or a name whose first binding in the function is that literal; logging never acquits. Sentinels pass (`None` beside dict returns, `-1` beside a count), as do raises, generators, `finally` returns, a success return of a call or a parameter, and assign-and-fall-through, each named on the page with its reason; nested functions are judged on their own returns, the bug in the first measurement. Measured over 1,216 product files: 496 hits in 230 files across 16 branches (from 656 / 294 / 17); the 40-hit sample re-run keeps 22, 8 of the 12 true, 5 of the 13 sentinels (the five return the same default from an `if` on another failure path, which a mechanical rule reads as success), 9 of the 12 documented best-effort, so precision moves to about 36% and the remaining false side is the by-design class, which a line bypass with a reason already covers. Of backup's seven rows it catches `drive/tracker.py:114`; `client.py:128` is HELD by seedgo, its `None` a sentinel by the rule as written since `_api_call`'s success path returns a call, while the function one up that misreads it, `get_or_create_backup_folder`, is convicted at 184; `generator.py:143` is not caught, its success path returning no string literal. backup is convicted at 8 lines in 3 files. Red-first on planted specimens for every conviction and every acquittal path, 17/17 mutants killed, one reproduced from devpulse's seat (names not resolved to their first binding: the test file goes red); the model checker, the new checker and `readme_update.py` all 100 on the new rule; `EXPECTED_STANDARDS` 79 → 80; fleet audit +29 s cold; seedgo 5,430 green; the three new files 38/38 on their first checklist run. Displayed averages: ai_mail, aipass, api, devpulse and flow each one point down, the other 13 unchanged, backup 98. Cures are the owner's pacing, not this entry's.

Not landed, the owner's call: `logged_fallback` (an `except` that does not re-raise and returns a literal default in a function with a real success return, logging not acquitting) measured 656 hits in 294 files across 17 branches, 623 of them logging, precision about 31% on a 40-hit hand-classified sample (12 true, 13 a distinct sentinel the callers check, 12 documented best-effort, 3 shape), and it catches 2 of the 7 backup rows it was built for; evidence in `seedgo/docs.local/pp1_logged_fallback_STOPPED.md`.
