### Changed

- **seedgo: `clear_text_secret_logging` 1.3.0 convicts a secret reader's document name in its log message** (CodeQL round eleven on PR #774, 3d317b0a, 2026-10-11; seedgo building, devpulse landing). The alert's path, read from the SARIF, ends at api `handlers/auth/secrets.py:83` where `get_secret` interpolated its `slug` parameter into an f-string, and parameters never seeded the file-local arms. Arm 3 is the one parameter seed, as narrow as the shape allows: in a file that defines a secret lister (`list_secrets`), a def named as a secret reader (`get`/`read`/`load`/`fetch` beside `secret(s)`/`trusted`/`confidential`, no exclusion word, setter verb, identifier or list segment) has document parameters, its required positionals the lister does not take; one of them reaching the log call's message (f-string piece, either side of `%` or `+`, `.format()`, `str()`/`repr()`, string methods) is a row. The lister's own parameters are the namespace the caller chose (`provider`), a `%s` argument is not this arm's row (arms 1 and 2 still judge arguments, the standard stays stricter than CodeQL, whose reach is the message alone), and a rebound parameter, a redaction, `len()` or a short slice acquits. The pre-cure file convicts :83 on `slug` and only there; the cure acquits; fleet 0 rows before and after. Wider variants measured and rejected: every required parameter (one false row, `provider` at :64); the last required parameter ungated (a guess by position). `test_checkers_batch5.py` 1.6.0 adds 24 tests.
- **ci: the Security workflow prints CodeQL's result paths into the codeql job log** (PR #774 round eleven, 45ba6aa0, 2026-10-11). GitHub's code-scanning check annotates only the sink of a clear-text-logging flow (prax `logger.py:135`, the fleet's one log line) and the code-scanning alerts API refuses without an auth drone does not carry, so rounds eight to ten cured sources guessed from a local taint model and the alert's source count never moved. After `analyze` (now `id: analyze`), a step reads the SARIF directory the action reports and prints each result's rule, level, message, sink and every code-flow step as file:line with CodeQL's own step note, locations only, never source text, `if: always()`. `drone @git run view <id> --log` carries it; the first run named the two sources in one read.
- **seedgo: `clear_text_secret_logging` 1.2.0 follows reads and adds on a built value** (CodeQL round ten on PR #774, 6280dd1c, 2026-10-11; seedgo building, devpulse landing). 1.1.0 seeded arm 2 from a secret-named call's result and stopped one hop short of the api chain CodeQL most plausibly reports: `stored = secrets_store.get_secret(...)`, then `records = stored.get("tokens")`, where the taint was lost, then the comprehension, `touch_token`'s loop and `_is_due(record.get("last_used"))` into the `last_used %r` warning. Arm 2 now follows reads of a built value (`.get`/`.pop`/`.setdefault`/`.items`/`.keys`/`.values` carry the receiver on; a `.get` default does not) and adds of one (`.append`/`.extend`/`.add`/`.insert(i, x)` on `x` bind the named list or set; a dict literal or `dict(...)` holding a built value is built). `str`/`repr`/f-strings/`%r` stay rows; `len()`, `type(x).__name__` and a slice of four or fewer stay redactions; seeds are unchanged. Measured over 1,383 product files: the live fleet 0 rows before and after, every sub-arm 0 alone, the pre-cure `tokens.py` convicted at :655 and only there. The .md v1.2 carries the round-ten measurement table; `test_checkers_batch5.py` 1.5.0 adds 20 tests, the pre-cure tokens cut and an appended-keys fixture among them, each red with its arm disabled.
- **seedgo: `clear_text_secret_logging` 1.1.0 seeds arm 2 from a secret-named call's result and follows a value through a same-file helper** (CodeQL round nine on PR #774, 0dd4b54b, 2026-10-10; seedgo building, devpulse landing). The alert left on round eight ran through a shape 1.0.0 could not see: `secret = _get_secret(bot_id)` into a local, handed to `non_secret_keys(secret)` whose return is built by iterating the parameter, the result on a prax warning. - **hooks + drone: deletion, raw git and raw gh belong to the admin seat, and the gates no longer step aside** (DPLAN-0356; the owner, 2026-09-30: "drone rm should only be known by u... raw git should be no access... rm is a big no no"; then "do more research, why is how can it crash... not adding band aids"; then "build this better"). Built by @hooks over four promoted phases and @drone over four legs; landed and verified by devpulse.
  - **Policy:**
    - Every raw delete verb is refused for every seat (rm, rmdir, unlink, shred, find -delete/-exec rm, xargs rm, readable interpreter deletes).
    - `drone rm` is refused unless the caller holds the verified admin grant.
    - Raw git, reads included, is refused off the admin seat, and the refusal names the drone twins.
    - Raw gh is refused, except a body-less `gh api` GET.
    - The rm refusal teaches the owner's cure: rename `(disabled)` and/or move into a local `.archive/` (created if missing); archived files can stay forever.
  - **The investigation found the gates were built to step aside.** Five layers turned any failure into "allow":
    - the bridge import;
    - the trust lookup (an untrusted or edited hooks.json meant ZERO gates: five measured windows, 704 hook calls ungated on 09-07);
    - engine import/raise/timeout;
    - each gate's `except`;
    - subprocess timeouts.

    All three logged gate crashes were half-done in-place edits of live gate code. Raw `gh api` was a full GitHub write path for every seat.
  - **Cures:**
    - Security no longer depends on trust: AIPass gates resolve from AIPASS_HOME, a bad or untrusted config falls back to the gate set, and `hooks_enabled:false` never switches gates off.
    - Gates fail closed: import, raise or timeout blocks with a loud text and an alert.
    - Gate code goes live only through `drone @hooks promote` (lint + compile + full suite + bridge smoke, then an atomic swap).
    - One shell-word reader (`shell_reader.py`) re-reads eval/-c/substitutions and script files.
    - Protected paths (hooks/trust/settings files, `.git/`, the registries) match by inode, and are default-deny for any program not on a read-only list.
    - Identity is the verified grant only; the name lists are gone.
  - **drone:**
    - `drone @git log [n] [path]` and `drone @git blame <file> [-L a,b]` added as read twins.
    - The issue/run/workflow gh pass-throughs split into fleet reads and owner-tier writes, with unknown subcommands refused.
    - `drone rm` judges and reports a symlink where the link lives.
  - **Verified:**
    - Canary live, throwaway files: every delete and git/gh write refused, moves allowed, nothing reached `temp`.
    - Two Opus red teams and a final Fable review, each finding cured by root cause through phase 4.
    - Fleet spot checks (@trigger, @flow): nothing legitimate refused.
  - **Known limit, by the final review's verdict:** text gates teach; enforcement needs the kernel sandbox. hooks' `sandbox.py` exists but is off, and needs deny-write inside writable trees and egress control first.

- **CI: a hung or dead xdist worker ends the job red with the test named, not a 20-minute cancel** (PR #774 rounds five and six, run 38100884450, 2026-10-10). The macOS leg printed `[gw2] node down: Not properly terminated` while memory's `test_search_extras` control test was in flight, xdist spawned a replacement worker, and the session never finished: eight minutes of silence, the job cap, no summary. Reproduced on a Linux seat with one `os._exit(1)` under `-n 2 --dist loadscope`: the default worker restart hangs past 90 s, `--max-worker-restart 0` ends the same run in 6 s naming the test. Two flags on every xdist lane (ci.yml matrix, windows-test.yml, macos-test.yml) and the thread method on coverage: `--timeout-method thread`, because the default signal method cannot interrupt a wait inside C (a lock, a portal join) and the 300 s ceiling never fired; the thread method dumps every thread's stack and exits the worker. `--max-worker-restart 0`, because a worker that dies is a red: the session ends with `worker gwN crashed while running <nodeid>` instead of a replacement that may never finish. Why the worker died is open: no faulthandler dump, so a silent signal or exit; a whole-suite sweep under a Linux probe that refuses any signal to a pid the worker does not own found none (24625 passed), and round six's macOS leg ran green in 9m26s.

- **api: the socket tests wait for the route's detach line before leaving the client context** (the 3.10 hang on PR #774 round three, run 38087470864; merge train PPLAN-0061, 2026-10-10; api building, devpulse landing). `detach_and_wait` returned on the session's hangup, which is the FIRST line of the pump's `finally`, not the route's last. - **hooks: a headless first prompt could split the turn-0 fire, losing the kernel and identity for a dispatched agent's whole run** (DPLAN-0355; found by canary during the cadence trial, root cause by hooks, devpulse ruling and landing 2026-09-30, 28886bf0). The four grounding loaders run as sibling processes and must agree on one turn. The guard that kept them together was the transcript size. A `claude -p` first prompt runs before the transcript exists, so every sibling read 0, and 0 switched the guard off. That left a 2s window measured from the first decision. Now one decision per prompt: a key of sha1(transcript size + prompt text) stored beside the turn, and siblings with the same key share a turn however far apart they run. The 2s window remains only for payloads with neither prompt nor transcript path. Ruled: a real next prompt within 2s now counts. Pins P1 and P2 red first, P3 guard, 2 mutants red, hooks suite 2,271. `cadence.py` landed in one atomic replace because every seat imports it live. Note: 28886bf0 also swept in canary's own test-data edits from the trial's void arm A (note list --json, a span helper rename; canary suite 364 green). Left in for the owner to keep or revert.

## [2026-09-19] — the diet-and-boundary train: the README leaves the startup read fleet-wide and eighteen faces shrink under a 10k cap with `--help` corrected on each, the docs page standard and the eight-section README shape scored by seedgo, the owner's name swept out of everything that ships with a ratchet behind it, memory's runtime write fence and the Vera Studio leak purged, the hooks edit gate reading the registries, the watchdog off the Monitor tool onto a once-wire, and eight citizens' Windows and CI cures (DPLAN-0347 / DPLAN-0348 / DPLAN-0349 / DPLAN-0350 / DPLAN-0351 / FPLAN-0593 / FPLAN-0622 / FPLAN-0628, merged as PR #770, v2.8.11)

### Added

- **seedgo: the docs page standard — one shape for every `docs/*.md` page, scored in audits** (DPLAN-0351 / FPLAN-0628; seedgo building, devpulse landing). The owner, 2026-09-19 09:48: "expecting same structure throughout with guides experience for the agents… its a lot of docs so ill be only random checking." Two independent surveys of the fleet's 179 pages (seedgo's and a devpulse sub-agent's, compared in DPLAN-0351 Notes) agreed on what the corpus already does and refuted the generic-slot skeleton devpulse had drafted: 418 of 437 section headings are single-use topic names and the best pages use them, so the shape is a bare README back-link at the top, one `# Title`, one present-tense purpose paragraph, free topic sections at depth ≤3 with commands by reference, and fixed names only for the optional `## Why it is this way`, `## What is not verified` and `## Related` (the corpus's one shared heading, 56 pages). No history, no cured entries, no defect paragraphs. New in `aipass_standards/`: `docs_page.md`, `docs_page_content.py`, `docs_page_check.py` — five scored checks over `<branch>/docs/*.md` one level deep (one H1 first, a purpose paragraph, heading depth, relative links and images resolve, size at the cap), plus advisory nominate-only lines in `check_branch_info` for the back-link above the purpose, story arms at 7/8 precision or better (`used to`, `previously`, cure verb beside a date), and defect prose (a line linking to a known_issues page is a pointer, excluded). Pages named `known_issues`/`tech_debt` are exempt by name, scored and advisory, until the owner rules on defect registers. The 20k cap did not exist as a key: `context_standards/pack.json` gains `caps["docs/*.md"].max_chars = 20000`, read at call time through `startup_budget_check.docs_page_cap()`, and a test pins that the checker holds no copy. Measured before landing: 160 pages scored, 16 exempt, 15 of 18 branches at 100, 0 dead links, 0 over size; 3 pages red for a missing purpose paragraph (ai_mail S84, api SECURITY, backup tests), each given its one line in this landing so every branch reads Docs_Page 100. Advisory baseline for wave 0: back-link missing on 119 pages in 17 branches, story 69 lines in 15, defect prose 11 lines in 8. 28 cases + 1 content test, 28/28 mutants killed, suite 4357. `EXPECTED_STANDARDS` 48 → 49. Seedgo's own `docs/v5_vs_haiku_shadow_diff.md` moved to its `docs.local/research/`. The scaffold template contract went to spawn; the render-time read waits on spawn. README consistency, measured with no rule added: all 18 READMEs carry Quick Start, Commands and Architecture; the de facto order (Quick Start · What It Does · Live Inventory · How To Reach Me · Commands · Architecture · Documentation · Integration Points) is exact on 6, and an ordered 8-section check would flag 11 of 18 today, the owner's call.

New `context_standards/name_ratchet.py` + `name_ratchet_baseline.json`, wired as gate 2 in `.github/scripts/seedgo_audit.py` between the startup ratchet and the audit, advisory (`NAME_RATCHET_GATES = False`: it prints its red and the job carries on; flipping it is one line). The name is a case-insensitive substring of any line in any `git ls-files` file and of the path itself; the home-path rule covers `/home/<x>`, `/Users/<x>` and `C:\Users\<x>` in `.md` and `*_content.py`, trailing slash optional (the slash-required shape missed 2 of the 5 telegram table cells), placeholders pass (`user`, `me`, `someone`, `<…>`, `{…}`, `$…`, `runner`). - **memory: a runtime fence on every write path — memory never writes outside AIPass, and the leak is purged** (DPLAN-0349; memory owning, devpulse landing). The owner's ruling A, 2026-09-18: an AIPass agent must have no way to write another project's files; reading is allowed, writing never. What happened: one `drone @memory` call from a Vera Studio cwd on 09-17 07:47 persisted that project's registry into `memory_json/known_registries.json`, and every rollover walk after it (six runs, 09-17 07:59 → 09-18 18:57, from writer's and verify's PreCompacts and two auto_process passes) wrote four Vera Studio branches' `.trinity` files, created `.backup/` and `.chroma/` directories in their trees (47 files, 13 dirs) and ingested their entries into the AIPass global Chroma. The fence, new `apps/handlers/write_fence.py`: `outside_root(target, root)` is the pure verdict on RESOLVED paths by containment, not `startswith` (so `/x/aipass_other` is outside `/x/aipass`); `fence_write(target, lane=)` is the one wrapper — an ERROR naming path and root, a `write_fence_refused` op-log row, nothing written. ROOT is the repository root walked from memory's own source file up to `AIPASS_REGISTRY.json`, never cwd; no allow-list, no env override; it fails SHUT when the root resolves to the filesystem root (repo_root's last resort on a wheel with no registry, where `/` would admit every write). Guarded: `write_memory_file` (the gate for extractor, trinity_push, tab_renderer, normalizer and todo_roll), rollover backup and restore, `_recreate_trinity_file`, `normalize_memory_file`, the backlog parent, the branch-local Chroma path, `spawn_pusher._write_json`, `receipt._write`; unfenced on purpose because they write memory's own state inside its own tree: config, op logs, `.ai_central`, `AIPASS_ROOTS.json`, push report, template bump, the processors, the indexer, the lock and the global `.chroma`. No cwd persistence: `persist_registry` and `load_known_registries` are gone, `_find_caller_registries` only walks and drops any out-of-root registry, the watcher now shares the detector's scope (one definition; +3 residents its own walk had missed). `known_registries.json` is retired to `memory_json/.archive/` (17 entries: 7 real, 10 pytest temp paths the old code had appended). Rollover scope 26 → 22, the difference exactly Vera Studio's four branches, the same from both cwds. Purged from the global Chroma: 285 records in 7 `<branch>_<type>` collections (vera 114, verify 121, writer 36, research 14; 09-17: 213, 09-18: 37, and 35 from April in `vera_local` — same species, same certainty), every id verified before deletion, every text present word for word in that branch's own local store, the collections dropped; search returns 47 collections, 0 Vera-branch. NOT removed, other owners' lanes and the owner's call: 204 + 179 Vera sender/recipient rows in ai_mail's sent and deleted collections, 121 `flow_plans` chunks of @vera-owned plans, and @backup's 08-15 snapshots of the store. The meta line "archived to @memory" is stamped only through the fence. The `.backup/` dirs, `rollover_backup_*.json` files and `.chroma/` stores memory created inside Vera Studio are still there for Vera to judge; the full write table with a log line per row is in memory's `docs.local/sub_agent_drops/vera_writes_2026-09-18.md`. Also: `test_declared_roots` tripwire narrowed to the claim that matters (an external citizen declaring core or resident) after Vera's honest `residency: external` stamp fired it. Red first: 22 pins failed before the wiring, 5 mutants red; 16 net new tests inside existing classes. From the devpulse seat: 1895 passed / 2 skipped; the scope pin `test_the_rollover_lane_never_reaches_into_another_repository` green plainly and with a Vera Studio caller cwd; `audit aipass @memory` 100. Open on memory's pad: two hooks `rollover FAILED` lines at the last seconds of two Vera runs, undiagnosed.

- **hooks: the edit gate reads who may edit whose files from the registries — the owner's boundary ruling, encoded** (DPLAN-0349, hooks FPLAN-0627; hooks owning, devpulse landing). The ruling, 2026-09-18: an agent is sandboxed to its own files; devpulse alone edits anywhere; seedgo and spawn edit anything inside AIPass and never beyond it; a manager edits her own project's agents' files and nothing outside her project; reading another's files is allowed, writing never. Measured BEFORE the cure with `edit_gate.handle` on the live tree, three lanes each (Edit, `sed -i`, `python -c`): trust ran downward, so any AIPass seat could write any project nested under it (`projects/baud` allowed for seedgo and for hooks); a manager had no standing on the tool lane (Vera refused on Edit into her own writer agent) and nobody inside a project was fenced on the shell lane (hooks `sed -i` into memory allowed); project-level files (the repo root's `.aipass/`, `.claude/`, README) were anybody's; the three trusted names counted in ANY project — a Vera branch named seedgo was trusted inside Vera; and the registry contents were never read at all, the project root being a `*_REGISTRY.json` filename glob and the branch a `src/<pkg>/<branch>` path shape. AFTER: new `apps/modules/write_ownership.py` 1.0.0 reads the boundary — the caller's project is the nearest ancestor of the session cwd holding a `*_REGISTRY.json` (the same marker as the mail fence, GH #733), a branch is the deepest registry row whose path holds the file, a manager is the row with `owner: true` (spawn's sealed field, never the passport), and seedgo/spawn are trusted only when the caller's registry is `AIPASS_REGISTRY.json`; the path shape survives only as a fallback where a project has no branches table. Crossings are refused in BOTH directions unless the caller is the verified admin seat (the downward-trust pin REVERSED from allow to refuse; the verified-admin twin still passes). Inside a project the shell lane convicts on write grammar only (redirect, `tee`, `sed -i`, `cp`/`mv` destination, `dd of=`) and never on an interpreter's held paths, because a read cannot be told from a write and the ruling allows reading — the residual (python writing another branch of its own project) is stated in `docs/edit_gate.md` rather than hidden. Project-level files now belong to the manager, which includes hooks' own `.aipass/hooks.json`, `.aipass/project_hooks.json` and `.claude/provider_manifest.json` — @hooks no longer edits them and routes them through @devpulse; per-file ownership of project-level paths would need a registry field nobody invented. A `*_REGISTRY.json` that parses as a non-empty table with no `branches` key (flow's `PLAN_REGISTRY.json`) no longer marks a project, so @flow's plan files do not read as a foreign project to @flow. The gate's outer "unexpected error (allowing)" now logs at WARNING, because the fence is a call-time import and a crash turns every fence off for that call. `docs/edit_gate.md` opens with what the gate cannot see: a write a service makes from Python — a drone verb, @memory's rollover, any `python -m` door — never passes through it, so every service that writes files must carry its own fence (memory's is the first, landing separately). Also: `tests/conftest.py` 2.2.0 isolates the fleet-shared `src/aipass/.diagnostics_state.json` (autouse), because every live seat's auto_fix writes it and a test Editing a `.py` picked up another seat's open import error and went red — very likely hooks' long-standing todo 49 flake. `edit_gate.py` 1.16.0 (1,495 → 1,464 lines), `bash_writes.py` 1.6.0, three test files. 19 new cases plus 1 reversed, all inside existing classes, 11 red before the cure; 12 mutants on a `/tmp` copy of the package, all killed. The gate reads source, so this was live fleet-wide from the working tree the moment it landed — expect first refusals from citizens that wrote project-level files or used `sed` into another branch.

- **hooks: grounding fails loud and small, every injection is on a ledger, a mail body is data, and two proposed cures refused on numbers** (DPLAN-0347 / FPLAN-0593 Phase 5, hooks FPLAN-0620; hooks owning, devpulse landing). **Degraded fail mode** (`cadence.py` 2.6.0): when turns cannot be counted, cadence used to force turn 0, which fires every loader (21,383 chars a prompt); now only `DEGRADED_LOADERS` fire (the kernel plus the alert and mail channels, 3,750 chars) and navmap, branch and identity are withheld, not replaced, with one WARNING per degraded turn. Grounding a seat was promised and did not get (a stamped tree with no kernel, a branch with no prompt, a loader that raises) opens the kernel block and part 1 of the post-compact re-ground with a `[GROUNDING DEGRADED …]` banner naming what was carried, what is missing and why; a tree that promises nothing stays silent (`grounding_content.py` 1.3.0, `tier0_kernel.py` 1.2.0, `post_compact_regrounding.py` 2.1.0). **Injection ledger** (`apps/modules/injection_ledger.py` + `apps/handlers/config/ledger_store.py`, both 1.0.0; `engine.py` 1.7.0): one JSONL line per dispatch that reached the model, per hook chars (UTF-16) and a short sha, grouped on cadence's turn token because parallel siblings can read a lagging turn number. Warn-only; it warns on an injection over the 10,000 persist line and on a record it could not write. `drone @hooks ledger` reads the caller's own session: the first bare read printed a neighbour's turns, because every citizen runs a live session. **Mail-body gate** (`git_gate.py` 1.1.0, `bash_writes.py` 1.5.0): the gate scans `code_text()`, which blanks a heredoc body whose consumer only reads it and hands back a shell's own program text tokenized, so prose quoting a write-shaped line no longer refuses a reply and `bash -c "<write>"` is no longer read as an empty quoted argument. A first version appended every interpreter's program and refused a read-only `awk` filter on a real turn; it is now shells only (bash, sh, zsh), and awk, perl and python programs read as they did before. **Template and cap message** (feedback c273274e): `.aipass/project_hooks.json` runs `pre_edit_gate` on Bash too, so new projects get the scripted-write fence and the memory shell refusal. That refusal names `drone @memory` and measured caps only where @memory imports (`edit_gate.py` 1.15.0). **Memory file writes:** an Edit or Write that would leave a `.trinity` file unparseable is refused (it was allowed through a catch-all), and an edit that repairs a broken file is allowed with a WARNING. The tripwire charges only a file that does not measure clean. A clean change, even to the seat's own file, is reported as a question and logged at INFO, because another seat's compaction rolls this seat's `local.json` mid-call. **MagicMock leak:** `test_log_write_failure_does_not_crash` handed a bare Mock path to `append_jsonl`, whose mkdir left `MagicMock/LOG_FILE/` in the branch root from 2026-07-10. The test now uses a tmp path, and a tree-level test fails if any mock-named directory appears in the branch root. The leaked directory went through `drone rm`. **Refused, with the numbers:** *cadence-by-default*, fenced as a restatement: DPLAN-0347 named 4 opt-outs, but this repo's 13 UserPromptSubmit entries need 9. A default lives in the engine every stamped project runs, and two projects carry `temporal` and `context_gauge` with no opt-out key, so those two would drop from every turn to every fifth. An 11-turn trace per handler is identical before and after this phase's other rows. *Tripwire grace-then-re-stat*: every memory writer is atomic, and the retained logs (09-12 → 09-16) held 2 real breakages, open 9 s and 8 s. A grace long enough to hide the false alarms hides those too, so the cure landed at the source instead (the unparseable-edit refusal above). `edit_gate.py` is at 1,495 lines, under the 1,500 split line only after its docstrings moved to `docs/`, and needs a real split. Measured: 2080 passed / 2 skipped from both the branch and the repo root, `audit aipass @hooks` 100, checklist 34/34 on every changed source, branch prompt 8,824 of 9,000.

- **memory: the todo backlog trims by moving deeper, never by deleting** (DPLAN-0347 / FPLAN-0593 Phase 5; memory owning, devpulse landing). The per-agent backlog grew forever and nothing trimmed it — seedgo's was already at 72 records. The trim is now a move: records past `rollover.backlog.max_records` (100, in `memory.config.json`) go to a sibling `backlog.archive.json` under the same order-of-operations contract the roll already uses — append to the archive, atomic replace, read back and compare every record, and only then shorten the backlog, so a record may sit in both files for an instant and never in neither. Nothing is dropped, because the backlog is the only copy of a rolled todo and is never vectorised: a trim that deleted would delete the last copy of open work. It hangs off `append_to_backlog`, the one choke point both the roll and the push cross, so it fires when the file grows rather than on a sweep nobody runs, and a failed trim never fails the append. No usable ceiling means NO trim, never a trim to zero — the failure mode is "the file stays long", never "the last copy is gone". `high_water` is not lowered, so no number is re-issued. Two consequences stated rather than discovered later: an archived record is not reachable by `todo restore`, which reads the backlog only, and the archive grows forever by design. Also landed: `entry_limits.draft_percent` is a config key (the module constant is gone and a pin keeps it gone), and `apps/modules/limits.py` is the modules gateway that was missing — @hooks and @seedgo both reached into the handler by dotted path because there was no door, and seedgo's mirrored copy can now retire.

- **seedgo: the per-file startup ratchet, and `host_leak` — the greeting can no longer grow back** (DPLAN-0347 / FPLAN-0593 Phase 5; seedgo owning, devpulse landing). `startup_ratchet.py` 1.0.0 in the context pack, wired into the existing `seedgo-audit` CI job ahead of the audit loop (`.github/scripts/seedgo_audit.py`, no new step, no `ci.yml` change): CI goes red when a branch's `README.md` or `.aipass/aipass_local_prompt.md` grows past its cap. Chars as `wc -m` counts them, never lines or tokens; a file AT its cap passes, over is `>`. Caps are READ from their owner at run time and no cap number exists in the gate — pinned by an AST walk asserting no `{10000, 9000, 6000, 15000, 25000, 600}` literal in either file: README 10,000 from seedgo's own `context_standards/pack.json`, prompt 9,000 from hooks' `BRANCH_CHAR_BUDGET`. Every failure line names four things — file, measured, cap, owning branch (`… measured 10,316 chars, cap 10,000 chars (OVER by 316), owner @seedgo (context_standards/pack.json → caps["README.md"].max_chars)`) — because a red that does not say who owns the file costs a seat a round trip; an unreadable owner cap fails loudly naming the owner and the exception, never falling back to a remembered number. Scope is deliberately today's measured pair: `.trinity` and the dashboard are machine-local and gitignored so CI cannot see them, and `docs/` is measured but not gated while the fleet still holds pages that predate the 20,000 rule. Proven both ways before landing: green across 18 branches / 36 gated files on head (tightest hooks README 9,116 and aipass prompt 8,968), and red against a copied fixture tree (grown hooks README 10,316 and aipass prompt 9,068 both failing, a README set to exactly 10,000 passing), the fixture removed and the live tree never grown. 28 pins in two existing test files, 28/28 mutants killed with sha256 restore proof. Also `host_leak` 1.0.0, the v5 pack's 16th rule, advisory and nominate-only (`SCORED = False`): a test that fakes a platform AND weaves a host path into composed text beside a literal — the Windows CI red where a test faked macOS, built its fake `lsof` line out of `tmp_path`, and the POSIX-only parser could not read the line the test itself wrote. The broad arms were measured and REFUSED with numbers: "fakes a platform + any host value" is 23 rows fleet-wide, all 23 hand-read, 0 real; "host path into composed text" alone is 223 rows; the shipped pair-shape is 0 rows on the fleet today, catches the pre-cure unit, and leaves its cured sibling clean. The other CI red's shape (a fixture depending on module-level state another test warms) was measured and refused too: 393 production module-level containers, 160 unseeded reads, 8 with a sibling seeder, 8 of 8 false, 0 recall on the defect it was built for — the refusal and its numbers are written into `host_leak.md` so nobody re-derives it. 22/22 mutants killed; 4 of them found real defects in the rule's own code first.

- **memory: the closed field shape, `lint fields` and the keep-count ceiling** (DPLAN-0347 / FPLAN-0593 Phase 1, thread 16; memory owning, devpulse landing). Every field of a `.trinity` entry is now capped, not just one: `memory.config.json` publishes `entry_limits.entry_types.<type>.fields` as `{type, required, max_chars, max_items}` — sessions `status` 40, key_learnings `key` 80, `tags` 10 items / 120 joined, todos `priority` 10, `date` 10 everywhere (the one cap the room did not name: a closed shape with an uncapped string is not closed; measured max is 10 on all 803 entries across 22 branches); `summary` / `value` / `task` / `note` unchanged — plus `file_budgets` (local 25,000, observations 15,000, passport 6,000 file / 600 per string, SIZE only: spawn owns the passport schema). Why: `todos.status` was the uncapped hole that grew devpulse's local.json to 64,657 chars (S464); the cap on one field per type left every other string free to become the next one. `changed_entries` returns two new reasons in the published six-key shape plus `field` and `units`: `unknown_field` (the field may not exist) and `field_over_cap` (chars or items); `check_file_budget` adds `file_over_budget` for the passport row; `missing_field` and `unmeasurable` reused. Field violations use a stricter identity than the canonical cap — an entry is carried only when the whole dict is in `before`, because a write that edits only `status` leaves the summary byte-identical and the text test would wave through exactly the edit this shape exists to catch. `drone @memory lint fields [@branch]` lists every string field by chars (max / p95 / n against its cap, passport row included) and flags what is outside the shape; fleet run 22 branches, 2,938 measurements, 5 outside — devpulse `status` 917 and 154, `key` 83, aipass `identity.purpose` 869, devpulse `identity.class_extension` 674 — all legal until touched. The keep-count ceiling: `config set` and `set-default` refuse, and load clamps, a count whose worst-case file (every entry at every cap, serialized) busts its budget — sessions 16, key_learnings 17, todos 14, observations 19 at today's co-tenants, the refusal naming the budget and the other two tenants; no shipped default clamps (15 ≤ 16, 15 ≤ 17, 10 ≤ 14, 15 ≤ 19), config md5 identical before and after a refused set. `trinity_push` derives its entry shape from the config — `ENTRY_RULES` is gone, seedgo's `trinity_groups` mirror is the last copy and goes in Phase 2. `todo restore` of a non-canonical backlog entry is now a refused write that leaves both files as found (the backlog contract forbids reshaping); the text stays readable via `todo backlog`. Files: `memory.config.json`; `entry_limits` 1.11.0, `config_loader` 1.5.0, `budget` 1.0.0 (new), `lint_handler` 1.3.0, `memory_files` 1.4.0, `trinity_push` 1.4.0, `tab_renderer` 1.6.0, `lint` 1.2.0, `rollover` 0.8.0 (1,498 lines against seedgo's 1,500 — the next addition needs a split). ~70 pins in six existing test files, mutants run and restored on seven handlers; 1808 passed in CI shape (`-n auto --dist loadscope`) and at `-n 3`; seedgo audit @memory 100. Found while building: the non-entry structure figures in DPLAN-0347 (local.json 3,254 / observations 2,068) were memory's own measurement and inflated by the indent method; correct is ~1,629 / ~1,306; the conservative 3,500 / 2,500 allowance stands, which is why sessions has one slot of headroom (16 against 15).

- **ai_mail: a dispatch wake refreshes the recipient's dashboard before the session spawns** (DPLAN-0347 / FPLAN-0593 Phase 3, ai_mail FPLAN-0599; ai_mail owning, devpulse landing). `wake.py` 3.2.0 calls `refresh_recipient_dashboard` (new handler `wake_dashboard.py` 1.0.0, which calls prax's `refresh_single_dashboard`) for the RECIPIENT branch at the one point past every gate and above all three spawn lanes (tmux manager, systemd scope, detached Popen), so the agent's first status glance is written before the process that reads it exists. Why: `DASHBOARD.local.json` is the single glance the startup protocol reads and nothing refreshed it on the way in — a woken agent read whatever its own last session left behind, "0 unread" while the dispatch that woke it sat in the inbox (canary's card was 3 h 29 m stale at the moment of the probe). One branch, never the fleet: `refresh_all_dashboards` walks 18 and the recipient is one of them. FAIL-OPEN, and that is the one exemption from failing honestly in this file — an import that cannot resolve, a raise, an error status prax RETURNED rather than raised, or a refresh still running at `DASHBOARD_REFRESH_TIMEOUT` (5.0 s against a measured 0.85–0.98 s) each record a prax WARNING naming the branch and a `warn` step, and the spawn goes ahead: a stale dashboard costs the woken agent one refresh, a dead wake costs the dispatch. The bound needs a thread (`signal.alarm` is POSIX-only and main-thread-only; this runs under the daemon as often as under a terminal), `daemon=True` so an overrun cannot hold the process open either. The import is local and through prax's module door (`aipass.prax.apps.modules.dashboard`), never the handler — a module-level import would make a broken prax dashboard an ImportError at ai_mail import time, which is exactly the trade the fail-open exists to refuse. Measured live (probe wake at @canary, 2026-09-15 17:28, haiku): refresh 0.33 s, `last_updated` 13:59:18 → 17:28:56.087, the register row opened 58 ms later at 17:28:56.145, the agent's first turn ~1.5 s after that (run completed 17:29:14 after 16.5 s) — the card is written before the agent exists, zero agent tokens. Files: `apps/handlers/dispatch/wake_dashboard.py` 1.0.0 (new — the helper went to its own file because `wake.py` measured 1,554 lines with it inline, over seedgo's 1,500; `wake.py` imports it under its old private alias, so every pin and stub keeps the name it had), `apps/handlers/dispatch/wake.py` 3.2.0 (1,464 lines), `test_wake.py` +6 pins in the existing file (red first: 6/6 red on the missing helper before the build). 6/6 mutants red, including "refresh below the tmux lane" and "fleet refresh instead"; 1498 passed both rootdirs; seedgo 34/34 on `wake.py` and 23/23 on the test file — it caught two of my own rows first, a silent catch in the worker (now logged in the thread that sees it, so the record exists even when the join times out) and a `/tmp` literal in a pre-existing darwin test.

- **drone: `drone @git commit` refuses an essay in the subject line** (DPLAN-0347 / FPLAN-0593 Phase 3, drone FPLAN-0600; drone owning, devpulse landing). `commit_handler.py` 1.2.0: a commit whose first line exceeds prax's `SUBJECT_CAP` (120) is refused with exit 1 — nothing staged, nothing committed — and the refusal text is the rule itself: subject under ~80 chars in `type(scope): what` form, blank line, the why in the body at any length; the refusal shows the offending length and the cap. Why: eight recent commits carried 1.3–4 KB single-line subjects with no body, and `git log --oneline`, the dashboard's `last_commit_msg` and the PR list all render the subject, so every glance carried the whole paragraph; prax capped the display this morning, but the door is where the shape belongs. The number is imported from `aipass.prax.apps.modules.dashboard`, never copied — a commit subject and a plan subject are the same glance — and the pin reads the import line out of the source, because `is`-identity on a small int passes even when 120 is hand-copied (that mutant survived until the pin changed). The gate runs first in `commit_changes()`: above repo resolution, above staging, above `--all`'s ruff and pytest lane (pinned: zero `subprocess.run` calls on a refusal), and the `--repo` external door inherits it. Second door found and capped: `pr_handler.py` 1.1.0's `create_pr` composes `feat(<branch>): <description>` and commits it, so it measures before `acquire_lock` — a refusal holding the repo-wide lock would block every citizen while it teaches. Leading blank lines are stripped before line 1 is measured, as git's own cleanup does. `git_module.py` 1.4.0 names the cap in `git commit --help` and rejoins `repo_door` to the handler import block (seedgo's dead_code 1.1.0 landed). Proven live from the devpulse seat: a 183-char subject refused, exit 1, HEAD unchanged. 11 tests in two existing files, 9/9 mutants red; drone suite 1370 passed both rootdirs; seedgo audit @drone 100. README: new section on the cap, Known Issues bullet closed.
- **aipass: the provider manifest carries a settings scalar, and doctor names the gap** (DPLAN-0347 / FPLAN-0593 Phase 3, aipass FPLAN-0601; aipass owning, devpulse landing). `.claude/provider_manifest.json` 1.1.0 gains `cli.claude.settings`, a map of TOP-LEVEL personal-settings keys and the values AIPass wants — first entry `includeGitInstructions: false`; the manifest is the single source and no default for the key exists in code. `provider_wire.py` 1.1.0 merges it through the verb that already writes hooks (`auto_wire_provider`, same dated backup, same atomic write): a key the file does not have is set, a key the user set to a DIFFERENT value is reported and left alone ("Kept your includeGitInstructions=true (manifest wants false) — your value wins, nothing overwritten"), and no other key in the file is read or written; scalars only (a nested block typed into the slot is dropped with a WARNING), with `false` and `0` kept distinct so a 0 cannot read as a satisfied `false`. `_doctor_wire.py` 1.1.0 / `doctor.py` 1.1.0 give `aipass doctor` one diff row per manifest key — `manifest wants false, provider has MISSING` / `… provider has true` — each carrying the exact cure (`Run: aipass doctor --fix`; for a conflict, the line that says the human value stands and names what to drop first), and the interactive/`--fix` gate now reads the settable gaps instead of the glyphs, so a value the user set never makes doctor offer to wire over it. Why: `includeGitInstructions` is effective ONLY in the personal settings file (the project copy is ignored, S470; personal proven effective, S471), Claude Code injects a ~4k-char gitStatus block every session without it, and no installer wrote the key while the manifest had no slot for a scalar — doctor could not even see the gap, so a fresh clone regressed ~4k tokens silently and DPLAN-0346's DONE bullet on this was wrong. Found while building: the interactive run calls the manifest check twice and the replace filter stripped only the fixed labels, so a settings row — labelled with the manifest KEY — printed twice; `merge_manifest_rows` now replaces every label the fresh pass carries. Proven on a scratch HOME end to end (MISSING named with the cure → the wire verb sets it → doctor reads it as wanted → a hand-set `true` reported with zero writes, the seeded `model` key untouched); the live `~/.claude/settings.json` was never opened for write. 13 pins in two existing test files, 6/6 mutants red, 1114 passed; seedgo 34/34 on all three sources and audit @aipass 100 — it caught a module doing `json.loads` on the settings file first (now `json_handler.read_json`). Also closed: `test_doctor.py` stubs the sandbox checker so the suite no longer runs real `npm` (3 logs per run in `~/.npm/_logs` → 0). Both wire doors now merge the slot: `refresh_provider_hooks` at install (setup.sh's only wire door, `provider_wire.py` 1.2.0) and `auto_wire_provider` in-process, so a fresh clone gets `includeGitInstructions` at install rather than at the first `aipass doctor --fix` — proven on a scratch HOME through setup.sh's heredoc verbatim, including an upgrade re-run that reports a hand-set `true` and leaves it.
- **aipass: the test-write policy resolves the project root, not bare cwd** (DPLAN-0347 / FPLAN-0593 Phase 3 follow-up). `init_flow.py` 1.3.0: `_get_test_write_policy_path` resolves `find_registry()` and stamps at `<registry root>/.aipass/test_write_policy.json`, falling back to cwd only when no registry exists (a fresh install, where cwd IS the project root). Why: bare `Path.cwd()` meant any suite run from a branch directory created a SECOND policy — `src/aipass/aipass/.aipass/test_write_policy.json`, one byte off the root file (json_handler writes no trailing newline) — and @hooks' gate walks UP, so the nearest copy silently outranks the fleet's live ruling. Second occurrence of the same door (DPLAN-0337 R5 removed the first). Reproduced from an empty tmp cwd, cured, re-measured: the same run now leaves the directory empty. `test_init_flow.py` 1.1.0 adds an autouse floor pointing the policy into tmp_path for the whole file plus three pins; 2/2 mutants red. The stray copy could not be `drone rm`'d (`.aipass/` is a hard carve-out with no override); on Patrick's word it was moved to aipass's untracked `.archive/` with a dated stray suffix.
- **aipass: the structure scanner reads project-registry residency** (DPLAN-0347 / FPLAN-0593 Phase 3 follow-up). `structure_scanner.py` 1.1.0 adds `resident_root()`: the first ancestor holding a `*_REGISTRY.json` that LISTS the agent (by name, case-insensitive, or by a path row resolving to its directory) is that agent's home, and `check_placement` measures each agent — and reads package names — against that home, falling back to the scan root. Why: a citizen of a project under `projects/` legitimately lives outside the framework's `src/`, and measuring it against the framework root produced one WARNING per scan forever — @trigger escalated `captured_structure_scanner` four times in an hour, 28 lifetime since 2026-08-28, and the real count was 4 per scan (aipass_site, baud, earmark, finch). Measured: 4 WARNING lines on the last pre-fix scan, zero on the two after, all four resolving to their own project roots. Residency is a listing, not adjacency: a registry listing someone else is no cover, and an unregistered citizen outside `src/` is still flagged (both pinned). 5 pins in `test_structure_scan.py` 1.1.0, 2/2 mutants red. aipass suite 1124 passed, audit 100.
- **spawn: the birth contract — a newborn starts inside every owner's cap, and `update` reports `.md` drift instead of falling through it in silence** (DPLAN-0347 / FPLAN-0593 Phase 3, spawn FPLAN-0602; spawn owning, devpulse landing). Template split: `templates/citizen/README.md` is the face (purpose, `drone @self` for the live inventory, a `docs/` index; the command list and the Three-Layer block are gone), `.aipass/aipass_local_prompt.md` is breadcrumbs under a contract comment naming hooks' `BRANCH_CHAR_BUDGET` as the cap's owner, and the `docs/README.md` stub carries the per-module convention (one file per module or handler group, under 20,000 chars, indexed from the README). Newborn startup footprint 11,277 → 9,369 chars (README 2,089 → 1,711, prompt 4,153 → 2,376); `drone @seedgo audit context` on a scratch newborn shows no column over cap. `update_ops.py` 2.2.0 adds `_md_state()`: every existing `.md` is compared against the rendered template and answered as matches / differs / unreadable with a line per file in the preview (`update.py` 1.2.0) — never a write, because the README diet is owner judgment (DPLAN-0199); measured on canary as 7 differ, 16 match. `test_birth_receipt.py` 1.1.0 pins the newborn under every cap, the passport per-string cap, the dashboard rendered at birth from the template (no call to flow or prax), and caps-never-copied — every cap is read from its owner at assert time (seedgo `pack.json`, hooks `BRANCH_CHAR_BUDGET`, memory `file_budgets`, prax `DASHBOARD_CHAR_BUDGET`) and a hand-copied literal fails the suite. `test_update.py` 1.2.0 pins the `.md` arm as read-only. Found on the way: the hooks edit gate already refuses a 643-char passport principle in the template itself — the per-string defect cannot be authored through the Edit door at all.
- **seedgo: the `startup_budget` pack — the greeting is a measured number, not a percentage somebody notices** (DPLAN-0347 / FPLAN-0593 Phase 2, seedgo FPLAN-0598; seedgo owning, devpulse landing). `drone @seedgo audit context [@branch]` renders the fleet table: one row per branch, README / prompt / local / observations / passport / dashboard in chars (`wc -m`, never bytes or tokens) against each layer's cap, over-cap marked. Branch-level, ADVISORY (gates nothing; the per-file CI ratchet is Phase 5). Caps are read from their owner at call time, never copied: README 10,000 from `context_standards/pack.json` (Patrick 16:02 — the one number seedgo owns, in JSON so the ratchet can read it without importing Python), prompt 9,000 from hooks' `BRANCH_CHAR_BUDGET`, dashboard 6,000 from prax's `DASHBOARD_CHAR_BUDGET`, `.trinity` 25k / 15k / 6k + 600 from `memory.config.json entry_limits.file_budgets`; an unreadable owner is an ERROR row, never a default; `external_inputs()` declares memory's config so the incremental cache cannot serve a stale row after a cap moves. The pins are behavioural, not identity — monkeypatch hooks' or prax's constant and the row must move, so a hand-copied literal goes red (CPython interns small ints, so `is` cannot tell an import from a copy; drone hit the same today). Measured on the fleet (final run): 17 of 18 READMEs over 10,000 — memory 95,704, api 92,978, ai_mail 85,110, prax 77,953, drone 69,040, hooks 68,126, daemon 62,147, trigger 57,729, flow 46,285, spawn 36,300, seedgo 35,464, skills 30,490, backup 25,700, aipass 23,660, commons 22,849, cli 15,493, canary 13,370; devpulse 4,742 the only one under — every prompt under 9,000 (hooks 7,960 highest), every `.trinity` file under budget, two passports over the 600-char per-string cap (aipass `identity.purpose` 869, devpulse `identity.class_extension` 674). Startup_Budget fleet average 71%, every branch still Overall 100: advisory working. Files: `context_standards/{pack.json, startup_budget_check.py 1.0.0, startup_budget_content.py 1.0.0, startup_budget.md}`; `audit_display.py` 1.2.0 gained one generic fleet-table arm (returns early when no checker publishes a `fleet_row`, so other packs' output is byte-identical); one name-scoped bypass for `measure_corpus` (called only through pack.json's `measured_by` string, which `unused_function` cannot see). 22 new test functions in existing files, 23/23 mutants red; seedgo suite 4188 passed from the repo root. Deviation, ruled acceptable: seedgo reads memory's config key directly rather than importing memory's handler (a cross-branch handler import fails its own encapsulation standard and memory publishes no modules gateway for these) — a one-line memory gateway is a Phase 5 row.

### Changed

- **the fleet's docs pages take the standard's shape: a back-link on every page, the move stamps gone, the defect registers retired** (DPLAN-0351 wave 0; devpulse landing, eight sub-agents). Two rulings from the owner this morning. On the 16 `docs/known_issues.md` / `docs/tech_debt.md` pages (born in the 09-15 README diet, defect paragraphs by definition, cured entries still standing on 13 of them): "retire them. unless, tech depth and maintenance nightmare is what they are move to docs.local." So each moved, unchanged, into its branch's untracked `docs.local/`, and the 59 links to them in 52 tracked pages went: index rows deleted, Related bullets deleted, prose pointers trimmed to the claim they carried (drone's `testing.md` lost a Related heading that had held only that bullet). Open defects live on pads and in plans from here; a stranger sees the CHANGELOG and a module page's "What is not verified". Then, on "can haiku subagents add the back link? all files": 110 pages in 16 branches got `[<- Back to the README](../README.md)` as their first line, measured against the checker's own rule (a README link above the purpose paragraph), the 67 "Moved out of README.md on 2026-09-15 (DPLAN-0347…)" provenance stamps went as history the CHANGELOG already carries, and daemon's ten below-the-purpose links moved up. After the wave the back-link advisory reads 8 of 160 pages: spawn's six (spawn awake on its scaffold build, its own pass follows) and canary's two live edits. Audit 100 on all 15 branches touched, Docs_Page and Readme rows included, every `docs/*.md` still reachable from its README. - **kernel: the cross-branch rule says what it is about — an AI editing another AI's files — and names services as the framework running** (DPLAN-0349; the owner's words 2026-09-18 23:46, added on his go at 23:57). The kernel's line was `No cross-branch file edits. Issue in another agent's code → mail the owner.` and nothing anywhere in the injected prompts distinguished an agent's edit from a service's write. So when a log showed @memory's rollover code writing another project's `.trinity` files, the only rule a seat had matched it and the seat called it a breach — which sent a night into a boundary program over service doors that the owner then pulled back: AIPass agents offer services (mail, prax logs and dashboards, the daemon's scheduled wakes, rollover) and projects import those services to use them; a service writing into the project it serves is how AIPass runs, not an agent crossing a line. The line now carries that distinction in one sentence each way. Kernel measured 3,034 → 3,251 chars with its comment block (the 2,000 target is the open step-5 ruling in FPLAN-0622).

Both halves pinned (`TestEscapeExport`, 11 cases; two mutants each failed exactly their own cases). `docs/rich_markup.md` carries the rule — escape the data, do not disarm the line — and the split table; cli's own `--help` had the case (its example lost its `[bold]` tags) and is hand-escaped. - **seedgo: the last mirrored number retires — the draft percent is READ from `memory.config.json`, never carried** (DPLAN-0347 / FPLAN-0593 Phase 5 follow-up; seedgo owning, devpulse landing). `trinity_groups.py` 1.2.0 → 1.3.0. `_DRAFT_PERCENT = 80` existed only because @memory published the percent as a module constant with no key to read; it publishes `entry_limits.draft_percent` now, so the number comes out of the same config dict as the caps and the entry shape — no import, no second source, nothing new for the audit cache to watch. **Never assumed:** a config that publishes no usable percent (absent, not an int, outside 1–100) gets no guessed one — the tab renders `draft to <entry_limits.draft_percent unpublished>` and the Meta lines group refuses whole, naming the key and its owner. @memory's own loader narrows to its regeneration seed instead, which is its call about what it writes, but a checker that quietly agreed with a seed would be scoring files against a number nobody published. - **memory: `rollover.py` split at 1,498 lines, two under the hard fail, and `todo restore` now names the field it refuses** (DPLAN-0347 / FPLAN-0593 Phase 5; memory owning, devpulse landing). The module sat two lines under seedgo's 1,500-line hard fail, so the next real edit would have failed the audit — the split came before the next feature rather than after it. 1,498 → 899: the config verbs to `apps/modules/rollover_config.py`, the shared JSON emitter to `apps/modules/rollover_json.py`, moved code being the code that was there, with `rollover.py` re-exporting every name so `rollover.<name>` still resolves. It reports and never repairs, pinned as such, so a later restore cannot quietly pre-answer the open ruling on legacy pads. **Found while splitting, and the same species as both of tonight's CI reds:** each rollover test harness imported the real module one line BELOW its cli stand-in, so the module's console bound to a mock and stayed cached past teardown, and 191 tests then printed nothing while still passing. Serial order only — `loadscope` puts the two files on different workers, so no CI run has ever seen it. Cured in both harnesses with the reason written above the line. **Left at 99% here, and that was wrong — cured in the commit below.** `rollover_config.py` was parked with a named finding rather than resolved, on the reasoning that a bypass to restore a number was worse than an honest 99%. That reasoning never checked the gate: the `seedgo-audit` job has hard-failed any branch under 100% since 2026-06-05, so the decision did not park the finding, it turned CI red. The follow-up bullet has the cure and the corrected diagnosis.

- **seedgo: Rich_Markup follows the literal to the print site** (DPLAN-0347 / FPLAN-0593 Phase 5; seedgo owning, devpulse landing). `rich_markup_check.py` 2.0.0 (+ `rich_markup_content.py` 2.0.0 and a `rich_markup.md` that did not exist) reads two hops the old checker could not: a module-level literal printed by name elsewhere in the file, and a function whose returned literals are printed at a call site in the same file, concatenation read through at both levels. Why: the checker read the PRINT SITE only, so a help page assembled as a returned literal in one module and printed by a caller scored 100 while eating its own placeholders — reproduced red-first by running the transcribed 1.0.0 scan against the uncured file (0 violations, score 100) and the new one (score 0, 29 eaten tokens: `[args]`, `[global]`, `[count]`, `[path]`, `[owner]`, …), with the cured file scoring 100 under both. Second family, from the fleet rule the cli branch published tonight (escape the data, do not disarm the line): a `markup=False` call whose literal carries a tag Rich would have styled is now flagged, because it prints the tags, as is a hand-escape stranded under `markup=False`. The limits are stated rather than papered over, each with its own silence pin: one file, one hop, no chaining, no locals/`join`/`%`/indexed access, no Rich renderable wrappers, no names bound twice — measured as 264 of 5,570 print-site arguments (4.7%) staying unreadable, and a deliberately over-generous cross-file probe finding 0 eaten tokens fleet-wide, which is why call-following was refused. Hand-escaping at a normal print site is NOT flagged: for a styled page that must also show a literal placeholder there is no other spelling, so the demotion lives in the guidance, not in a red. Fleet before/after: 17 branches unmoved at 100, one real finding on one file in one branch (a module-level help constant whose `[opts]` the terminal eats, verified through a capture console), 0 false positives; not cured here — the file is not this branch's. 23 new pins asserted against rendered bytes from a real Console, 84 passing in the existing test file, 24/24 mutants killed with sha256 restore proof.

- **api: an upload whose generated name collides no longer deletes the earlier upload** (api owning, its todo 13; devpulse landing). `_write_stream` opens the destination with `O_EXCL`, and on any `OSError` it discarded the destination — including the case where the create itself was refused because the name was already taken, which deleted the EARLIER file, the silent loss `O_EXCL` exists to prevent. Now a `created` flag is set only after the create succeeds and the discard runs only for a file this write made. Two cases in the existing class, red first: a collision (the name generator patched to the first upload's name) raises `UploadUnavailable`, the earlier bytes are intact and the folder holds one file; a body that dies mid-write after the create still leaves no partial. Four mutants killed (discard unconditional, never discard, flag set before the create, flag never set). The test file's shebang went with it. 56 passed in the file, 1714 from the branch, `audit aipass @api` 100. Two attribution swaps from DPLAN-0350 wave 3 ride in the same two files.

Seedgo reconstructed the pre-cure lines in its own scratch and measured the AST: the haystack (`" ".join(str(call) for call in ….call_args_list)`) WAS read as repr text, across the two statements, and `.resolve()` kept a path a path — the miss was the needles. `home, foreign = self._fenced_world(tmp_path, monkeypatch)` bound both to a helper's return, which the pass classified as None; a path returned from a helper was a known blind spot named in the detector's own docstring, and it bit on the first new occurrence. `mock_repr_path.py` 1.1.0 reads same-module helper returns: a tuple return binds element by element, a helper whose returns disagree in kind stays opaque, and only `self.`/`cls.`/`ClassName.`/bare-name calls resolve — 238 helpers now read fleet-wide. The other direction checked too: 105 path needles into unreadable haystacks, 9 inside functions touching `call_args`, all 9 hand-read and reading the real args — 0 hidden reprs. - **drone: the PR lock answers "blocked" on a Windows PermissionError instead of escaping** (drone owning, devpulse landing; the last line of the fleet lock-pattern sweep, seedgo's `exclusive_create_race` advisory now 0 fleet-wide). `git/lock_handler.py` 1.1.2: `acquire_lock` does an `O_CREAT | O_EXCL` create and handled `FileExistsError` as "already held"; on Windows an exclusive create against a lock another process is mid-removing raises `PermissionError`, which escaped as an uncaught exception out of the door every `dev-pr` and `commit` crosses. No wait loop: the door has no budget and answers blocked at once by design, so the new arm answers the same way — it re-reads the lock and says `Lock blocked: already held by <holder>` if the file still reads, or names the denial (`create denied (<the denial>) - a lock mid-release on Windows, retry; if it repeats, the repo root is not writable`) if not, logged at WARNING so a root that is truly unwritable does not pass for a busy lock. 2 cases inside the existing `TestLockAcquire` with a fake `os.open` that denies only `.git_pr.lock`, matched by `Path(path).name` and counted, never `str(call)`; both red first with the escaping `Errno 13`; 5/5 mutants red (holder arm dropped, denial unnamed, condition inverted, a retry added, "retry" dropped from the message). `docs/git_interface.md` names the Windows arm. From the devpulse seat: 1372 passed at `-n 3`, `audit aipass @drone` 100. The Windows answer is manufactured in the tests; Windows CI is the real proof.
- **seedgo: an advisory sees a path asserted against a mock call's repr, and the Windows standard says what a Linux seat cannot observe** (`windows_compat_check` 1.3.0, new pure detector `mock_repr_path.py`; seedgo owning, devpulse landing). Windows Test 35416653326 went red on three flow tests that joined `str(c)` over `mock_logger.error.call_args_list` and asserted the lock path was in it: `str(call(...))` is a repr, repr doubles backslashes, and a POSIX path has none, so it passed here by accident. The detector is a per-function name-flow pass — repr text (str/repr/f-string of a mock call record or its containers, carried through join, slice, lower/strip and bound names) meeting path text (tmp_path, tmpdir, Path, tempfile, os.path and anything built from them) at `in`/`==`/`.count`/`.find`/`.startswith`. Excluded and named: the real message one level inside the args (flow's cure), a path side repr cannot change (`.name`, `.as_posix()`), a side already escaped, a platform guard. Corpus `tests/**/*.py`, info channel, no score. Fleet count: 3 before (exactly the CI lines), 0 after flow's cure, 0 in the other 570 test files; two broader arms were measured (0 and 14 hits, all 14 read by hand and none real) and not shipped. Ten cases in the existing test module, 18/18 mutants red in memory; 4306 passed / 53 skipped, `audit aipass @seedgo` 100. `windows_compat.md` gains "What a Linux seat cannot observe — pin it by shape": a state POSIX lacks (nothing is ever delete-pending) and a spelling POSIX never makes (no backslash), so a green Linux run proves nothing about either; and the one thing it can observe, flow's instrument — `pytest --basetemp` with a literal backslash puts one in every tmp path and turns the repr shape red on Linux. The exclusive-create advisory is down from 8 lines to 1 (drone `git/lock_handler.py:171`).

The api defect above is a shape: an exclusive create (`os.open` with `O_EXCL`, or `open(p, "x")`) whose `try` handles `FileExistsError` and lets `PermissionError` escape, or catches it in a retry loop only to give up on the first one. Every create was hand-read with its handlers and callers, and the grep that said six files "handle it" held for none: those `PermissionError` mentions guard `os.kill`, `/proc` reads or `os.replace`, never the create. REAL, escaping: flow `runner/lock_ops.py:84` (the detached runner crashes instead of saying "already running") and ai_mail `dispatch/daemon.py:251,:273` (`_write_pid_file`; the daemon never starts). SOFT, give-up: flow `save_registry.py:59`, `mbank/process.py:58`, `aggregate_ops.py:45`, `append_closed_plan.py:43`. Latent: drone `git/lock_handler.py:171`. - **memory: `rollover_config.py` back to 100% — the display literals move behind a handler and the three config verbs are named for what they are** (DPLAN-0347 / FPLAN-0593 Phase 5; memory owning, devpulse landing). Run 35069130247 went red on `seedgo-audit` alone — `FAILED: 1 branch(es) below 100%` / `memory: 99%` — with every test, lint and coverage job green and the new startup ratchet passing (README 7,887/10,000, prompt 6,763/9,000). The threshold has hard-failed under 100% since 2026-06-05, so the decision to park the finding at 99% was itself the red. **The diagnosis was wrong twice before it was right, and both corrections came from measurement rather than argument.** First reading: "the failing check is size alone." It was two checks — `check_file_size` (657 against a 600 hard fail) *and* `check_thin_orchestration` — read as one because a filtered grep of the checklist showed a single FAIL line. @memory found why it hid: a standard ticks green at score ≥75 while the audit counts the failed check, so the file read **34/34 on the checklist and 80% in the audit at the same moment**. Second reading: "take the bypass, it is precedented." @memory measured what nobody had and refused it — `is_bypassed(path, "modules")` takes the standard name with no per-check key, so one entry would drop the whole modules standard *including size*, on the one file in the branch that had just proved it regrows (656 → 657 on a four-line edit), and the scoped reason proposed for it would have been readable to a human and invisible to the checker. **The cure, in two halves.** The display half: `apps/handlers/cli/config_content.py` (new, 197 lines) holds the literals as `fmt_count`, `defaults_lines`, `overrides_lines`, `branch_limits_lines`, `help_lines` — data in, markup lines out, never prints, no `aipass.cli` import — and the module prints what it returns, so handlers-may-not-print is satisfied on its own terms rather than dodged. 657 → 568, size clean. The naming half: `config_get` / `config_set` / `config_set_default` → `handle_config_get` / `handle_config_set` / `handle_config_set_default`. Not cosmetic and not the rename that was refused earlier — that one proposed `show_`/`update_` prefixes, and `show_` claims display for a verb that writes. `ORCHESTRATION_PREFIXES` carries `handle_` commented "Sub-command routing", and `_handle_config` dispatches to exactly these three. Read end to end before ruling, `handle_config_get` is resolve → banner → fork on branch → fork on JSON vs screen → delegate → log: every line a decision or a delegation with no extractable body, so the checker skipping it is the checker being right. **The standards finding this leaves for @seedgo, which is the real one:** `check_thin_orchestration` uses function LENGTH as a proxy for "implements logic", and a verb answering both the machine surface (`--json`) and the screen — both required by seedgo's own standards — carries two forks a single-surface verb does not. `THIN_WRAPPER_MAX_LINES = 40` is fair for one surface and wrong for two. @memory also corrected its own reference count mid-flight: of "16 references", 4 were `log_operation` event names, left unchanged deliberately because renaming them would split existing log history in four files for no check's benefit. Measured: branch audit 100% overall with modules 100% and 0 violations / 0 failed checks / 0 type errors across 57 files; 1,870 passed / 2 skipped at `-n auto` loadscope, `-n 3`, and serial; all five rendered outputs byte-identical to HEAD through a recording Rich console at width 110 (help 3,334/51, defaults 428/6, overrides 304/4, no-overrides 63/2, branch limits 1,042/11); no outside callers fleet-wide.

- **ai_mail: the macOS cwd test no longer takes its expected value from the host it runs on** (FPLAN-0593 Phase 5; ai_mail owning, devpulse landing). Windows run 35058244702 went red on `test_wake.py::test_get_pid_cwd_darwin` — `assert None == 'C:\\Users\\runneradmin\\…\\pytest-project'` — while Linux and macOS both passed it, so it was red on every Windows head of the diet and it alone stood between PR #770 and a green merge train. Cause: the test fakes darwin and then built the fake `lsof -Fn` output out of `tmp_path`, which on a Windows runner is a drive-letter path; `_get_pid_cwd_darwin` accepts only a name line whose prefix is `n` followed by a forward slash, so the parse fell through the loop and returned None. A comment recorded that `tmp_path` had been chosen so the literal would not hardcode a POSIX directory the Windows run cannot name — that change is what broke it. Fake `lsof` output is data the parser reads, not a directory the host has to own. Cure in the test file alone: a synthetic POSIX literal and no `tmp_path` in the signature, chosen over a skip guard because this test is the only coverage the macOS parser gets on the other two runners. The leading slash is now load-bearing and pinned by its own case, red-first against a manufactured Windows path and measured both ways from the devpulse seat: a drive-letter name line reads None, a POSIX one reads the path back. 1,499 passed in the CI shape, one more than before. **Seen and reported, not cured:** `dispatch/daemon.py` carries AST-identical twins of all four functions — `_get_pid_cwd`, `_get_pid_cwd_darwin`, `_read_session_type`, `_read_session_type_darwin` — diverging only in the log tag, and its darwin lanes have no coverage at all, so the same trap sits there unexercised. A shared helper taking the tag as an argument is the cure; a naive merge would make daemon-side log lines say `[wake]`, which is how a daemon poll is read in prax.

- **memory: the push's dry-run tests no longer pass or fail on which xdist worker they land** (FPLAN-0593 Phase 4 follow-up; devpulse edit, memory owning and mailed). macOS run 35050261305 on 31c71f5d went red on two `test_trinity_push.py::TestDryRunWritesNothing` tests with `unknown section 'sessions'` while the same tests were green on every earlier head and green locally in the full run. Cause: the test fixture config published the four entry types without their `fields` maps, and since the closed field shape landed (Phase 1) that map is the only source of an entry's shape — with it absent the push falls back to a module-level rules cache, so the class passed only when an earlier test on the same worker had warmed the cache from the real config. xdist's `loadscope` distributes classes, not files, so a cold worker was a matter of scheduling. Cure in the test file alone (1.2.0 → 1.2.1): the fixture config now carries the closed `fields` map for sessions, key_learnings, todos and observations, mirroring `memory.config.json`. The class passes alone and the file passes whole.

What it reads: every function in a `tests/` file; it flags `sys.modules.pop(K)`, `del sys.modules[K]` and `delattr(M, attr)` where M is provably a module — the exact shape that made `memory/tests/test_contracts.py` exit 0 on macOS and Linux 3.13 (a helper evicted the rollover module, re-imported it bound to a mock cli, and teardown never put it back).
